**`_99` LANDED (2026-07-31) â€” sACN input-bridge `addMembership
EINVAL` boot crash:** report
`202607/20260725_99_sacn_bridge_einval_fix.md`.
**ROOT CAUSE â€” NOT the NIC.** A direct probe joins 5 multicast
groups successfully on this box three ways (iface unset,
`0.0.0.0`, the adapter's own address); one Wi-Fi adapter, one
private /24, healthy. The bug is **ours and it is an ordering
race**: `new Receiver({universes})` keeps OUR array
(`this.universes = universes`) and runs its join loop from the
socket's `listening` callback â€” a tick later, **iterating that
live array**. `sacn_bridge.js` then ran `recomputeRoutes('boot')`
SYNCHRONOUSLY, and `addUniverse(u)` joins `u` NOW **and pushes it
into the same array** â†’ the deferred loop joined it a SECOND time
â†’ duplicate `IP_ADD_MEMBERSHIP` = `EINVAL` on Windows. The package
re-emits that as `receiver.emit('error')`; the bridge had ONLY a
`packet` listener, and an EventEmitter `'error'` with no handler
**throws** â†’ dead before one frame. The repro is damning: the
bridge's own log printed `added:[38], failed:[]` â€” SUCCESS â€” and
the process died a tick later.
**TRIGGER = DATA, not the box:** any universe in the boot union
absent from the boot subscription list. When the `ðŸ“¡ Subscribed
Universes` field is set it **REPLACES** the patch-derived list
outright (`sacn_bridge.js:129-131`), so **a scene patched to a
universe the field does not name crashes the bridge at boot**.
`_92` passed through exactly that on U38/U39; **`_92` Â§A8 step 1
(attach the TE signs to a MarsinLED output) re-creates it** â€”
which is why this had to be fixed structurally, not by widening
a field.
**FIX (4 parts, no fallbacks):** (1) **boot gate** â€” nothing
subscribes until the receive socket is listening; the held reason
is replayed IN FULL one tick later and every deferral prints a
line (ordering, not suppression); ordering is guaranteed because
`socket.bind(port, cb)` registers the package's loop as a
`'listening'` listener inside the constructor and ours registers
after. (2) **classified `receiver.on('error')`** â€” an
`addMembership` failure is loud + isolated, naming the interface,
stating UNICAST still arrives while MULTICAST does not, and
pointing at the config lever (the same contract
`applyUniverseSubscriptions` already documents for the RUNTIME
path â€” the two halves now agree); **every other socket error is
FATAL** (`exit 1`, "refusing to run half-alive"). (3)
**self-policing invariant** at `listening`: `receiver.universes`
must equal the boot list, else hard exit naming the racing
universes + "fix the ordering, do not retry" â€” a future refactor
fails at startup with the diagnosis pre-written. (4)
**deterministic + logged interface selection** â€” the boot log now
always states which interface the joins use plus the full IPv4
inventory, warns when several NICs are up (OS choice = coin flip)
or none is (the brief's original hypothesis, now a NAMED
diagnosis); optional `sacn_interface` in `simulation/config.yaml`
pins it and **throws with an inventory** on a mismatch or an
ambiguous adapter â€” never a silent NIC switch. Unset = the
shipped behavior, printed as such.

**LANDED 2026-07-31 â€” `_96` OPTIONAL-DISCOVERY LIFECYCLE + CONTROLLER
STATUS (Opus, `20260725_96_optional_discovery_lifecycle.md`):** closes the
ROOT CAUSE behind `_92` Â§4 (six rope strands dark for weeks because the only
path to a `device:` binding was a live discovery conversation).

- **Lifecycle `unbound â†’ PROVISIONAL â†’ VERIFIED`.** Operator ruling: *"the
  discovery must be an optional stage in the controller lifecycle and not
  required."* A PROVISIONAL block is `device: {vendor, provisional: true}` â€”
  **no controllerId, no push receipts**; the schema throws on either, and the
  absence of `provisional` still REQUIRES a controllerId, so the two shapes
  are mutually exclusive by construction. Bind-by-controllerId doctrine is
  intact: it governs VERIFIED bindings; a provisional card is IP-matched only
  to find its own first contact, then promoted.
- **A provisional card patches EVERYTHING** â€” patches.yaml records, engine
  model lanes (`patch:` not `unpatched: true`), bridge relay routes,
  subscribed universes â€” **byte-identical to a verified card**, and
  **promotion moves nothing**. Both pinned by test. Mechanism: no new branch
  anywhere; `isBoundLedController` is now the UNION of the two grades and every
  layer inherits it. Truly unbound cards keep the `_92` unpatched contract.
- **First contact = reconcile, never a side-pick.** Six codes
  (`device_not_recognized`, `controller_id_claimed`, `ip_mismatch`,
  `per_output_unsupported`, `board_output_count`, `board_id_mismatch`,
  `device_name_mismatch`); the first two are HARD BLOCKERS. A contradiction
  changes nothing on either side and raises a dialog with two explicit
  choices. Universes/enables/pixel counts are deliberately NOT contradictions
  â€” that is push drift and the sync chip owns it.
- **`0.0.0.0` composes**: the sentinel REFUSES a provisional binding (type the
  real IP first); a hand-written sentinel+provisional card still patches with
  the sentinel visible in every record. Conversion path pinned.
- **ONLINE/OFFLINE/UNKNOWN** (operator scope addition, same thread):
  server-side `POST /controllers/probe`, per-type probes â€” LED = HTTP
  `/api/status` (**MarsinLED never answers ICMP**, so ping would call the whole
  fleet dead), DMX = TCP connect ladder where a **refused** connection PROVES
  the host is up (sACN/Art-Net sinks answer nothing; ArtPoll would mis-report
  every sACN gateway). `unknown` is a first-class state and is never rendered
  as offline. Bounded pool (16) + 1.2 s ceiling + box-keyed cache; the pane
  never awaits a probe. An LED probe reply IS the fingerprint, so the sweep is
  the "next boot / recognition" trigger â€” provisional + ONLINE + fingerprint â†’
  the same promote path.
- **Numbers:** 76 new tests (33 lifecycle / 23 probe incl. real loopback
  sockets + RFC 5737 offline / 20 status model). Sim 1482 â†’ **1559, fail 9 =

**P0-F1 (stuck/DARK show, the headline):** `GET` **and** `POST
/timeline/overview` build the day ribbon SYNCHRONOUSLY on the HTTP thread in
O(days x cues^2) â€” `buildDaySegments` (`resolve_deck_state.js:331`) calls
`resolveDeckStateAt` per sample point, and each of those re-runs
`applicableCues` + `resolveDayTimes` over the WHOLE cue list, constructing two
`Intl.DateTimeFormat` per clock cue. Measured on a REAL engine (:7717): 64 cues
x 8 days = **2.8 s frozen**, 128 = **11.4 s** (a concurrent `GET /status` was
ECONNRESET), 256 = **58 s**, **512 â€” the schema's own cap â€” = 296 s**. The 40 fps
render loop, the sACN sender and the timeline tick share that event loop, so the
exterior goes dark and no client can reach the engine; the PROCESS stays alive,
so no supervisor restarts it. Needs no auth and no saved plan â€” one maker
preview of a big draft does it. The 512 cap predates the ribbon
(`show_plan.js:799` justifies itself with "a 10k-cue POST froze /status ~32s";

## _137 â€” View allocator word policy + word-aware bench budget (fixes `_134` Â§5.1 + Â§5.3) â€” LANDED

**Scope:** `simulation/src/dmx/view_registry.js`, `simulation/src/gui/view_masks_editor.js`,
`simulation/lib/bench_section.cjs`, `simulation/tests/bench_section_sync.test.js`, plus a

**Landed â€” Â§5.1, the allocator policy.** Base group bits can ONLY live in view word 0
(`reconcileGroupBits` â†’ `nextFreeBit`; mirrored in `engine.js` `assignGroupBits`); custom views
work in EITHER word because they resolve by NAME at model load. Word 0 was therefore the
single-consumer-constrained resource â€” and `nextFreeSlot()` walked `word 0 â†’ word 1`, handing every
new view a word-0 bit while word 1 sat empty. On titanic (24 groups + 17 views) word 0 hit
`0x7fffffff`, `nextFreeBit â†’ 0`, and `reconcileGroupBits(reg, [...existing, 'New Group'])` **threw**
`[Views] Out of view-mask bits â€¦` with 21 word-1 slots free. New policy:
`CUSTOM_VIEW_WORD_ORDER = [1, 0]` â€” `nextFreeSlot(registry, wordOrder)` fills **word 1 first** and
spills into word 0 only when word 1 is full. Chosen over a reserved word-0 headroom margin because a
margin needs a magic constant correct for no scene and would still let views eat word 0 while word 1
is empty; preference ordering is scene-independent, keeps the full 62-slot capacity, and still
throws at 62 (P0, no silent degradation). Verified: empty scene â†’ `{word:1,bit:1}`; 32 views â†’ 31 in
word 1 + 1 spilled to word 0; 63rd throws. **Existing pinned assignments never renumber** â€”
`createViewRegistry` preserves every `(word, bit)`, proven by regenerating all three scenes offline:
`titanic / studio_top_loft / test_bench` sidecars all `reproduces=true` vs tracked (stamp excluded).
`studio_top_loft` + `test_bench` were **not** rewritten (byte-stable, ample headroom in both words).
New API `setCustomViewSlot(reg, view, word, bit)` (the canonical cross-word relocation;
`setCustomViewBit` delegates, contract unchanged) **refuses** to move a per-fixture-membership view
across words â€” fixtures carry a word-0 `viewMask` only, so its membership would have nowhere to

new group(s) fit` / `CUSTOM VIEWS â€” 17 Â· 21 slot(s) free (14 in word 1, 7 spill into the group
word)` â€” the old flat number was word-0-only and mislabelled as the view budget. [**Corrected
2026-08-03** per `_135` D3: this block first quoted `28 slot(s) free`; the code
(`view_masks_editor.js:336` = `free.word1 + free.word0` = 14 + 7) always rendered **21**. Report

## _138 â€” `vMaskHi` reaches exported pixels (fixes `_137` Â§6.1) â€” LANDED

**Scope:** `simulation/` only â€” `src/dmx/view_registry.js`,
`src/dmx/pixelblaze_model_exporter.js`, `src/gui/view_masks_editor.js`,
`src/core/{light_pool,animate}.js`, `src/gui/gui_builder.js`,
`src/dmx/{rename_invalidation,auto_patcher}.js`, `server/save-server.js`, `main.js`,
`lib/{scene_model_parity,bench_section}.cjs`, `tools/bench_section_sync.cjs`, plus
`tests/view_mask_hi_export.test.js` (new) and `tests/rename_invalidation.test.js`.
**No engine source, no generated scene/model/sidecar file, nothing hand-edited.** Report
[`20260725_138_vmaskhi_pixel_export.md`](../reports/202607/20260725_138_vmaskhi_pixel_export.md).

**Where the word was dropped.** The clickâ†’engine chain has five links; only #1 and #4/#5 were
word-aware. **#2** â€” the Views panel's Assign/Unassign/delete/count wrote `f.viewMask`
unconditionally, ignoring `view.word`. **#3** â€” the exporter wrote `vMask: light.viewMask || 0` and
had **no `vMaskHi` field at all**; there was no `viewMaskHi` on a fixture config anywhere in the sim.
So `buildViewmasksSidecarJS` â€” which correctly reads `vMaskHi` for a word-1 view â€” found zero members
on every pixel and skipped the view with a `console.warn`. Both links had to be fixed: the exporter
alone would still have been fed the wrong field, the panel alone would have had nowhere to write.
**Two failure modes, not one:** (a) empty export, and (b) **aliasing** â€” a word-1 bit landing in
`viewMask` collides with a live **base group bit** (titanic w1 `0x1`/`0x2`/`0x4` are all word-0 group
bits), so a fixture clicked into `Left Jewelry` would have silently joined the group view
`Right Front Wall` in 3D isolation and in the per-fixture chip row. (b) is why "carry the bit anyway"
was not an option.

**The fix.** `view_registry.js` now owns the wordâ†’field contract as the ONLY place the fields are
named: `FIXTURE_MASK_FIELDS = ['viewMask','viewMaskHi']`, `PIXEL_MASK_FIELDS = ['vMask','vMaskHi']`,
`viewWord` exported, plus `fixtureMaskField` / `pixelMaskField` / `fixtureInView` / `pixelInView` /
`setFixtureInView`. The exporter carries `vMaskHi` on all three pixel-push sites (multi-pixel DMX,
simple DMX, LED strand). **Serialization is conditional** â€” `vMaskHi:` is emitted only when non-zero,
because `engine.js:418` declares the default `px.vMaskHi ?? 0`, so an absent field IS that zero and a
scene without word-1 per-fixture membership exports a byte-identical model (same rule `ledWire` /
`unpatched` already follow). Panel, `light_pool.js:448` and `animate.js`'s instanced-dot isolation all
go through the predicates. **Persistence was mandatory or the fix is cosmetic:** patch record +
structural-tree strip (`save-server.js`), `__globalPatchTree` rows (`main.js`), config defaults +
chips + rename snapshot (`gui_builder.js`), both `clearMetadata`/`clearAllPatches` paths
(`auto_patcher.js`), `DISPLAY_PATCH_FIELDS` + `prunePatchTreeEntries` + **`carryViewMasks` (breaking
contract change: `name â†’ {viewMask, viewMaskHi}`)** (`rename_invalidation.js`), the `vMaskHi`
freshness check (`scene_model_parity.cjs`), and `viewMaskHi` added to `DERIVED_METADATA_FIELDS` so a
ported bench block cannot import word-1 membership into titanic. The polymorphic
number-or-object shortcut for `carryViewMasks` was rejected â€” it would have made word-0 callers
silently correct and word-1 callers silently lossy.

**Two latent second-order bugs fixed in passing.** The Views panel matched the active preview view by
`__activePreviewView.bit === view.bit`; with two independent bit spaces two views can share a bit
VALUE, so that lit up â€” and could have cleared â€” the wrong card. Both sites now match by view
**identity**.

**`setCustomViewSlot` refusal â€” LIFTED.** `_137` Â§1.3's *"has per-fixture membership and cannot move
to word N â€” fixture masks only exist in word 0"* existed **only** because fixtures could not carry
`vMaskHi`. They can now, so the premise is gone. It is not simply deleted: auditing found a second,
real hazard â€” the function mutates the registry only, so a caller who relocates across words and
forgets to migrate the bits triggers **both** failure modes at once (empty export + a stranded
aliasing bit). So the move is made **atomic** instead: `setCustomViewSlot(registry, view, newWord,
newBit, fixtures = null)` **requires** `fixtures` for any cross-word move (throws, naming both fields
and the remedy, with nothing partially applied) and performs the migration itself after the
destination-word collision check. Same-word moves are unchanged; `setCustomViewBit` still delegates
and its panel caller still migrates from the returned old bit. Net: the capability the old message
denied is available; only the genuinely unsafe call shape is still refused.

**Group-based views verified unaffected (the brief's "state it").** `buildViewmasksSidecarJS` branches
on `view.groups.length > 0` **before** any mask field is touched and emits `groups: [...]`; no fixture
or pixel mask is read on that path. The engine tags membership from group names and merges into the
lane `word` selects. Word-agnostic by construction â€” which is exactly why `_137`'s 17 titanic
composites survived their cross-word migration. Pinned by test in both words.

**Regression test â€” `tests/view_mask_hi_export.test.js`, 13/13 pass**, offline, `_134`'s
zero-miss/zero-leak shape, driving the real `generatePixelMap` / `saveModelJS` /
`buildViewmasksSidecarJS`. Three bars (A 3px + B 2px in `Bars`, C 2px in `Rail`). The headline case:
a view created by `addCustomView` (which lands in word 1 naturally), operator clicks A + C, bit goes
to `viewMaskHi` and `viewMask` is never created, sidecar EMITS `bit: 0x0001, word: 1, pixelIndices:`
(it was skipped entirely before), resolved set `[0,1,2,5,6]` matched **three** ways â€” expected-by-name,
the sidecar's emitted indices, and `pixelInView`. Plus a leak guard (Bar B carries the SAME bit VALUE
in `viewMask` and must not appear), the **word-0 control** (pre-Tier-C `{name,bit}` view: high word
never touched, sidecar keeps the legacy no-`word:` form, and the serialized model contains the string
`vMaskHi` **nowhere at all**), model-text placement (`vMask: 0, vMaskHi: 1, patch:` on exactly the
members), the four `setCustomViewSlot` cases, and the group-based-view case.

**Re-export sanity â€” all three scenes byte-stable.** `grep -c pixelIndices` over the three tracked
sidecars â†’ **0 / 0 / 0**: no tracked scene has a per-fixture view at all, and titanic's 17 word-1
views are all group-based. Regenerated all three offline through `createViewRegistry(views.yaml)` â†’
`reconcileGroupBits(listPixelGroups(pixels))` â†’ `buildViewmasksSidecarJS` against the real models and
diffed ignoring only the `// Updated:` stamp: `sidecar-reproduces=true` for titanic (17 views,
word1=17), studio_top_loft (2) and test_bench (5). Additionally **not one pixel in any tracked scene
carries a non-zero `vMask` either**, so the conditional emission leaves the three model files and
every `patches.yaml` / `scene_config.yaml` byte-identical too.

**Gates.** `scene_model_parity.cjs titanic` **PASS** (0/0/1 info) Â· `--strict` **PASS** (0/0/1) Â·
`simulation` `npm test` **1752 / 1745 pass / 7 fail** (baseline `_137` Â§7: 1738 / 1731 / 7 â€” the suite
grew by exactly 14: the 13-test new file plus one added `carryViewMasks` word-1 test, and
1738 + 14 = 1752) Â· engine `tests/mixer/model_loader_word_aware.test.js` **14/14** Â· engine view/mask
mixer subset (`auto_views`, `in_view_intrinsic`, `pattern_mixer_masking`, `view_fader_ramp`,
`view_mask_constants`, `view_mask_hi_host`) **109/109**. **Zero new failures**; the 7 reds are the same
7 by name as `_137` Â§4/Â§7. Worth naming: reds 6-7 (`real scene test_bench: â€¦`) still fail on
`sId 7 â‰  0; fId 13 â‰  0` for the two `TE Sign V3` strands â€” **the new `vMaskHi` parity check adds no
finding to any real scene.**

**Findings filed, not fixed.** (1) A view with BOTH groups and clicked fixtures **silently drops the
fixtures**: the sidecar `continue`s on the groups branch, yet the panel's Assign writes the bit anyway

## _140 â€” offline audio harness mirrors `WasmHost`'s three injection passes (`inView()` unblocked) (2026-08-03)

**Report:** `.agent/reports/202607/20260725_140_harness_inview_injection.md` Â· branch `feat/bm_readiness`.

**Problem (filed by `_139` Â§5, reproduced).** `tools/pattern_audio_harness.mjs` could not compile a
pattern that calls `inView("Authored View Name")` â€” the documented targeting layer
(`docs/MARSIN_ENGINE_PATTERNS.md` Â§7.3, `.agent/skills/highdef_pattern_generation.md` Â§3). Measured
pre-fix: `COMPILE_FAIL: Line 9: strings cannot be used as a function argument`, exit 2. So an
`inView()`-targeted pattern could not run the harness, the `--gate` check, or the offline clip
pipeline, and `tools/gallery/gen_variations.mjs` (which spawns the harness) could not produce
titanic static/sound clips for one.

**Root cause â€” TWO faults, not one.** (1) `inView()` is not a VM builtin; it is a compile-time SOURCE
fold in `lib/in_view_intrinsic.js`. The harness drove `lib/marsin_wasm_runtime.js` (no injection stage
at all) and hand-applied only `injectFixtureConstants`, so the literal string reached the MarsinScript
compiler, which correctly rejected it. The real path, `lib/wasm_host.js` `compile()`, runs three passes
in order: `injectInViewIntrinsic` â†’ `injectMaskConstants` â†’ `injectFixtureConstants`. (2) **Not named in
the ticket and the more dangerous half:** the harness loaded the model with a bare
`import(models/<name>.js)`. The raw module is UNRESOLVED â€” every pixel `vMask: 0`, no `vMaskHi`, no
`<model>.viewmasks.js` sidecar merge (verified: titanic sample pixel `"vMask":0`). Bolting the fold on
alone would have folded every view test against a bit no pixel carries â€” a silent all-false render,
the exact codex-P0 failure the intrinsic exists to prevent. Both had to be fixed together.

**Fix (design decision owned per the brief): switch the harness to `loadModelForGauge()` + the real
`WasmHost`,** not a hand-built view table from the sidecar. Rationale â€” parity with the least
duplicated logic: `WasmHost.compile()` IS the engine's compile entry point, so the three passes and
their ORDER cannot drift, and `loadModelForGauge()` is the same word-aware loader (`_136`/`_138`)
that `tools/param_truth/render_context.js` and `tools/perf_gauge.mjs` already use. The view table is
assembled exactly as `engine.js` does (groups at word 0, presets at their authored word), the
bit-free-view promoter is wired, and a promotion re-packs meta post-compile (mirrors `engine.js`
`repackMetaIfDirty`). The hand-rolled meta pack (which used `p.localIndex || 0` instead of the
engine's `derivePixelLocalIndices`) is gone.

**Files (six).** `marsin_engine/tools/pattern_audio_harness.mjs` (the fix) Â·
`marsin_engine/lib/model_loader.js` (pure extraction: the inline `metaArray` map became exported
`buildMetaArray(pixels)`, so the harness re-packs without a second copy of the ABI) Â·
`marsin_engine/tests/tools/harness_inview_injection.test.mjs` (new, 3 tests) Â·
`.agent/skills/highdef_pattern_generation.md` Â§8.2 (the "Known tooling gap" note replaced with the
measured reality) Â· report `_140` Â· this block.

**Loud-failure surface kept and EXTENDED, no fallbacks.** Unknown view â†’
`COMPILE_FAIL: Pattern references unknown view(s) via inView(): <name>. Known views for this model: â€¦`
exit 2. New named failures: model fails to resolve â†’ `MODEL_FAIL: <model> failed to load: <reason>`;
declared `pixelCount` â‰  `pixels.length` â†’ `MODEL_FAIL` (was silently reconciled); missing pattern file
â†’ `PATTERN_FAIL: no pattern file <path>` (was an incidental ENOENT inside the old injector try/catch).
The one added `try/catch` wraps `await loadModelForGauge(...)` only, to honour the documented

already exported `buildMetaArray(pixels)`, which is exactly what this harness needed.

View. Known views for this model: â€¦`, exit 2. Missing model / missing pattern already loud, unchanged.

### `_156` AMENDMENT 2 â€” post-`_158` Â§5 residuals closed (R-158-A/B/C), all falsified

`_158`'s re-verification returned **READY FOR PHYSICAL SMOKE** with D-158-1/2/3

**R-158-A (MEDIUM) â€” a permanent sequence offset read as a lost datagram.** The
all-sequences-equal rule assumes one shared sequence per engine frame, and that
lockstep is EMERGENT, not guaranteed: each `sacn` Sender owns its counter from 0,
and the engine's model-reload path creates a Sender mid-run (`engine.js:1726`) and
advances one universe three times (`:1758`). `_158` reproduced a permanent âˆ’7
offset â€” the multi-source gateway emitted 0 of 10 frames while single-source LED
destinations kept running (correct fail-loud per P0, but unrecoverable without an
engine restart) and the log said *"a source datagram was lost"*, sending the
operator to hunt network loss. **Bridge-side diagnosis fix only â€” nothing in
`marsin_engine/` touched; engine-side sequence semantics belong to the `_157`
slices.** New `offsetSignature()` computes wrap-aware SIGNED lag (seven behind
reads `-7`, not `249`). **The discriminator is the MINIMUM lag each source reaches
while the window is open, not a repeated signature** â€” offsets swing within a
single frame as its datagrams land one at a time, so consecutive readings are
never identical (that was the first attempt and it never fired); a source merely
one frame late touches 0 at some point in the cycle, a permanently offset one
never does. After 6 flushes without an emission, any source whose minimum lag is
still non-zero is FIXED, and the new diagnosis jumps the throttle window because
it contradicts the line printed before it. Message names the offset (`U5 at -7`),
rules out the wrong remedy (`This is NOT network loss and it will NOT recover on
its own`), names the cause class (`engine MODEL RELOAD`) and states the remedy
(`**RESTART THE ENGINE**`). Regression is `_158`'s repro verbatim, plus a second
half asserting a ONE-OFF loss still reads as a lost datagram â€” otherwise the new
message would merely replace the old misdirection.

**R-158-B (LOW/MED) â€” a total-`none` arm froze every box.** D-158-2 gave a
slice-less destination `requiredSources` = every source the mapping reads; with
EVERY slot `none` the mapping reads nothing, so that set was empty everywhere and
nothing ticked â€” 0 frames, every bench box holding its last look, arm accepted.
**Chose emit-zeros over refusing the arm**, per the ruling text ("unselected =
actively held dark") and because "own the whole bench and hold it dark" is a
legitimate mid-session gesture. A destination with an empty `required` set now
emits unconditionally (it can be neither whole nor torn â€” the frame is all-zero by
construction), and a mapping with no source universes anywhere starts a
`DARK_TICK_MS = 25` (40 fps, the engine's own frame rate) ticker that marks its
destinations dirty. `unref`'d, started only for that degenerate shape

## `_167` â€” FIX: `GET /pattern-dirs/<invalid-slug>` no longer kills the engine

**Agent:** fix `_167` (Opus) Â· branch `feat/bm_readiness` Â· report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260805_167_engine_http_crash_fix.md`. Operator-authorized fix
of `_164` Â§3 â€” the one-request, unauthenticated, no-state-required remote engine kill.

**Root cause, confirmed exactly as `_164` and `_166` described it.** The
`/pattern-dirs/<dir>` route committed response headers (`writeHead(200)`) BEFORE
evaluating `listPatternsInDir(...)`, which correctly THROWS on any slug failing
`VALID_PATTERN_DIR` (`/^[a-z0-9][a-z0-9_-]{0,63}$/`). The catch arm's second
`writeHead(400)` then raised `ERR_HTTP_HEADERS_SENT` from inside the catch, uncaught â†’
`engine.js`'s `uncaughtException` â†’ `ENGINE FATAL` â†’ `process.exit(1)`.

**Fix, two halves, both in `marsin_engine/lib/api_server.js`.** (a) The route now
computes the JSON body BEFORE `writeHead`, so a refused slug yields a **loud, named
400** while the response is still uncommitted. (b) New module-scope export
`sendJsonError(res, status, payload, headers)` checks `res.headersSent` and refuses to
`writeHead` twice under any circumstance â€” it does NOT swallow: it names the error and
the intended status on stderr, then closes the socket. `headers` passes straight
through, so `sendJsonError(res, 400, x)` is byte-identical to the bare
`res.writeHead(400)` it replaces. **No global `uncaughtException`/`clientError` net was
added** (P0: no fallback behaviors) â€” grep-verified that no `server.on('clientError')`
exists; `engine.js`'s handler is untouched and its own comment already states the
"fix at the source, this is only the net beneath" doctrine (`_108` precedent).

**Same-shape audit (brace-matching scanner, `~/tmp/fix_167/scan_shape*.mjs`).** 97
try/catch blocks in `api_server.js` have a catch that calls `res.writeHead`. 56 never
commit headers before a throwable. **19 are the exact crash shape (a real function call
evaluated after headers are committed) â€” 18 FIXED, 1 false positive.** The 18: the
`/pattern-dirs` bug itself, plus `POST /scene`, `POST /scene/reload` (both of which had
a nested try that SWALLOWED the second-writeHead throw â€” replaced, no more swallow),
`PATCH /global-effect-slots`, `POST /global-effect-slots/<id>/<action>`,
`GET /party-config`, `GET /mixer/param-presets`, `PATCH /osc/config`, `POST /playlists`,
`DELETE /playlists/<name>`, `POST /deck/overlays/<id>/playlist[/entry]`,
`POST /deck/playlist`, `POST /deck/playlist/capture`,
`POST /mixer/channels/<id>/playlist[/entry|/capture|/discard]`. **`GET
/mixer/param-presets` is the notable second find** â€” its own comment claimed a corrupt
preset file would "fail loud"; it actually killed the engine. False positive: the
`/scheduled-tasks/<id>` outer try, whose `writeHead` lives in an async `readBody`
callback that cannot run before the outer catch. **23 tier-2 blocks listed NOT fixed** â€”
only property reads on already-resolved values run after headers there, not reachable
by malformed input; converting them is the follow-up that would make the class
structurally impossible.

**Pin test flipped**, exactly as `_166`'s addendum demanded.
`tests/e2e/pattern_dirs_crash_pin.test.js` went 1 test (assert the engine dies) â†’ **16**
(assert it survives): 10 hostile slugs (`..%2F..`, `%2e%2e%2f%2e%2e`, `Default`,
embedded space, embedded dot, leading `_`, leading `-`, 65-char, `%ZZ`, `%00`) each
asserting 400 + a NAMED reason + `proc.exitCode === null` + a live `/status`; happy-path
(`/pattern-dirs` lists `default`, `/pattern-dirs/default` returns a non-empty array);
end-of-sweep liveness; and 4 unit tests driving `sendJsonError` directly, including the
branch where `writeHead` would throw. Filename kept so `_164`/`_166` references resolve;
its own isolated spawn/teardown kept so a regression stays contained.

**Counts.** `pattern_dirs_crash_pin.test.js` isolated: **16 / 16**.
`http_malformed_sweep.test.js` (G-5) isolated: **36 / 36**. Full engine suite:
**2789 / 2782 / 7** â€” failing LIST byte-matches baseline (5x `audio_capture`, 1x
`effects_v2_mode_page_layout` file-level, 1x `osc_listener` EADDRINUSEâ†’EACCES), **zero
new failures**; `performance_mode.test.js` passed in this run. Total rose from `_164`'s
2772 because this file went 1 â†’ 16 and concurrent agents added their own.
`security_check.py --all`: **6 findings = baseline** (gitignored
`.scene_backups/studiodj/**`), zero in any file I touched. No git ops. Engine-suite
state-yaml residue present and documented-expected.

**Concurrency disclosure.** `api_server.js` was edited by at least two other agents
while I worked (a `/shutdown` route from the `_169` slice, an `outputRouting` change
from the bench-mirror work). Their hunks are in the tree alongside mine and were NOT
reverted; the full-suite number therefore measures the combined tree, and the two
isolated runs are the clean evidence for this fix.

**Operator note.** The fix applies at your NEXT engine restart. The engine currently
running on your box still has the crashing route in memory â€” until it is restarted,
`GET /pattern-dirs/Default` against THAT process still kills it. Nothing here touched
your live engine.

**Follow-up left open:** convert the remaining 23 tier-2 catch arms to `sendJsonError`
to make the double-`writeHead` process-kill class structurally impossible in this file.

## `_169` â€” `stop` now blacks the rig out before the force-kill (T1 FIXED)

**Agent:** fix `_169` (Opus) Â· **Branch:** `feat/bm_readiness` Â· **Report:**
`.agent/reports/202608/20260805_169_stop_blackout_fix.md`. Operator-authorized and
explicitly optional ("the stop to black out is optional but nice to have â†’ fix if
minimal work"). Fixes **T1** of `_160`. No git ops, no scene/pattern/playlist edits, no
operator port bound, no live process signalled. Scratch `~/tmp/fix_169/`.

**The defect.** `launcher.js stop` force-kills the tree (`taskkill /PID <pid> /T /F` =
`TerminateProcess`), so the engine's SIGTERM handler â€” the ONLY emitter of the shutdown
blackout (`engine.js` Â§8) â€” never ran and every controller held its **last live frame**
until its own unknown E1.31 timeout, while four docs promise "lights OFF â€¦ before
generator work". Unfixable launcher-side alone: Windows has no graceful signal (the
launcher's OWN teardown also force-kills its children), and the engine had **no in-band
shutdown route** â€” `POST /scene` / `/scene/reload` reach `shutdown()` but always restart.

**The fix â€” reach the EXISTING blackout, don't build a second one.**
`engine.js:2569` `engineCore.requestShutdown = () => shutdown()` (one hook onto the same
re-entrancy-guarded `shutdown()` the signal handlers call). `api_server.js:5511`
`POST /shutdown` â€” requires `{"confirm": true}` (400 `CONFIRM_REQUIRED`), 500
`NO_SHUTDOWN_HOOK` if unwired, else 200 then `setTimeout(â€¦, 50)` â†’ the hook
(respond-then-act, the `POST /scene` pattern). `launcher.js:1070-1129`
`blackoutEngineBeforeKill(lock, deps)` + calls at `:1140` (stale-lock branch) and `:1154`

## `_170` â€” RAW DMX on the wire (S-D1): the Ã—2.55 percent clip is DEAD

**Agent:** fix `_170` (Opus, operator-authorised "do #4") Â· **Branch:** `feat/bm_readiness`.
**Report:** `.agent/reports/202608/20260805_170_raw_dmx_wire_fix.md`. Fixes `_157` **D1**
= `_153` **F1b + F7** = `_105` **F3 + F8** â€” one root cause, four symptoms, one slice.
**No git ops. No operator process touched, no port bound, no packet emitted.**

**The defect.** The vendored `sacn@4.6.2` treats `Sender.send({payload})` as a **0..100
PERCENT** field (`packet.js:138` â€” `inRange(payload[ch] * 2.55)` unless `useRawDmxValues`)
and `objectify` divides wire bytes by 2.55 on receive. **No project source ever set the
flag, and every project source wrote raw 0-255 DMX into that field.** Measured with the
real `Packet`: `0->0 1->3 32->82 50->127 100->255 101->255 200->255 255->255` â€” **exact
round-trips 2 of 256**, on the engine lane AND the mirror lane. Everything the engine
rendered above DMX 100 left as FULL, so colour was crushed toward white on every
controller on the ship; the browser got 0-100 "DMX" (the 39 % preview, `_105` F3); and the
mirror truncated those percent floats into a `Uint8Array` (F7's ~100 levels) on top.

**The fix.** (1) All **four** senders declare `useRawDmxValues: true` in
`defaultPacketOptions` â€” engine `sacn_output.js`, `sacn_output_bridge.js`'s pool, the input
bridge's **relay** senders, the **mirror** senders (beside `MIRROR_CID`). (2) The receive
path reads `packet.payloadAsBuffer` via a new `rawDmxPayload(packet)` in `sacn_bridge.js`,
never `packet.payload` (that getter IS the percent view), so relay resend + mirror splice +
WS broadcast all carry raw bytes. (3) The browser needed **no change** â€” `sacn_mapper.js`'s
`/255` was always right arithmetic fed the wrong unit; a repo grep confirms **zero** `2.55`
compensations existed anywhere, so there was none to remove. (4) The mirror needed no
arithmetic change either: integers instead of floats into its `Uint8Array` kills F7 with
the unit. **Shape deliberately unchanged** â€” `rawDmxPayload` keeps `objectify`'s sparse
(zero-omitting) shape so ONLY the unit moves.

**The `_157` pitfall was real and is heeded.** Handing `payloadAsBuffer` back as `payload`
objectifies it to percent and then writes that percent AS the byte: measured
`1->0 64->25 128->50 200->78 255->100` â€” **2.55Ã— DARK**. `rawDmxPayload` returns a plain
1-indexed object of raw numbers; an executable **PITFALL GUARD** test pins it.
`payloadAsBuffer === null` is structurally unreachable from the wire and is treated as an
invariant violation (`âŒ` + `process.exit(1)`, like `checkBootSubscriptionInvariant`) â€”
**not** a throw, because the vendored `Receiver` wraps `emit('packet')` in try/catch and
would swallow it.

**PROOF â€” all 256 values, three lanes, ZERO distortion.** Every wire byte produced and read
with the package's OWN `Packet` class (the `_157`/`_164` technique), never a hardcoded
offset. **A** engineâ†’wire **256/256**. **B** wireâ†’`payloadAsBuffer`â†’`rawDmxPayload`â†’relay
resendâ†’wire **256/256** (the relay's exact round-trip `_157` P8 measured under the old
units is preserved under the new ones). **C** rawâ†’`spliceMirrorFrame`â†’`mirrorPayload`â†’
mirror senderâ†’wire **256/256**. Was 2/256 on A and C. Position independence asserted too
(first/middle/last channel).

**Test flips: 6 pins flipped, 5 new tests, 2 truth tables extended past {0,255}.**
Flipped: `sacn_output_wire.test.js` header ("KNOWN QUIRK, pinned not fixed / blocked on
R-D1" â†’ "NOW FIXED", `_155` A5's {0,255} rule retired), its `_155` A5 value test, its
1-indexing `notEqual(â€¦,0)` â†’ `equal(â€¦,42)`; `engine_bridge_contract.test.js`'s "relays as
the sacn-percentage-scale equivalent" â†’ "as RAW DMX 255"; `bench_mirror.test.js`'s `_155`
A4 CID source pin (now requires `useRawDmxValues: true`) and its `_153` Â§10 / `_158`
D-158-3 pin (now requires `routeFrame(â€¦, rawDmxPayload(packet), â€¦)`). New: the full R-D1
0..255 table in the engine, a `defaultPacketOptions`-placement mechanism guard, the R-D1
end-to-end 256-value PROOF + PITFALL GUARD in `engine_bridge_contract`, and the 256-value
**armed mirror** compose+wire proof in `bench_mirror_arm`. `bench_mirror_resolve` gained
mid-range truth tables per fixture family (PAR: 32/64/128/200 on each of R/G/B/W + a
10-ch ramp; STRAND: same per RGBW pixel lane + a 16-ch ramp), retiring the `_155` A5 /
`_156` "0 and 255 only" restriction in prose. Held UNCHANGED on purpose: the ALL-ZERO
"empty payload" pin (sparse shape preserved). Harness: `inbound()` builds the raw
512-byte buffer (same `{channel: 0..255}` API, now fails loudly outside 0-255) and
`FakeSender` records `useRawDmxValues`; three direct `emit('packet')` sites updated.

**Suites â€” zero new failures.** Sim baseline **2008/2001/6 fail/1 todo** â†’ after
**2024/2017/6/1**, failing LIST byte-identical (same 6, same files, same lines; G8's
`summer_camp_dome/patches.yaml.original` still outstanding for the operator). Engine
baseline **2784/2776/8 fail** â†’ after **2793/2786/7**, the 7 a strict SUBSET of the 8.
`security_check.py --all`: **6**, all gitignored `.scene_backups/studiodj/**` â€” baseline.
**Tree moved under this session** (concurrent `_167`/`_168`/`_169` + bridge-routing/scene
edits), which is why totals rose by more than this slice's own +5 sim / +2 engine tests.
**Contention caveat:** the strobe case (failed baseline, passed after), `EADDRINUSE`, and
`pattern_dirs_crash_pin` are timing-sensitive; the engine list is stable only up to those.

**OPERATOR â€” bench A/B, before you restart anything.** Full recipe in the report Â§6.
Short: on the **currently running** stack (old code still in memory) ARM the bench mirror
for `test_bench`â†`titanic`, select **`test_const`** with **Color 1 = deep amber/orange,
S=1, V=1** (hue â‰ˆ 0.05-0.08 â€” R at 255, G mid-range, B at 0; the one look that puts a
channel at each extreme AND one exactly where the percent scale did its worst), note every

**WARNING â€” the whole SHIP will read darker at the same slider positions.** The old wire
was a crude, colour-destroying 2.55Ã— brightness boost, and the rig has been running on it

**Not touched:** `launcher.js`, `marsin_engine/lib/api_server.js`, `CaptainPad/**`

**`_173` â€” AUDIO COMPANION KEEPS REVERTING TO THE TEST SIGNAL: root cause found +
fixed.** Report `.agent/reports/202608/20260805_173_audio_companion_state_fix.md`.
Operator: *"it keeps going back to the test signals â€¦ I want it to remember our
last settings."*

**Root cause â€” the engine test suite PATCHes the operator's live show.**
`audio/companion/companion_server.js` resolved `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATH` from a
**hardcoded** `../../config.yaml` and did **not** honour `MARSIN_CONFIG_FILE`, so
every spawned companion resolved `companion.engine` â†’ `127.0.0.1:6968` and
`companion.osc` â†’ `127.0.0.1:10000` â€” the live stack. The two suites that boot the
real companion (`tests/companion/companion_osc_accounting.test.js:67`,
`â€¦/companion_new_signals.test.js:76`) both send `{type:'setMode',mode:'test'}`,
which write-throughs as `PATCH /audio/config {"capture":{"device":"test"}}`. The
engine persists that into `states/<scene>/audio_state.yaml` and rebroadcasts
`audioConfig`, flipping the operator's real Companion to the synthetic generator
mid-session and on every boot thereafter. **Reproduced end-to-end** against a fake
engine (`~/tmp/fix_173/repro_clobber.mjs`) â€” the PATCH is logged verbatim. Git
agrees: titanic `capture.device` went `audio=Microphone (Amazon USB Streaming
Mic)` (`3246deb2`) â†’ `test` (`7d2cb6d7`, committed) â†’ `''` (now). Second-order
damage: with the source on `test`, `applyEngineCaptureDevice` never populates
`configDevice`, so the Companion's "Mic / Line" button writes **`''`** â€” which
`audio_capture.js:145` **throws** on for win32 (`device_not_configured`). Hence
the loop: test â†’ click mic â†’ deaf â†’ back to test.
**Not the engine:** `engine.js` has no `'test'` device path and no silent
micâ†’test fallback (no P0 violation). **Not the state-dir redirect:** every
`engine.js`-spawning suite already goes through `spawn_engine.mjs` /
`MARSIN_STATE_DIR`; HIL is gated to `test_bench`. The Companion was the only gap.

**Fix (4 files, minimal).** `companion_server.js`: `ENGINE_CONFIG_PATH` resolves
through `MARSIN_CONFIG_FILE` â€” unset â‡’ tracked config (operator path
byte-identical), set-but-relative/empty â‡’ **throws at boot** (no silent fallback).
New `tests/helpers/companion_isolation.mjs`: `isolatedCompanionEnv()` writes a
scratch config with `companion.engine.host`/`companion.osc.host` â†’ **the RFC 5737 TEST-NET-1 black-hole address**
(RFC 5737, never routed) and `companion.source: test` (so a spawned companion also
never opens the operator's mic); `assertEngineLinkDown()` fails the suite if the
link is up. Both companion suites now spawn with that env and assert the link is
DOWN **before** sending `setMode`. **`127.0.0.9` is NOT a black hole** â€” the
assertion caught it: the engine binds `0.0.0.0`, which accepts every local
address and all of `127/8` is local.

**Operator step (once, live, no restart):** CaptainPad â†’ AUDIO â†’ SETTINGS â†’
device picker â†’ *Microphone (Amazon USB Streaming Mic)*. `titanic` currently holds
`capture.device: ''` (unstartable on Windows); the engine is running so it was
deliberately NOT hand-edited. `test_bench` already holds the real device.

**Suites.** Engine **2796 / 2789 / 7** â€” the `_172` baseline name for name (5 Ã—
`audio_capture` win32 env, `osc_listener` EADDRINUSEâ†’EACCES, `effects_v2_mode_
page_layout` file-level); zero new. Focused companion pair **5 / 5 / 0**.
`security_check --all` **6** (gitignored `.scene_backups` baseline). Sim not run â€”
no `simulation/` file touched. Post-run residue = my 4 files only; no state file
gained a `capture.device: test`.

**Disclosed:** the repro + the first assertion-failing run each leaked a few
seconds of synthetic audio OSC at the live engine (runtime-only, overwritten at
~86 Hz) and the repro opened the USB mic for ~2 s â€” the same leak both suites have

## _181 â€” coordinate range story

**Date:** 2026-08-06 Â· **Agent:** Fable debug (read-only) Â· **Report:** .agent/reports/202608/20260806_181_coordinate_range_story.md

Operator observed calibration planes (patterns 66/67/68) only find titanic pixels between
0 and ~0.5 on all three axes. NOT a model/exporter/pattern bug: both shipped models span the
full 0..1 on nx/ny/nz (measured: titanic 964 px, test_bench 166 px, all axes exactly 0â†’1;
exporter does per-axis min/max normalization at pixelblaze_model_exporter.js:639-654). Cause
is the engine-owned global SIZE fader: wasm_host.js applySizeScale divides live coords by
mult = 0.25Â·16^size (engine.js:763-770, identity at 0.5), and the titanic scene state has a
persisted size: 0.773 (globals_state.yaml) â†’ mult â‰ˆ 2.13 â†’ coords span 0â†’0.469 â‰ˆ the observed
0.5. test_bench state sits at size 0.5 (identity), which is why the bench calibrated clean.
Verdict: by design (show feature), calibration-workflow footgun. Consequence for authors:
render3D coords span [0 .. 1/sizeMult], sizeMult âˆˆ [0.25, 4] â€” never hard-code 0..1 edges;
per-axis stretch also distorts distances (titanic x covers ~96 world units, y ~14.7). Fix
options described only (procedure "SIZE=0.5 before calibrating" is the cheapest). No changes
made; probe under ~/tmp/fix_181/.

## _183 â€” audio metadata recon + FLUX root cause

**Date:** 2026-08-06 Â· Opus investigation agent, READ-ONLY (no source edits, no git ops).
Report: `.agent/reports/202608/20260806_183_audio_meta_recon.md`.

**FLUX root cause â€” found, proven offline, one link.** The Audio Companion **never publishes
`micFlux`**. The engine side is complete and correct: `micFlux` is a built-in CPC key
(`audio/postproc/audio_signals.js:90`, `oscAddress /marsin/mic/flux`, `live:true`,
`broadcastHz:15`), it is in `GET /param-center/schema` (verified by an offline `ParamCenter`
probe against a temp state file), the OSC listener binds its canonical address, and CaptainPad
lists it in the modulation picker (`deriveAudioSignals` â†’ `useModulationSourceOptions`). What
does not exist is the producer: `defaultCompanionConfig()`
(`audio/companion/companion_config.js:237-250`) and the persisted `companion_config.yaml` both
design only `micLow/Mid/High/Kick + dom1/2 freq+energy` â€” **no flux signal** â€” and
`CURATED_OUTPUTS` (`:94-106`) omits `micFlux`, so even an operator adding one by hand in the
designer gets `resolveOscOut("micFlux") â†’ cpcKey "micflux", address /marsin/audio/micflux`
(a NEW dynamic key), not the built-in. The analyzer's `r.flux` is published only into the
Companion's OWN in-process ParamCenter as `micFluxRaw` (`companion_server.js:1295`), and raw
mirrors carry no `oscAddress` â€” so it never reaches the wire. Nothing is broken in transport,
serialization, CaptainPad filtering, type schema, memoization, labels, or runtime validation.

**Worse than a dead meter.** `applyModulations` skips a mapping only when the source key is
ABSENT; `micFlux` is PRESENT at its default 0, so a flux mapping fires every frame with
signal 0 â€” and in `override` mode that **pins the target at `range[0]`**, overriding the
operator's slider. Blast radius: **32 of 75 patterns** declare `<- micFlux`, and **11 saved
playlist modulations** bind `key: micFlux` (`titanic/ambient.yaml` Ã—4,
`ambient_sound_reactive.yaml` Ã—6, `titanic/default.yaml` Ã—1, plus `test_bench/default.yaml`).
Example: `mod_sliderEmberSwell_micFlux` pins `sliderEmberSwell` at 0.08.

**Minimal fix (no aliasing, no fallback keys):** add `micFlux: '/marsin/mic/flux'` to
`CURATED_OUTPUTS`; add `intensity('flux', 'micFlux', 'rawFlux', <cutoffHz>)` to
`defaultCompanionConfig()` (`rawFlux` already exists as a raw source at `companion_config.js:44`);
add the matching signal to the persisted `companion_config.yaml` (the file overrides the
default, so JS alone changes nothing live). **Decide explicitly** on the secondary gap:
`gainByKeyForOsc()` (`audio_signals.js:453-461`) omits `micFlux`, so once flux flows the
persisted `micFluxGain` knob is dead AND engine-side `micFluxRaw` stays 0 (raw mirrors are
wired only for `GAIN_BY_KEY` entries, `osc_listener.js:338-353`) â€” either wire it or retire
the knob; a half-wired gain is the exact failure mode that map exists to prevent. Verify via
the `_173` seam (`tests/helpers/companion_isolation.mjs`), never against the live stack.

**Canonical metadata extension point for the feature.**
`AUDIO_MODULATION_V1` has exactly ONE parser â€” `tools/audio_mod_spec.mjs` (`parseAudioModSpec`,
`:127`), offline tooling only; **the engine does not parse the block today**. It already parses
the optional `# note` on every mapping line and then **STRIPS it at `:188-191`** â€” the "short
explanation" the feature wants is already authored in every pattern header and thrown away one
line before the return. The join key is free: the block's `slider<Name>` token IS the WASM
export `name` IS `ModulationMapping.target.parameter` (`pattern_defaults.js:56-58`). The
serialization seam is the existing `codeDefault` precedent: `codeDefaultsForPattern`
(`api_server.js:997-1010`, per-pattern Map cache) + `annotateCodeDefaults` (`:1018-1024`,
"additive, does not touch existing fields"), stamped onto `exports:` at `api_server.js:3561`

payloads carry it with zero new endpoints. `cpcOwned/cpcKey/cpcLabel` (`:3565-3572`) is the

## _184 â€” audio suggestion metadata + FLUX fix

**Date:** 2026-08-06 Â· Opus, primary implementer Â· branch `feat/bm_readiness` (post `9e8b23b8`)
Â· report `.agent/reports/202608/20260806_184_audio_meta_impl.md` Â· **no git ops** Â· all
verification offline / in-process (no operator port touched, no live engine or Companion call).

**FLUX IS FIXED â€” and it needs ONE operator action: RESTART THE AUDIO COMPANION.** The design
is read once at boot, so a running Companion is still on the old flux-less config no matter
what the file says. After the restart, 11 saved `micFlux` mappings that were effectively frozen

the value `audio_structure_detector.js:488` reads as its build-score flux input.

a curated output and vice versa â€” so a future sixth band crashes the Companion at boot rather

## _185 â€” 08_ocean_liner portability

**Date:** 2026-08-06 Â· Report: `.agent/reports/202608/20260806_185_ocean_liner_portability.md`
Â· No git ops, no live processes, nothing bound an operator port.

**The break (_184's follow-up 3), closed.** The uncommitted `08_ocean_liner`
rewrite referenced `FIX_RAW_LED` / `FIX_TE_SIGN`; `summer_camp_dome` carries
neither, so `POST /deck/playlist/entry` returned `400 Compile error` and two
`playlist_api` tests failed. Not a test bug.

**Mechanism.** `lib/fixture_type_constants.js` holds a global append-only registry
(RAW_LED=1, PAR=2, VINTAGE_6=3, BAR_18=4, HAZE=5, FOG=6, TE_SIGN=7).
`buildFixtureTypeIds()` emits **only the roles a model's pixels actually carry**;
`wasm_host.js:134` injects them on every compile path and
`name_id_registry.js:142` throws on any other `FIX_*` token. Per-model tables are
DERIVED from geometry, not authored â€” so "establish the constants for every model"
is not a thing the system supports, by design.

**Idiom chosen (a).** Self-declare the canonical id for roles that are OPTIONAL
accents, exactly as `14_lunar_current:56`, `21_pelagic_manta_rays:68` and
`35_sparkle_rain:63` do â€” all three declare only `FIX_TE_SIGN`. Declaring the
canonical id means the injected prelude and the pattern's own `var` agree on
models that carry the role (verified: identical prelude on titanic/test_bench â†’
behavior byte-identical), and match no pixel on models that don't. I deliberately
did NOT also declare `FIX_PAR`/`FIX_VINTAGE_6`/`FIX_BAR_18`: bars and Vintage rails
are this pattern's load-bearing instruments, and swallowing their absence would
turn a loud compile failure into a flat untyped wash â€” a fallback (codex P0).

**Shared-tree collision â€” my net edit to the pattern is ZERO bytes.** The
operator's other AI session added the identical two-constant block (lines 22-25)
to `08_ocean_liner.js` while I was mid-edit. I removed my own (five-constant)
block and kept theirs untouched; the file now has exactly one such block, CRLF
intact, every other byte of their rewrite preserved.

**Tests (offline).** `playlist/playlist_api` **19/19**, incl. both named
regressions green. `mixer/all_models_load_lint` **34/34**.
`patterns/{calibration_patterns,param_truth_smoke,specialty_white_uv,white_amber_lane_match}`
+ `io/fixture_type_constants` **121/121**. Zero failures anywhere I ran. Note
`node --test tests/patterns/` (dir form) dies with `ERR_UNSUPPORTED_DIR_IMPORT` on
Node v24 â€” list the files.

## _186 â€” spotlights URL precedence debug

**Date:** 2026-08-06 Â· **Agent:** _186 (Fable debug, read-only) Â· **Report:** `.agent/reports/202608/20260806_186_spotlights_url_precedence.md`

**Question:** does `?spotlights=644` beat the "Max Spotlights" UI/saved value (operator
expectation: URL authoritative)?

**Verdict: YES at boot, clamped loudly to 200.** `?spotlights=` sizes the SpotLight pool
(`light_pool.js:36-39`) and, when present, overwrites `params.maxSpotlights`
(`light_pool.js:349-350`) BEFORE the GUI builds (`environment.js:204â†’217`), so the slider
shows the URL value and the saved 60 loses. 644 > `MAX_SPOTLIGHT_POOL_SIZE=200`
(`light_pool.js:20`) â†’ effective 200 with cap toast + console (not silent). Slider moves
after boot are deliberate and well-defined (active limit â‰¤ pool, `:252-255`).
`profile=full` carries no spotlight budget.

**Deviations:** (D2) without the URL param the pool is fixed at 60, so saved/UI values
61..200 are SILENTLY ineffective; (D3) the URL-session value persists into
scene_config.yaml on save (no `transient` flag, `config.js:320-321`) â€” precedent-consistent
(lightingMode/profile persist too) but the persisted 200 then squashes to 60 on plain boot
(save lies, via D2); (D4) light_pool syncs `params` only, not `configTree`.

**Fix spec (in report):** move `spotlights` into `applyBootUrlOverrides()` (both params +
configTree, loud invalid/cap handling); size the pool at `initLightPool` from the resolved
`params.maxSpotlights` instead of a module-load constant (fixes D2 + makes D3 round-trip
truthful); keep persist-on-save per repo precedent (`transient: true` in 8 scene YAMLs +
save-server template is the opt-out if the operator wants session-only). Read-only: no
source touched.

## _189 â€” spotlight over-cap session accept

**Date:** 2026-08-06 Â· Opus implementer Â· Branch: feat/bm_readiness
**Report:** `.agent/reports/202608/20260806_189_spotlight_cap_prompt.md`
**Builds on:** _186 (audit) â†’ _187 (the precedence chain / pool-sizing fix)

Operator ask: "if the URL is above the max cap, ask the user to accept it or not,
and when they do, raise the cap temporarily for that session."

**Landed.** `?spotlights=N` above `MAX_SPOTLIGHT_POOL_SIZE` (200) now puts a
**blocking confirm** at boot â€” inside `applyBootUrlOverrides()`, so the answer is
known before `initLightPool()` allocates anything.
- **Accept** â†’ pool = N, slider ranges 1..N, slider labelled `âš  Max Spotlights
  (session N)` with an explanatory tooltip, one `console.warn`.
- **Decline / dismissed / no dialog / prompt threw / non-boolean** â†’ the old
  behaviour byte for byte: clamp to 200, `console.error` + cap toast. Only a
  literal `true` raises the cap; no timeout accepts, nothing is remembered.
- **Session-only, enforced twice:** the ceiling lives on
  `params.__spotlightSessionCeiling` (never the config tree, never localStorage)
  and is deleted at the top of every `applyBootUrlOverrides()`; and new
  `clampPersistedSpotlightBudget()` runs after **both** `reconstructYAML()` sites
  in `gui_builder.js` (explicit save + auto-save via `exportConfig`, and the
  unload beacon) so `scene_config.yaml` can never record more than 200. Persistence
  decision = clamp-to-hard-cap (not restore-pre-raise): stronger invariant, and it
  also catches hand-edited YAML. Live session is untouched by a save.
- **Sanity ceiling `SPOTLIGHT_ABSOLUTE_CEILING = 2000`** â€” above it there is no
  prompt at all, just a loud refusal (`?spotlights=999999`). ~16 fragment-uniform
  vectors/light â†’ 2000 wants ~32k, ~10Ã— any GPU's budget and ~12Ã— the 160 count
  where Mac WebGPU already goes white/black; still only a few thousand small JS
  objects, so a typo wedges a tab rather than OOM-ing the browser.
- A **saved/hand-edited** value above 200 clamps and never prompts â€” consent is
  asked for what the operator just typed, not for what was in a file.
- Native `confirm()` deliberately: `scene_manager.js`'s themed `showModal()` is
  Promise-based and its overlay doesn't exist that early in boot, so it cannot gate
  a synchronous boot step. Dependency-injected (`deps.confirmSpotlightOverCap`) so
  the gate is driven headless in tests; `buildSpotlightOverCapPrompt()` exported so
  the consent wording is pinned.

`simulation/README.md`, `docs/14_light_optimizations.md`. `environment.js` needed
nothing â€” the existing boot order already puts the gate ahead of allocation.

## _191 â€” spotlight sampling optimization

**Date:** 2026-08-06 Â· **Report:** `.agent/reports/202608/20260806_191_spotlight_sampling.md`

The "Sim Spotlight Sampling" dropdown decides which fixtures get one of the
limited pooled THREE.SpotLights. Operator asked for the existing options to be
optimized and for a best-practice option with no flicker (= no pool-reassignment
churn as a pattern moves brightness around).

**Census + the bug.** `closest` was **dead**: the resolver accepted only
`closest_bucket`/`uniform` and silently returned `uniform` for everything else,
so picking `closest` in the GUI â€” the operator's favourite for close work â€” ran
`uniform`, and so did any typo in a scene file. Codex-P0 silent fallback, now a
loud `RangeError` naming the value and the roster, validated once at boot.

**Flicker root causes.** F1 rank-based selection over a list whose length
changes every frame (the analytic gate drops dark pixels, so one entry appearing
shifts every stride index); F2 `closest_bucket`'s window anchored on the nearest
*emitting* pixel, so the anchor jumps and the window slides; F3 positional
assignment with no incumbency and no ramp â€” every set change is a hard cut.
Ties and the 1/255 gate were checked and ruled out.

**Optimizations (semantics preserved, asserted against a verbatim copy of the
old selector).** Squared-distance window test (693,100 â†’ 300 `sqrt` calls per
300 frames), contiguous-prefix bucket scan, a provably no-op sort deleted, the
global distance sort now skipped for the stable modes, and a pooled/allocation-
free collect path (**0.307 â†’ 0.052 ms/frame** at 4800 px, GC churn 19.6 MB â†’ ~0
per 400 frames; 4 heap allocations per pixel per frame â†’ 0).

**New: `stable_importance`** â€” importance (brightness Ã— proximity) ranks,
a coverage grid spaces, incumbency + 1.35Ã— / 12-frame hysteresis holds, â‰¤8
fills and â‰¤2 handoffs per frame bound the change, and a 15-frame crossfade makes
every appearance/handoff a dip instead of a cut. Deterministic, no `Math.random`.
**Slot reassignments: 54.2/frame (`closest_bucket`) â†’ 1.93/frame â€” 28Ã— calmer**,
worst frame 60-of-60 â†’ 8.

**New: `rotating_coverage` (experimental).** The operator's persistence-of-vision
idea, evaluated honestly: at 60 Hz vsync a K-way time share gives 60/K Hz per
light and CFF is ~50â€“60 Hz, so **no K both fuses and adds coverage** â€” the fast
regime is refused in writing. The slow regime ships: a 6 s (0.17 Hz), staggered,
0.5 s-crossfaded rotation; 160 distinct fixtures over 30 s on a pool of 60.

Roster now lives in code (`SPOTLIGHT_SAMPLING_MODES`), written into the config
tree by `addControl` so a save records the truthful list â€” same split as _187's
slider range. **Default unchanged**; nothing under `scenes/**` was edited; the
_186/_187/_189 pool-sizing chain is untouched.

**Touched:** new `simulation/src/core/spotlight_sampling.js`, plus
`simulation/src/core/light_pool.js`, `simulation/src/gui/gui_builder.js`, new
`simulation/tests/spotlight_sampling.test.js` (27 tests), one harness line in
`simulation/tests/spotlight_pool_budget.test.js` (33 pass).

**Tests:** full sim suite **2217 / 2209 pass / 7 fail / 1 todo** â€” failing list
identical to the known baseline (5Ã— `bench_section_sync`,
`pixel_map_view_defaults` "compression threshold" now at `:510`,
`bench_mirror_state:212`, todo `scene_data_lint:109`). No live processes, no

## _200 — timeline resume force-disarm

2026-08-14. Four operator rulings landed as one "timeline authority + lifecycle"
bundle. Engine changes reach the live stack only at the operator's next restart.
Full write-up: `.agent/reports/202608/20260814_200_timeline_priority_disarm.md`.

**Ruling was NOT satisfied before.** RESUME while a Live Touch ARM was active
was usually 423'd outright — `rejectTouchControlLeaseConflict` blocks every
untagged mutating request while a desk is armed, so Live Touch held the show
hostage through the lease gate alone. When it did land, `resume()` never touched
the ARM: the deck pin came back but the ARM's param-centre source lock
(`{mode:'global',source:'api'}`) stayed held, so the plan's catchUp writes all
bounced with reason `source_lock` — deck visible, show frozen. Timeline
operator-lease expiry behaved identically (the `timeline_deck_pin` activation
reason deliberately skips the Live release), and left
`liveTouchTimelineTakeoverOwner` set so the next Live mutation silently
re-seized the timeline.

**Now:** `TimelineService.resume()` and `_releaseOperatorLease()` both call
`deps.yieldLiveTouch(why)` FIRST → `forceDisarmLiveTouchForTimeline` runs the
NORMAL disarm (`armLeaseClear` with `force:true`, same steps/order, only the two
fallible ones individually guarded so nothing can abort the release) → WS
`liveTouchForceDisarm {why, autoRearm:false}` → `docs/ui/touch_control_wire.js`
drops to DISARMED saying "TIMELINE RESUMED" and cannot auto-re-arm.
`/timeline/resume` + `/timeline/autopilot` are now lease-exempt.

**Ordering:** cleanup FIRST, then the DECK landing, then the caller's catchUp —
because releasing the source lock is a *precondition* of the takeover, not a
tidy-up. Hostage risk is removed by making the disarm unabortable, not by
reordering. One forced exception: `engine.js:722` exits if the live_touch layer
renders without an owner session, so while Live is on air the session rides the
outgoing blend via the existing `pendingLiveTouchDeadmanOwner` marker and is
ended by the existing completion hook. Found by a real engine crash in test.

**Disarm always resumes** (`resumeTimelineAfterDisarm`, called from every
`armLeaseClear` and from `revertToAutomaticShow`): armed→disarmed has exactly two
landings — plan enabled → plan RUNNING, plan disabled → no-plan idle. No limbo.

**Plan disabled = totally inert.** Two real bugs: `setAutopilotEnabled(false)`
left a running program alive (controller stayed 'program' → planActive true →
banner + deck pin on a switched-off plan), and the tick had NO autopilotEnabled
gate, so the arbiter armed a pending-program lease that AUTO-STARTED the show
~30 s later. Fixed with `planEnabled()` as the authoritative predicate,
`_isPlanDrivingDeck()` as the ONE plan-active predicate (`getState().planActive`
now literally returns it — the duplicated expression is gone), a plan-disabled
gate in both the tick and `_catchUp`, and `setAutopilotEnabled(false)` routed
through the shared `_goDormant()` teardown (ends the cue NOW via the same work
natural expiry does; loads no replacement look — a disabled plan drives nothing).

**Performance-mode takeover passcode.** The three named principals already
existed in `lib/captainpad_auth.js` (owner/Sina, collaborator/Misha,
bringup/Sailors, from external `$BM26_SECRETS`). Added `verifyPassphrase()` —
same credential check + same lockout, issues NOTHING — and gated all three
"take the rig FROM the plan" paths on a fresh `X-CaptainPad-Passcode` per
attempt. Session tokens are deliberately ignored: required EVERY TIME. Reverse
direction (resume / lease expiry force-disarm) is never gated.

**Tests.** Baseline (effects+timeline) 1009/1009 before. After:
effects+timeline+io+security **1236/1236**; CaptainPad vitest 1078 pass; tsc
clean. e2e+state+mixer 796/801 — the 5 failures are pre-existing
`dev_test_bench` model groupBits drift from another session, untouched here.
New: `tests/timeline/timeline_plan_disabled.test.js` (9, incl. the mid-cue-fire
disable race and restart-stays-disabled) and
`tests/effects/live_touch_timeline_priority_api.test.js` (3, incl. the full
passcode matrix). Four timeline tests were re-pointed from
`setAutopilotEnabled(false)` to `takeover()` — they used a disabled plan to
reach "manual", which the ruling now forbids; pending-lease coverage is intact.

**Open gap (highest-priority follow-up):** CaptainPad has NO takeover-passcode
prompt yet. `PrivilegedAuthSheet` exists but only logs in for a session. Until
the TAKE OVER buttons open it per attempt and send `X-CaptainPad-Passcode`,
performance-mode takeover from CaptainPad returns `TAKEOVER_AUTH_REQUIRED`.

## _201 — takeover passcode prompt

Date 2026-08-14 · `CaptainPad/**` only · report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260814_201_takeover_passcode_prompt.md`

Closes _200's flagged gap: CaptainPad now PROMPTS for the operator passcode,
per attempt, whenever performance mode is live and something tries to take the
rig from the timeline.

**One gate, exhaustive by construction.** CaptainPad has exactly two functions
that can POST `/timeline/takeover` (`useTimeline._takeover` /
`_performTakeover`), so gating those covers every affordance: the PlanLockBanner
TEMPORARY TAKE OVER on deck/mixer/touch-control, the mixer's
takeover-and-switch-output variant, the IMPLICIT takeover fired by touching any
manual control under a live plan (`useOperatorTakeover.notifyInteraction`, ~20
call sites), and the EVENT sheet's scoped PERFORM. New
`utils/takeover_passcode.ts` holds the pure gate + a prompt broker; one app-wide
`TakeoverPasscodeHost` mounted outside `<Tabs>` renders the sheet.

**New sheet, not PrivilegedAuthSheet.** That one opens a 30-minute SESSION and
offers "remember on this device" — exactly what the ruling forbids. The new one
borrows its visual idiom and drops every persistence affordance. Big-thumb /
night: 64pt input at 22pt, 56pt buttons, secureTextEntry, theme tokens only.

**Storage audit: the passcode lives nowhere but the in-flight request.** Typed
chars in ONE `useState`, wiped on submit AND on close; passed as a function
argument to `postTimelineTakeover(body, passcode)`; lands in one
`X-CaptainPad-Passcode` header. No module state, no AsyncStorage, no session, no
retry cache, never logged, never echoed in an error. Two consecutive takeovers
prompt twice.

**Three outcomes, not two.** `takeover()` now returns
`'ok' | 'cancelled' | 'failed'`; CANCEL issues NO request and never alerts (a
cancelled mixer takeover also skips the layer switch). Only the three engine
codes count as passcode refusals — everything else closes the sheet and goes to
the normal error channel. The engine's own lockout (incl. `retryAfterMs`) is
surfaced verbatim; no client-side lockout invented. No host mounted → throws
loudly rather than taking over unauthenticated.

**Tests.** +35 (`utils/takeover_passcode.test.ts` 18,
`utils/timeline_takeover_api.test.ts` 5, `hooks/useTimeline_takeover.test.ts`
12). CaptainPad vitest **1078 → 1113 pass, 0 fail** (same empty failing list);
`tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint 0 errors. Placeholder passcodes only.

**Remaining gap:** the Live Touch **panel** ARM button is not CaptainPad code —
it lives in `docs/ui/touch_control_wire.js` (iframe from the sim on :6969) and
still hits the engine's `/layers/*` live_touch gate with no prompt. Out of this
task's `CaptainPad/**` boundary; needs its own prompt or a bridge through
CaptainPad's host over `live_touch_bridge`.

## _203 — party signal disconnect honesty

Date 2026-08-14 · `CaptainPad/**` only · report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260814_203_party_signal_honesty.md`

Audio-closure campaign fix 1: the AUDIO tab's PARTY SIGNAL pill no longer
asserts ON/OFF from a cache with no engine behind it.

**The seam is the transport, not the value.** `audioParty` rides `liveParams` on
`/ws/signals`, and that cache is deliberately never cleared on disconnect (every
meter holds its last frame). New narrow hook `useLiveSignalsConnected()` in
`hooks/useEngineState.ts` subscribes ONLY to the signals-bus status — it
re-renders on connect/disconnect edges, never at the 15-30 Hz value cadence, and
mutates nothing. New pure reducer `nextPartySignalTruth()` in
`utils/audioSignals.ts` folds `{connected, doc, value}` into the value the pill
may display; `describePartySignal` still owns the 0.5 boundary, untouched.
`audio.tsx` reduces into a ref DURING RENDER so the unknown paints on the same
frame as the drop.

**Freshness = document IDENTITY.** The engine replays its last cached
`liveParams` payload to every fresh `/ws/signals` connection, so "a message
arrived" needed a sharper test than message count — but NOT "revision moved"
(that replayed value is the engine's real held gate; gating on it would hold `…`
forever on a quiet analyser) and NOT a staleness timer (`liveParams` is
change-driven — a calm room emits no frames, so a timeout would flip a healthy
rig to unknown, and it would mean inventing a threshold). Each WS frame parses
to a fresh object, so identity cleanly separates "the engine just told us" from
"React still holds the pre-outage frame".

**Behaviour:** startup `…`; live `>=0.5` ON; live `<0.5` OFF; drop while ON or
OFF → `…` immediately; reconnect → `…` until a document actually arrives, then
whatever THAT says. Pill tone unchanged, no second party threshold, no detection
retuned, no unrelated live state cleared.

**Tests.** +8 in `utils/audioSignals.test.ts` (the six required + no-audioParty
and idempotence guards), asserting the operator-visible label end to end.
CaptainPad vitest **1113 → 1121 pass, 0 fail** (same empty failing list);
`tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint 0 errors on the touched files (2 pre-existing
warnings in `useEngineState.ts`, untouched lines); `npm run web:build` exports.
No component test — vitest here is scoped to pure `.ts` and there is no RN
testing library in the tree.

**Residual:** a half-open socket (Wi-Fi vanishing with no TCP close) still reads
connected until the OS times it out. Closing that needs an engine-side heartbeat
on the signals topic — engine work, new contract, not a presentation fix.

## _202 — live touch ARM passcode

Date 2026-08-14 · `docs/ui/**` + `simulation/tests/**` · report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260814_202_livetouch_arm_passcode.md`

Closes _201 §7.1 / _200 §5.1 — the LAST surface that could seize a running plan
without being asked. The Live Touch panel (sim-served `docs/ui/touch_control*`,
iframed into CaptainPad's touch-control tab) now prompts for the operator
passcode per attempt and retries exactly one request with
`X-CaptainPad-Passcode`.

**Affordance audit — ARM is the only one.** The engine gate
(`checkTakeoverPasscode`) has three call sites; this surface reaches two.
`/timeline/takeover` is CaptainPad's (covered by _201). `POST /layers/activate
target:'live_touch'` while `controlLock === 'plan'` **is the ARM button** — the
only `/layers/activate` in the wire that is both owner-tagged and pointed at
`live_touch`; handback, abort, idle-route-sync and the pagehide keepalive all
target deck/mixer and are never gated. The third, the IMPLICIT re-takeover the
engine maps onto any owner-tagged mutation, is a fader mid-drag, not a takeover
gesture: the engine itself answers it with "make an explicit takeover gesture",
so it is REPORTED loudly ("press ARM to take over with an operator passcode")
rather than raising a modal from a fader movement. After _200's force-disarm it
is nearly unreachable anyway (`armLeaseClear` clears the takeover owner).

**New `docs/ui/touch_control_passcode.js`** — same idiom as
`touch_control_lifecycle.js` (frozen `window` namespace, no imports, drivable
from `node:vm`), which is what makes the gate testable without a browser. It
classifies the three refusal codes, maps them to operator language, runs the
gate, and renders the sheet. `send(passcode)` is called exactly once per
submission — that shape is what makes "one retry" provable.

**No storage, anywhere.** The value is a function argument plus one `<input>`
wiped the instant it is read; nothing else holds it. No storage API is *called*
in either file, the gate never calls `postMessage`, no `postMessage` block in
the wire mentions a passcode, and nothing writes it to a URL. Two ARMs prompt
twice; cancel retries nothing and lands DISARMED; a rejection keeps one sheet
open with the ENGINE's reason and never echoes the attempt. No prompt available
→ loud refusal before the deadman lease is even taken.

**Iframe verified in a real Chromium child frame** (offline, gate module only,
faked transport, live stack on 6966-6972 never contacted): the sheet renders in
the child document and NOT the parent, the parent got zero postMessages across
the whole flow, focus lands on the input and real typing + Enter submits, the
overlay covers the frame viewport at `z-index:100000` (above Spatial fullscreen's
1000 and the wire's toast 9999) and sits outside the `inert`-able `#shell`.
Caveat left for the real iPad: iOS may not raise the soft keyboard for a
programmatic focus outside the touch gesture — mitigated with a 72 px box and a
printed "tap the box" hint. An abandoned sheet cannot hang the ARM chain:
`forceDisarmedUi()` and the `pageshow` cancel both call `closeTakeoverPrompt()`,
which resolves the pending ask as a cancel (the lifecycle guard only runs
*between* steps).

**Tests.** +25 in new `simulation/tests/touch_control_passcode.test.js`
(`node:test` + `node:vm` + a ~40-line DOM stub — no jsdom vendored). Sim suite
**2274 tests, 2266 pass, 7 fail**, failing list identical to the baseline
measured first (all 7 are another session's scene/fixture work). Engine
`tests/effects/touch_control_*` 32/32. `node --check` clean on both touched JS
files. `security_check --all` 6 findings, identical to baseline (pre-existing
MACs in gitignored `.scene_backups`). P0: placeholder passcodes only, injected
through the `send`/`prompt` seams.

**Residual:** nothing left on the takeover-passcode ruling — engine, CaptainPad
and Live Touch all prompt per attempt. The plan-predicate duplication from _200
§5.2 is still open, CaptainPad-side.

## _204 — companion PATCH retry + note docs

**Date:** 2026-08-14 · Report:
`.agent/reports/202608/20260814_204_companion_retry_note_docs.md`

**Fix 2 — derived-config PATCH now retries on a LIVE link.** The queue used to
park a failed snapshot in `pendingDerivedEdits` but clear `queue.pending`, so
the only thing that could ever push it again was `onStatus(connected)`. When the
HTTP request died while `/ws/control` stayed UP (ffmpeg respawn, `503
audio_not_initialized`, 2 s HTTP timeout) that event never came and the
operator's Derived Tune edit sat unsaved while the UI showed it applied.
`EngineConfigLink.patch()` now attaches `error.status` only when the engine
ANSWERED, so transport failure and verdict are distinguishable without parsing
prose. Transport failures, 5xx, 408 and 429 retry on **250 ms → 4000 ms
exponential backoff, 8 attempts (~23.75 s)**; every other 4xx reverts and is
**never** retried. On exhaustion the snapshot stays parked (still locally
authoritative, still replayed on reconnect) with a loud broadcast — never
dropped, never silently "saved". Serialization holds: the retry snapshot lives
on the timer, not in `queue.pending`, a newer edit cancels the armed retry, and
everything still funnels through `startDerivedGroupWrites` so concurrency stays
1 per group. The revert's truth-fetch gets the same bounded re-read.

**Fix 3 — the brief's premise was inverted; docs were right, the EVAL was
leaking.** `note_estimator_noisy.test.mjs` built its analyzer from
`loadEffectiveAudioAnalysisConfig({modelName:'titanic'})`, which merges
`states/titanic/audio_state.yaml` over `config.yaml` — so the operator's live
`bands.inputGain` moved the whole 24-seed holdout. Same code, same seeds:
**gain 1 (tracked config.yaml) → 93.43% settled / 51.09% full-seg / 99.17%
recall / 18-of-24**; gain 1.48 (HEAD state) → 94.07 / 51.43 / 99.17 / 18-of-24;
gain 9.1 (live worktree) → 98.27 / 57.94 / 100 / 22-of-24. The hermetic row
reproduces every published figure exactly, to two decimals, across eight
statistics. So the holdout was made **hermetic** (tracked `config.yaml` audio
block only, no scene overlay — all 4 tests still pass, no floor touched) rather
than bumping the docs to a number no other machine can reproduce. Only the
latency figures actually needed correcting: 440/450 ms → **451 ms**, 854 →
**853.6 ms**, 935 → **934.8 ms**, now identical in both surfaces. Heavy tier
(11.22 / 9.81 / 13.33) unchanged and explicitly re-marked report-only.

**Parity gate.** New `tests/audio/note_evidence_docs_parity.test.mjs` (5 tests)
parses `docs/AUDIO_SIGNALS.md` and `marsin_engine/config.yaml`, demands each
figure appear exactly once per surface, fails naming BOTH absolute paths on any
disagreement, holds a third witness (`EXPECTED_FIGURES`) so the same typo cannot
be pasted into both, checks the published moderate figures clear `HOLDOUT_POLICY`
floors parsed from the gate's source, and asserts heavy stays labelled
report-only. Negative control verified: flipping one docs figure fails loudly,
then restored byte-for-byte.

**Tests.** derived PATCH ordering 2 → **5** (+3, all asserting
`controlConnections === 1` so no run can secretly be the reconnect path); parity
**+5**. Focused batch (config API / store / transaction / analysis config /
audio config / derived-signals config / engine link / derived config / Derived
Tune UI / derived PATCH ordering / parity) **123/123**; BPM evaluator + noisy
note + synthetic note **20/20**; full companion suite **211/211**.
`git diff --check` clean; gitleaks clean on all seven touched files;
`security_check --all` 6 findings = the `_173` baseline (gitignored
`.scene_backups` MACs). `states/**` SHA-256 identical before/after — zero
residue. Live stack untouched: no mic, no 6966-6972/5568/8081/10000.

**Residual:** eleven other test files call `loadEffectiveAudioAnalysisConfig`
and may carry the same scene-overlay reproducibility hole — worth an audit.
Separately, gain 9.1 genuinely scores far better on note tracking than the
shipped `inputGain: 1`; that is an operator tuning call, deliberately out of
this thread's scope.
