## _212 — mirror reload resilience

Date: 2026-08-14. Report:
`.agent/reports/202608/20260814_212_mirror_reload_resilience.md`.
Files: `marsin_engine/lib/sacn_output.js`, `simulation/server/sacn_bridge.js`,
`simulation/server/sacn_output_bridge.js`, +2 test files.

**Incident B (two silent `code=1` bridge exits) — NOT a crash.** `sacn-in` died
~20 min into a stuck mirror; `sacn-out` died earlier the same evening during
ordinary operation with no mirror activity — the control case that breaks the
"stuck mirror killed it" theory. Ruled out every internal cause: children run
`stdio: 'inherit'` and Windows pipes are synchronous (verified — 6.3 MB through
a slow reader then `exit(1)`, nothing lost), every in-process `exit(1)` site
prints `❌` first, an escaped throw prints a stack (verified on Node v24.18.0),
the launcher's freeze-kill logs two lines first and logged neither, and
`sacn-out` is 115 lines with no sender/timer/state and no path to `code=1` at
all. **`taskkill /F` on Windows exits `code=1`, `signal=null`, silent** —
reproduced exactly. Both victims are the two `bridge: true` children and the two
sACN-port holders (`:5568`/`:6971`, `:6972`); `http`/`save` survived both. So:
force-killed from outside, almost certainly a port sweep / partial teardown from
a concurrent session. Standing hazard — a force-kill **while armed skips the
blackout**, freezing the mirrored boxes.

**The stuck path is provably bounded** (all state keyed by destination/universe;
~1.4 log lines/s) and now pinned by test — it cannot kill the bridge at any
duration.

**Real killer found en route:** `readSceneTrees` had a bare `yaml.load` (its
sibling `readSceneRoutePairs` always guarded its own) reached from
`resolveMirrorFor` above that function's `try` blocks, on the armed health check
**every 3 s** — a scene file saved mid-write by another agent → unhandled
rejection out of the unawaited async engine poll → process death. Guarded, plus
`guardedRecompute` at the poll call site.

**Hardening (both bridges):** `uncaughtException`/`unhandledRejection` → name it
with its stack, then **exit nonzero** (loud then dead; continuing on unknown
state is a fallback, and a wedged-but-responsive bridge is invisible to the
freeze watchdog — supervision is the recovery mechanism, and a restart comes up
disarmed with full relay). Armed `sacn-in` takes the bounded blackout first.
Plus a **synchronous `fs.writeSync(2)` exit breadcrumb** stating what its own
absence means — self-exit vs external kill is now distinguishable, which is the
one thing that would have closed this in seconds.

**Incident class A killed at the root.** `sacn` gives each `Sender` its own
counter, so universes stayed aligned only by the accident of being built
together and fed every frame. A hot reload breaks all three legs (new sender
starts at 0 mid-run; a de-mapped universe keeps its sender but freezes its
counter; the 3× blackout burst skews +3). Fix: **one engine-frame sequence
stamped onto every sender in `sendFrame`** — alignment by construction, immune
to sender lifetime, still strictly-forward and mod-256 legal. The mirror's
all-sequences-equal proof is untouched. Guarded by a startup assertion that
`sacn`'s `sequence` property still exists.

**Operationally: the "model reload while armed" playbook is gone** — the armed
mirror now rides through a reload with at most a brief pause. No restart, no
re-arm. **The live engine gets this at its next restart** (nothing applied to the
running stack; HIGH ports + black-holed sACN only).

**Tests.** Engine wire suite 11→15 (+4 alignment/model-reload), **verified
non-vacuous**: with the stamp neutralised both MODEL RELOAD tests fail. New
`bench_mirror_stuck_longevity.test.js` (3): 4,000 accelerated refused frames —
emits nothing, still naming the offset in its LAST line, throttled, O(1) heap,
still answers, and **recovers on its own** when the offset clears. Suites:
engine **3335/3330 pass/5 fail**, sim **2276/2262/13**, bench-mirror + all
bridge + launcher + contract **256/255/1**. Every failure pre-existing and
outside this slice (engine: `dev_test_bench` `groupBits out of sync`; sim:
fixture/patch/scene-CLI, CaptainPad theme parity, display orientation, and
`_176 §5.3` stray state file from another session's run).

## _219 — TEST-NET-1 sACN black hole (engine test sweep) — 2026-08-14

**The fake black hole is gone.** Every engine-spawning test pointed `--dest` /
`sacn.destinations` at a LOOPBACK address and called it black-holed. It never
was: the sim's sACN receiver binds `0.0.0.0`, so it accepts datagrams aimed at
ANY local address and all of `127.0.0.0/8` is local — those frames were
received by the operator's bridge and relayed to the rig exactly like ones
addressed to the default. Same flaw `_173` measured and fixed for the
COMPANION endpoints; it was never carried across to sACN (`_211` re-disclosed
it, nobody swept it). Report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260814_219_testnet1_sacn_dest_sweep.md`.

**The sweep: 48 literals, 22 files.** 45 under `marsin_engine/tests/` (21
files: all `e2e/`, `effects/`, `state/`, plus `integration/`, `security/`,
`special_events/`, and the `helpers/spawn_engine.mjs` doc-comment every new
suite copies) + 3 in
`simulation/agent_tools/live_touch_arm_lifecycle_test.cjs` (new
`BLACKHOLE_HOST` const, the config write, and its own can't-reach-a-controller
self-assert). All now on **TEST-NET-1 (`192.0.2.x`, RFC 5737 — reserved for
documentation, never routed)**. `config_boot_matrix` alone was 13 sites (6
`--dest`, 4 YAML fixtures, 3 comments). Comments were rewritten to say WHY
loopback is not a black hole, so the wrong answer isn't re-derived. Left
alone: `effects/color_window_engine_api.test.js` (a concurrent agent had
already converted it) and the two hits in `helpers/companion_isolation.mjs`,
whose doc-comment names the loopback address as the COUNTER-example.

**Re-taught, not just patched.** `.agent/memory/spawning_a_test_engine.md` got
a new "the black hole must NOT be a loopback address" section + a corrected
harness recipe; `.agent/ops/timeline_e2e_tests.md` safety wall 1 now
prescribes TEST-NET-1. Historical reports/tracker blocks untouched.

**Verify:** `npm test` = **3360 / 3353 pass / 7 fail**. Failing list vs
baseline: the 5 `dev_test_bench` groupBits drifts + the split-baby-galleries
gallery test, both pre-existing; **plus one FOREIGN** —
`tests/patterns/party_dancers.test.js` (UNTRACKED, a concurrent agent's
in-progress suite, 0.7625 vs 0.75), not chased. Zero new failures in anything
I touched; all 11 real-engine-spawning suites still boot and pass, which is
the actual regression signal. `security_check.py --all` = 6 findings, the
`_204`/`_214` baseline (gitignored `.scene_backups/` MACs). No git ops, no
pinned port bound, no `states/**` or `simulation/scenes/**` write from my run
(the modified `states/titanic/*` are the live engine autosaving, newest write
stamped before my suite started).

**Flagged, not done:** `.gitleaks.toml` asymmetry — `bm26-public-ip`
allowlists the RFC 5737 ranges, `bm26-report-ip` (which covers `.agent/**`)
does not, so the prescribed black hole can't be written as a literal quad in
any agent doc. Docs say `192.0.2.x` instead. Adding the RFC 5737 line to
`bm26-report-ip` is the tidy fix but loosening a privacy rule is Sina's call.

## _217 — COLORS schemes + engine crossfade + fullscreen + perf overlay — 2026-08-14

**The `_216` contract built, all 11 items** (`docs/55_colors_schemes_and_perf_overlay.md`);
report `.agent/reports/202608/20260814_217_colors_schemes_perf_overlay_impl.md`.
The operator's five intents: Live Touch scheme generators in the Deck COLORS
window, the crossfade DRIVES THE RIG, the scheme's five colours feed it,
PATTERNS fullscreen when alone, performance mode hides PARAMS + AUTOPILOT.

**The tab clock is gone and the daemon does the work.** Intents 2 and 3
collapsed into ONE mechanism, as designed: a crossfade IS a 2-entry chained
TURNS ring `[(A,B),(B,A)]` on the EXISTING colour-autopilot daemon, with
`delay_s: 0` for the continuous triangle. The `_211` preview loop is retired —
no `setInterval`, no rAF, no `phase` left in `colors_window.tsx`; the card is
`CROSSFADE · DRIVES THE RIG` and its wash / PAR strip / wheel handles / BLEND
readout all derive from the broadcast `colorPalette1/2`. STOP freezes natively
(`_cancelTween`). Measured on the OPERATOR'S rig through the :7167 dist:
`{delay_s:1, transitionMs:1500}`, `/param-center` walked
0.4312 → 0.1713 → 0.0000 → 0.0536 → 0.1135, then STOP held 0.130000 across two
reads 1.5 s apart. Rig restored byte-for-byte afterwards (palette AND the
5-pair config), verified field by field.

**The hidden fallback the design named is dead.** `_scheduleNext`'s
`Number(st.delay_s) > 0 ? … : DEFAULT_DELAY_S` would have turned the
operator's explicit CONT into a silent 30 s hold (codex P0). Gone; the default
now covers only the truly-absent case, and that narrowing has its own test so
it cannot creep back. `validate` refuses `delay_s 0` with `transitionMs < 100`
outright — zero hold plus zero fade is a CPC spin loop and must be
unrepresentable, not clamped.

**D1 shipped with one AS BUILT refinement: `isColourShaped` is
RANGE-checked.** A pure shape check breaks on values that are not on the unit
wheel — the existing crossfade fixtures use `h` = 0/100/240, and
`lerpHue(0,100,t)` collapses the modular delta to zero, so the fade would
silently STOP MOVING. Requiring every channel finite in `[0,1]` is the
precondition modular arithmetic needs, and it is exactly what keeps the
contract's "existing lerp tests unchanged" true. Reference table pinned in
BOTH suites so engine and client can never drift.

**D2 shipped whole:** `c1`/`c2` are a hue number OR `{h,s,v}`, validated by one
exported `validatePaletteChannel` that the daemon AND `api_server`'s resolver
share, so the two front doors cannot disagree. Client emits a plain number
whenever s=1∧v=1, so every existing ring keeps its exact wire. All four
generators port VERBATIM. `litPairIndex` now compares all three channels —
without that a HUE ring (five entries at ONE hue) highlights turn 1 for ever.

**The overlay cannot write layout, by construction.** `effectiveOpenWindows` /
`effectiveRailWindows` / `patternsFillsNarrow` are pure functions;
`useDeckWorkspace()` reads `usePerformanceMode().active` RAW (not
`usePerfLock()` — the captain bypass is edit rights, not screen composition)
and answers `open`/`isOpen`/`flexFor` from the effective set. There is no
action to dispatch, so the reducer and `deck_workspace_layout_v1` are never
reached. MEASURED: the stored value is byte-identical BEFORE / DURING / AFTER
a perf round trip in both orientations. Chips SUPPRESSED per D3 with the
static caption; COLORS stays exactly as the operator left it.

**Verify:** CaptainPad **1372 pass / 6 skip / 0 fail** (was 1328/6/0; +44),
**failing list EMPTY both sides**; `tsc --noEmit` clean; eslint clean on all
ten touched files. Engine failing list = the 5 `dev_test_bench` groupBits
drifts + the baby-gallery ENOENT + `party_dancers` (a pattern-tuning numeric
drift, `0.7625` vs `0.75`, from the concurrent audio-tuning work on this
branch — this wave touched zero pattern files and it fails identically in
isolation). Colour suites 56/56 (was 37). 24 screenshots in `~/tmp/fix_217/`,

Rows needing CONT / full-HSV ran against an ISOLATED engine on :7842 (scratch

## _223 — Live Touch: pixel view unavailable + first-load theme flash — 2026-08-15

**Two operator regressions, one pass. Neither came from _217 or _221.**
Report `.agent/reports/202608/20260815_223_live_touch_pixel_view_debug.md`.

**Symptom 1 — "PIXEL VIEW UNAVAILABLE".** Live Touch reads a pre-resolved
artifact (`docs/ui/touch_control_pixel_views.json`) that byte-fingerprints
every input and **fails closed** on any mismatch. Exactly one of five
fingerprints was wrong: `viewsFingerprint` vs
`simulation/scenes/titanic/pixel_map_views.yaml`. The exporter's own
`--check` agreed. **The resolved geometry had not changed at all** — a clean
re-export moved **0 glyphs, maxdelta 0.0** across all four views; the only
delta was `views[top_down].framing` (saved zoom/pan) plus `yaml.dump()` key
reordering. So the brick came from the operator **framing the 2D Pixel Map**:
it auto-saves on every pan/zoom via `POST /save-pixel-map-views`, rewriting
the YAML, and nothing regenerated the artifact. **Confirmed live mid-session**
— after re-exporting at 08:07:57 the YAML moved again at 08:14:10
(`panX -0.58 → -35.58`) and Live Touch re-bricked instantly. A repeating
brick, not one-off staleness.

**Fix 1:** re-exported the artifact, AND closed the loop in
`simulation/server/save-server.js` — a successful titanic pixel-map write now
re-runs the exporter. The layout is already on disk at that point, so an
export failure does NOT fail the save (never lose the operator's arrangement):
it is returned in the response body and logged loudly. `child_process` at top
of file per AGENTS.md.

**Symptom 2 — blue-then-gruvbox flash.** `touch_control.html` hard-codes a
standalone blue `:root` (`--bg #1c3054`), `touch_control_theme.js` loads at
**line 5736 of 5751 — end of body**, and the host only replies after the
iframe `load` event plus a postMessage round trip. The theme link stamped
`theme-pending`/`theme-applied`, but **no CSS rule for either class existed
anywhere in the repo** — the classes were inert.

**Fix 2:** a first-paint gate, NOT a fallback palette (P0). Synchronous
`<head>` script stamps `theme-pending` when embedded; CSS hides the body AND
makes both backgrounds transparent AND neutralises `color-scheme`. `fail()`
now releases the gate so a broken handshake shows a visible error, never a
blank rectangle. **Two traps caught only by reading rendered pixels:**
`visibility:hidden` alone still painted solid `#1c3054` (an element's
background reaches the canvas even unpainted — html propagates, then body),
and under `color-scheme: dark` a "transparent" iframe still paints Chrome's
`#121212` base (MEASURED `rgb(18,18,18)`).

**Verify:** CDP `Page.startScreencast` frame-by-frame, control = the same file
with only the gate stripped. PRE-FIX **3 wrong-palette frames (1173..1200ms)**

privileged auth enabled (`BM26_CAPTAINPAD_AUTH_REQUIRED=1`) boots INTO
performance mode, capturing the pre-show snapshot from boot state (capture
failure = fatal); auth-off benches boot unlocked byte-identically; pads need

`editSession.principal` (owner/collaborator/bringup) set at exit, re-asserted
via new `POST /edit-session` (escalation + handover), broadcast as
`editPrincipal`; no timeout; dies on restart. (D4) multi-pad: persistence
follows the GLOBAL session principal, never the originating pad; owner
escalation blesses the current live look (stated in sheet copy). (D5/D6)
`effectiveAutoSave()` (:1363) gains a `principalMaySave()` term; sailor
sessions also SKIP `recordPendingDeckFlush` so owner keep-save can never
flush sailor tuning; explicit file-writers 403 `EDIT_PRINCIPAL_READONLY`

explicit captures :12630/:13141, `/settings` :12749, `/settings/save-now`
:12779); live param + structural edit routes stay OPEN. (D7) exit matrix:
`keep-save` owner-only; sailor `keep`/`restore` skip `forcePersist` so disk
stays as Sina left it. (D9) `engine.js shutdown()` writes zero state
(verified) → restart during a sailor session restores Sina's disk; chokes
re-read the gate at write time (timer-safe). (D8) loud-not-spammy: one log
line per session transition/403; amber `SAILOR SESSION — LIVE, NOT SAVING`
chip (tap = escalate); exit sheet reuses the takeover-passcode idiom (no
remember, wiped field).

## _229 — BENCH MIRROR STUCK recurrence: false alarm, `_212` holds — 2026-08-15

Read-only forensics on the live launcher log. Report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260815_229_bench_mirror_stuck_recurrence.md`. No code
edited, no git ops, nothing on 6966-6972 touched beyond two GETs.

**`_212` did NOT regress — every STUCK line today is a false positive, and the
engine never needed restarting.** Three independent proofs the engine-frame stamp
is live: the hunk is intact in `sacn_output.js`; the engine never rebuilt a
sender (one `Loading model...`, one `Sender started — 38 universe(s)`, live
`frame 549231`, `modelStale:false`, ~3.8 h continuous); and **the armed mirror
rode through FOUR model hot-reloads** (log lines 1788/2580/3335/4318) — pre-`_212`
the first would have wedged it permanently. That is the fix working, observed live.

**Root cause: the STUCK discriminator calls a torn read a fixed sender offset.**
`offsetSignature` normalises against the MOST ADVANCED source, so on any torn
flush the leader gets `d=0` and **every other source gets `d<0` by construction**;
`minLag` is then only ever sampled on already-torn flushes, so a universe that is
merely *systematically last in the engine's 38-universe send burst* never reaches
lag 0 and six consecutive tears declare it "at a FIXED sequence offset". The
source comment states the right intent ("is the offset the SAME on consecutive
flushes") but the code asks a weaker question that cannot be answered no.
Compounding it: `flushMirrors` gives a MISSING source 250 ms of grace as "NORMAL
for the few milliseconds between an engine frame's datagrams", but a source that
has arrived carrying the NEXT frame's sequence — the identical situation — gets an
immediate `❌` telling the operator to restart a healthy engine.

**Evidence.** 975 NOT WHOLE + 48 STUCK over 3h43m armed. **Circular spread is
exactly 1 in 850/975**; 33/48 STUCK name offset `-1`; 47/48 fire at the bare
minimum `flushes=6`. Decisive: **`count in this run` is `1` in ALL 975 lines,
never 2** — `_mirrorMisaligned` is cleared only on the aligned-emit path, so the
destination composed a whole frame between every pair. 3209 torn flushes against
~535,000 frames = **0.6 % tear rate**. A real offset is a large arbitrary constant
(frames elapsed between sender constructions), never 1, and composes ZERO whole
frames. Mechanism: `sendFrame` writes all 38 universes in one synchronous burst;
`mirrorInbound` schedules `setImmediate(flushMirrors)` after ANY single region
arrives, so a poll phase that delivers part of the burst yields `{N+1, N, N}`.
The 125 large-spread outliers (9-124) all cluster in 08:32-08:38 under CPU load
(live-touch `130_spatial_paint`, Expo SSR bundling, 2 sim clients, headless-Chrome
agents, audio mood source stale 10-39 s) — real frame loss, still self-healing.
Engine→bridge is **unicast 127.0.0.1**, so the Wi-Fi-multicast theory is out.

**`sacn-in` `code=1` at 08:38:24Z = external force-kill, a casualty not the
cause.** Zero breadcrumbs, zero FATAL, zero watchdog lines → `_212`'s decision
rule says killed from outside. Mechanism identified: `tools/port_cleanup.cjs`
resolves the **UDP :5568** holder via `netstat -ano -p udp` and `taskkill /T /F`s
it — that is `sacn-in` alone, which is why `sacn-out` (TCP :6972) survived. The
tearing predates the bounce by 3h43m.

**Bench is HEALTHY — restart NOTHING.** Supervised restart came up disarmed
(bench boxes held their last frame — the force-kill skips the blackout, `_212`'s
standing hazard recurring); operator re-armed 08:44:04Z; since then **2 NOT WHOLE,
0 STUCK**. The "**RESTART THE ENGINE**" instruction was wrong all 48 times.

**Proposed permanent fix (design only, NOT implemented — tree is mid-surgery).**
F1 an offset of 1 is never "fixed". **F2 (strongest, deletes the class alone)**
gate STUCK on `_mirrorLastWholeAt` — a genuine sender offset composes ZERO whole
frames. F3 make "fixed" literal: singleton set of observed `d`, `|d|>1`. F4 give
a torn read the same settling grace a missing source gets; summarise tears
periodically instead of 975 immediate `⚠`s. F5 rewrite the STUCK remedy text —
this is the wording follow-up `_212` deferred, now actively misleading. F6
optional one-deep staging slot per region to erase the residual 0.6 % drop. F7
`port_cleanup.cjs` should refuse to kill a bridge holding an armed mirror.

## _224 — COLORS: one transport, a sliding window, a pickable pair — 2026-08-15

**Four operator orders on the Deck COLORS window, all landed** — report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260815_224_turns_rotation_polish.md`. Client only:
`components/deck/colors_window_logic.ts` + `colors_window.tsx` and the two
colour suites. **No engine source change was needed** (`_217` already made
`delay_s: 0` and full-HSV rings legal, and a five-entry ring at zero hold was
already representable), so `api_server.js` (`_228`) and `app/(tabs)/index.tsx`
(`_225`) were never opened.

**1 — ONE TRANSPORT** (*"the turning ... needs to happen on the same timescale
as the two color crossfader"* / *"use the same fade time out and interval as the
two color"*). TURNS and the crossfade now share one FADE row, one HOLD row, one
pair of values and one patch builder: both cards render the SAME
`<TransportTiming>`, and `turnsAutopilotPatch` / `crossfadeAutopilotPatch` are
one-liners over `rotationAutopilotPatch(colours, holdS, fadeS)`.
**`derivedTransitionMs` is DELETED** — a derived 25 % fade was a second opinion
the surface could not show. The crossfade is now *literally* the same function at
ring length 2 (`turnsPairs([A,B])` IS `[{c1:A,c2:B},{c1:B,c2:A}]`, and the
hue-only A/B pin minimizes both channels to plain numbers, so the wire is
byte-identical to `_217`'s). **docs/55 §2.3's "TURNS keeps its cadence floor" is
SUPERSEDED**: CONT (`delay_s: 0`) is reachable from TURNS, so a five-colour ring
slides continuously — the engine's zero-hold-plus-zero-fade guard is untouched
and the client mirrors that refusal so the operator sees a sentence, not a
rejected POST. The shared HOLD row is a SUPERSET of the crossfade card's
(`0/1/2/5/10/30/60 s`) so set-and-forget cadences survive; 120/180 s do not, and
the shared default is CONT + 0.8 s rather than TURNS' old 30 s.

**2 — THE SLIDING WINDOW, INVERTED FROM THE RIG.** The ring `turnsPairs` builds
already WAS the operator's window (pair *i* spans slots *i*, *i+1*, sliding one
step per turn, wrapping) — what was missing was the readout. `litPairIndex` only
recognises the rig when it sits EXACTLY on a pair, i.e. during the hold, so **in
CONT the highlight would never light at all**. New `rotationCursor(palettes,
c1, c2)` inverts the engine's own tween: the daemon writes
`lerpParams(pair[i-1], pair[i], t)` (`h` short-arc, `s`/`v` linear), so six
components with one unknown → a least-squares projection onto the from→to
segment plus a residual check (`CURSOR_FIT_EPS 2e-3`) that REJECTS a palette some
other writer set rather than mapping it onto a plausible-looking progress.
Returns the window being ARRIVED AT and how far through, or `null` (the card says
so instead of lying). **The deadman rule holds** — derived, never clocked; it
moves only as broadcast tween frames arrive and stops dead when the rig does;
still zero `setInterval`/rAF in the file. On the glass: BOTH slots of the live
window light, a new `WindowRail` parks a two-cell highlight at
`cursorRailOffset` (drawn twice inside a clip so the T5→T1 turn slides THROUGH
the seam instead of teleporting), and the caption reads `On the rig now: T5 + T1,
holding.` / `Sliding to T4 + T5 — 62% through.` A MASTER ring has no fade fit by
construction (identical endpoints, no direction) — HOLD matches, otherwise
`null`, because inventing a direction would be a fallback.

**3 — WHICH TWO OF THE FIVE FEED A AND B.** With a scheme latched, two-colour
mode shows the five staged colours with the active two badged A/B. The gesture is
the window's EXISTING arm-then-tap grammar (COLOUR A / COLOUR B arm; a slot tap
assigns to the armed channel), and the selection is stored as **RING INDICES, not
colours**, so a wheel re-theme carries it forward — slots 2+4 stay slots 2+4 in
the regenerated palette. Both channels on one slot is REFUSED with a sentence
naming the conflict (a crossfade from a colour to itself is a dead transport);
the pick is still RECORDED when the manual-write gate refuses the WRITE, so it
survives to when the rotation stops. **A real bug the screenshots caught:** A and
B collapsed onto ONE hue after a re-pick, because `latched` was a bare `SchemeId`
and the base hue was re-derived from the ARMED slot — circular once A/B are
themselves scheme slots, so arming B re-themed the ring underneath the pick.
Fixed by making the latch `{ scheme, base }` — two values that must never
disagree, so they are one piece of state. While latched the row generates from
the latch's base (CONTRAST → TRIADIC keeps the hue) and **only a wheel drag
re-bases**; caption now reads `TRIADIC is latched at 226°`.

**4 — FIVE MORE GENERATORS** (*"add a few more technique to sample nice looking
color duos or 5 samples"*). `SCHEME_IDS` 4 → 9, the ports keeping their original
places at the head of the row: **ANALOGOUS** (±15/±30°, alternating sides),
**TRIADIC** (120° triad + two dimmed echoes), **SPLIT** (150/210° flanks — the
true 180° is deliberately absent), **TETRAD** (90° square + a dimmed base),
**GOLDEN** (five 137.5° steps → 0/137.5/275/52.5/190). Two rules shape them, both
about what the RIG does: adjacent pairs are the product (every neighbour
including the T5→T1 wrap must be a duo picked on purpose), and **no dead beat** —
where a construction repeats its base the repeat is DIMMED, pinned by a test that
no new ring has two identical adjacent colours. **Night-visibility floor
`SCHEME_ROTATION_MIN_V = 0.25`** (HUE's darkest step, the accepted precedent); the
four ports keep their own verbatim `0.1` floor, because re-flooring a PORT would
make the Deck and Live Touch disagree about what MASTER/HUE mean.

**Suites.** CaptainPad `npx vitest run` **1446 pass / 6 skip / 0 fail** (73
files), **failing list EMPTY**; `colors_window_logic.test.ts` 94 → **125**.
Engine `color_autopilot.test.js` **48/48** (+6: a 5-pair ring advancing one step

no new socket, no writes. A labelled two-chip toggle picks between two REAL
buffers: **`SHOW` (`preDimmer`, default)** and **`RIG` (post-dimmer hardware
truth)**. SHOW is the default on the engine's own documented reasoning (engine.js
~1300: dimmers "would otherwise wash the UI preview out to near-black") —
**measured live, `rig` averaged 50/1530 vs `preDimmer` 173, 92 % of samples under
value 40**, and the first screenshot pass rendered an almost invisible ship.

**THE RESOLUTION SEAM, declared not hidden.** The engine subsamples vis:
`vis.maxPixels: 100` + `visSampleIdx[i] = floor(i*pixelCount/maxPixels)` →
**measured 100 px/key at 5.2 Hz for a 964-pixel model**. That cap is not ours to
raise (`ChannelVizStrip` renders one RN `<View>` per sample per channel). So the
window draws EVERY mapped pixel at its true sim position and colours each from
the **nearest transmitted sample** — a ~10-px band along a strand, since model
indices are contiguous there — and **prints `720 PX · 100/964 COLOUR SAMPLES` on
screen**. `sampleIndexForModelPixel` is the tested exact inverse of the engine's
table, monotonic, and the IDENTITY once the cap stops binding. No colour is
invented; every byte drawn is one the engine really sent.

**Looks like the sim because it borrows the sim's two tricks:** `PREVIEW_GAMMA
0.6` (`_previewBrighten`, hue-preserving VALUE lift, display-only) and
`PIXEL_STAGE_BG '#0b0d12'` — the sim's own ground, **fixed on every theme** as an
`identity.ts`-class colour, because light only reads on dark and light-theme
`surfaceContainerLowest` is literally `#ffffff`. Plus an additive `lighter` halo
pass over lit pixels and half-pixel-snapped cores, with a faint ghost so the hull
keeps its shape through a blackout.

**Raw canvas, ZERO React on the frame path** (subscriber → ref → imperative draw;
typed arrays built once per view). **Measured live: 1000–1430 canvas fills/frame,
1.1–7.1 ms (median ~2–4 ms) at 618×463 → ~1–2 % duty at 5 Hz.** Hidden = mounted
but idle.

**Workspace:** id `pixels` appended LAST (every prior composition unchanged),
wide weight **4** (a wide-aspect picture is bounded by the narrower axis), chip
dot `C.secondary` — the palette's NEUTRAL, deliberately, since this window's
content IS colour; contrast-guarded on all five themes (gruvbox worst case 4.72)
and pinned in `restyle_contrast.test.ts`. **Performance overlay UNTOUCHED, like
COLORS** — the order said params & autopilot *settings*, and this window has no
controls; verified live, the screenshots were taken with the engine genuinely in
performance mode and PIXELS is visible in them. `_217`'s
`patternsFillsNarrow` still holds (PIXELS open = second window = pin restored).

**⚠ UPGRADE HAZARD FOUND AND FIXED — worth remembering.** "Default closed" does
NOT by itself leave existing layouts unchanged: only the CLOSED set is persisted,
so "open" is the absence of a name, and a store written before a window existed
cannot name it — a fifth window springs OPEN on everyone who ever touched the
bar. The store now also records **`known`** (the windows the writing build had an
opinion about); anything current and outside `known` is appended to `closed`, and
a store with no `known` is a pre-`_225` build treated as knowing the original
four (`LEGACY_KNOWN_WINDOWS`). **Key stays `deck_workspace_layout_v1`** — bumping
it would discard real preferences to fix one window. Reducer case matrix grew
8 → 16 reachable layouts.

**(2) Second playlist follows the app's layout mode.** `SplitPlaylistPanes` gains
`sideBySide`, wired `sideBySide={!isWide}`. **WIDE** (PATTERNS is a tall narrow
column): DECK B stays **under** DECK A, byte-identical to before. **NARROW**
(PATTERNS is a full-width short band): DECK B becomes a **column to the RIGHT** —
stacking there gave two ~140pt-tall panes, splitting sideways gives two
full-height columns. Same stored ratio (pane-1 share is meaningful on either
axis), same `[0.15,0.85]` engine clamp, same divider, same PanResponder; the axis
only selects the layout property, the gesture delta (`dx`/`dy`), the container
extent and the minimum (`MIN_PANE_W_PT 200` vs `MIN_PANE_PT 140`). **DECK B's ✕
unbind lifecycle untouched — placement only.** Axis read through a ref (survives
a mid-drag rotation); `touchAction:'none'` on web scoped to the NEW axis so the
shipped vertical divider is not disturbed.

## _233 — STUCK discriminator rebuilt + port-cleanup arm interlock — 2026-08-15

**`_229`'s design, implemented. The detector can now say "not stuck".** The old
one normalised offsets against the most advanced source (so every trailing
source read `d<0` by construction), sampled only on already-torn flushes, and
called 6 consecutive tears a FIXED sender offset — 48 false `❌ RESTART THE
ENGINE` lines in one session. Report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260815_233_stuck_discriminator_fix.md`.

**F1-F5 in `simulation/server/sacn_bridge.js`.** F2 (the class-deleter):
`_mirrorLastWholeAt`, stamped on the aligned path before the "nothing new to
say" short-circuit; STUCK needs 1000 ms with NO whole frame composed — a genuine
offset composes zero, a burst tear composes one every ~25 ms. F1:
`MIRROR_MIN_FIXED_OFFSET = 2`, so ±1 (850/975 of the incident's spreads) can
never be "fixed". F3: `offsetSignature` measures against a FIXED anchor (lowest
source universe) instead of the running max — the max flipped sign across the
sequence wrap — and the per-source SET of observed offsets must be a singleton;
capped at 2 values, so the stall path stays O(1) (`_212`'s property). F4: a torn
read gets the same 250 ms grace a missing source always had, and sub-grace tears
go to a per-destination rollup, ≤1 line/10 s, fired from both the torn and the
aligned path — its verdict half is DERIVED (a window with no composition says so
and points at the STUCK line). F5: `**RESTART THE ENGINE**` deleted; the line
states the measurement (`NO whole frame for X s` + `PERSISTENT multi-step
offset`) and names the causes that survive `_212` — dead source, second writer,
disarm/re-arm. **F6 skipped and documented in source**: a one-deep staging slot
puts two buffers per region into the one path that must stay trivially provable;
the residual 0.6 % drop is invisible on lights.

**F7 — `tools/port_cleanup.cjs` now refuses to kill an ARMED bridge.** The
bridge publishes a PID-stamped marker (`~/tmp/bm26_bench_mirror_armed.json`) in
the same synchronous turn the arm is recorded, releases it in the same turn the
arm is cleared, and reaps a stale claim at boot. `killPid` refuses only while
that PID is alive AND its command line still says `sacn_bridge.js` (stale claims
and PID reuse never wedge a launcher start); an unreadable marker widens the
refusal to any sACN bridge and says why. Override:
`BM26_FORCE_SACN_KILL=1` everywhere, `--force-sacn` for argv-forwarding callers
(`launcher.js` exits 2 on unknown options — its flag pass-through is a follow-up
for that file's owner). `writeArmMarker`/`clearArmMarker` REFUSE the production
path under `NODE_TEST_CONTEXT`; the harness injects a per-pid scratch marker.

**Verify:** `cd simulation && node --test tests/*.test.js` 2274/8 (baseline) →
2293/11, +22 tests. New `bench_mirror_stuck_discriminator.test.js` (7,
behavioural: the exact false-positive shape declares NO stuck and keeps
emitting; a 500 ms tear that recovers is NOT WHOLE, never STUCK; 30 burst tears
print nothing; a genuine 70-frame offset with zero whole frames STILL declares
STUCK) and `port_cleanup_arm_interlock.test.js` (13; nothing is ever killed —
the marker names PID 2147483647, which no OS can issue). The 3 extra reds are
`pattern_manifest.test.js` (`baby/`, `ambient_extra/`, generated `default.yaml`)
from the pattern-curation wave rewriting `marsin_engine/patterns/manifest.json`
mid-run — unreachable from this slice. Bridge-adjacent re-run 298/299 (the one

## _230 — Show autopilot: deck pattern rotation scoped to a special-event stage

**Scope changed mid-flight.** The brief opened with "author 6+ new tease patterns
past 20"; the operator then said *"don't add baby_tease patterns, just give me the
infra for it, I will ask chatgpt for the patterns themselves"*. Two drafts written
(`46_tease_checkerboard_morph`, `47_tease_ripple_interleave`) were **deleted** —
untracked, never committed, directory back to 45 immediately. A pattern author then
landed 35 files (tease 46-50, boy 51-65, girl 66-80) while I worked; that is not my
work, and §5 numbers are a snapshot of a set still being edited.

**The mechanism — one daemon, not two.** A stage may author `autopilot:`
{active, everySec, shuffle, groupMode/Size/Dwell, transition{enabled,mode,
durationMs,shuffle}}, and while it holds the rig the runner drives **the deck's own
pattern-autopilot daemon** (`lib/autopilot.js` + `deckTransitionConfig`) through the
same internals a timeline cue uses. A private timer in the runner would have raced
that daemon for the same deck channel; the daemon already awaits each swap before
rescheduling (`show 20s → fade 2s → next`, never overlapping), EBUSY-refuses
overlapping transitions, generation-guards every state change, and pre-warms the
next pattern. Falls out free: the card's countdown is the DECK's own
`nextSwapAtMs`, and a rotating tease is indistinguishable from the operator working
the deck by hand. Engine-side per the deadman rule — no tab timer drives the rig.

**"The deck settings exactly, no colour."** The tab renders the deck's own
`<PatternAutopilotPanel>` **verbatim**, not a lookalike: PLAY/PAUSE, cadence pills,
SHUFFLE, GROUP+SIZE/DWELL, and the nested DECK TX (ON, STYLE, CROSSFADE TIME,
SHUFFLE STYLE). Colour is absent **by construction** — no colour field exists on the
wire and the runner keeps the colour autopilot disarmed all show (Baby is hard-coded
RGB; a palette write would hand the reveal's colour away). PROFILE omitted: it needs
an attach/detach dep the runner does not own.

**Three things that make it safe.** (1) `supported` ≠ `active`: a stage with no
`autopilot:` key draws NO card and rotation is forced OFF while it holds — a blackout
must not swap patterns behind a dark ship; `active:false` still offers the parked
controls. (2) Handover is **stop-first**: `fire()` stops the old rotation
synchronously before any new-stage action lands, and the new cadence arms only after
the stage's LAST authored action (the reveal swaps its playlist at +700 ms under a
white flash — arming at t=0 would time against the playlist about to be replaced).
(3) ARM now snapshots the **whole** deck autopilot block AND transition config, and
FINISH restores all of it. Previously only the on/off flag was restored — correct
when the runner only ever turned it OFF, and would now leave the operator's deck
cycling on the tease's 20 s timing. Rotation also stops before the 3 s restore morph.

**Live tuning that is remembered.** `POST /special-events/autopilot` (sparse patch,
`{status:'ok', state}`, existing WS `specialEvents` frame — **no new WS type**)
retunes live and persists per `showId/stageId` **across runs**, so tuning done at the
rail is there next night. `{reset:true}` returns to the show file; the tab shows a
"Tuned live" strip + **SHOW DEFAULT** whenever an override is in force, so the YAML
can never quietly become a lie.

**Infra (part A).** `baby_color_contract.test.js` filed patterns by a hardcoded
number-range table — which threw the moment `51_boy_keel_breath` landed. It is now
**derived from the filename** (`<NN>_<family>_<concept>`), twins pair by **shared
concept** not `boy+15`, playlist/manifest/gallery counts derive from disk or from the
source playlist, and floors (not targets) stop a silent shrink. Manifest + gallery
confirmed to need **zero code changes** for `baby/NN` ids. New
`marsin_engine/patterns/baby/README.md`: naming rule, five steps, every enforced
contract *with its reason*, measured floors, the regeneration one-liner, and what is
deliberately not enforced.

**Verify.** NEW `special_events_autopilot_api.test.js` **13/13** (real engine, port
17233, `--dest 192.0.2.x`): the deck pattern **advances on its own** with no request
between read and assertion; a live `everySec:17` appears on the DECK's own
`GET /autopilot` and `durationMs:4500` on `GET /deck/transition-config`; FINISH
restores a deliberately specific pre-show deck (`delay_s 55`, shuffle, `trans_iris`
@7000 ms) exactly; 8 refusals land by name, never clamped. Also `special_events_api`
28/28, `show_schema` 27/27, timeline+baby_reveal_sequence 8/8, sim `pattern_manifest`
6/6, gallery green, CaptainPad **75 files / 1491 pass / 0 fail** (+7 new), tsc +
eslint clean. `baby_color_contract` **6 pass / 4 fail — the 4 are REAL findings about
the author's new 46-80**, not regressions (green on 01-45): twins

**LIVE RELOAD REQUIRED — not optional.** The running :6968 engine executes the OLD

**The operator's order is now true engine-side: params and playlist changes are

`docs/56_principal_scoped_persistence.md` in full. Report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260815_228_principal_scoped_persistence_impl.md`.

**Engine (`lib/api_server.js`).** (W1) in-memory
`editSession {principal, unlockedAt}` + `principalMaySave()` as a third term in
`effectiveAutoSave()`; the ~80 auto-save chokes needed NO edits because they
already re-read the predicate at write time (which is also why a mid-flight
timer is honoured, not raced). One log line per transition, zero per cycle.
(W2) `bootLockForShow = captainPadAuth.required && !interruptedPerformanceMode`
arms the lock in the perf-mode init block, but the pre-show snapshot is captured
**after the boot restore** — `captureLook()` serializes the RESTORED mixer, so
capturing at the init block would have snapshotted a bare boot rig. Capture
failure = fatal throw. (W3) the session check at the old `:12884` is GONE;
`verifyPrincipalPasscode()` (shared ring/lockout/never-echo shape with
`checkTakeoverPasscode`) verifies per attempt and its principal becomes the

skip `forcePersist`). (W4) sailor sessions skip `recordPendingDeckFlush` —
**performance mode is deliberately excluded from that skip**, or the exit sheet's
"N unsaved entries" ask and the owner `keep-save` flush would have broken.
(W5) `rejectIfPrincipalReadonly` → 403 `EDIT_PRINCIPAL_READONLY` at all eight
writers, always AFTER the perf gate. (W6) `POST /edit-session` (escalation +
handover; 409 locked, 503 auth-off). Live param + structural edit routes stay
OPEN — sailors drive the rig, they just don't write it down.

**CaptainPad (W7).** `editPrincipal` **plus a new `authRequired`** on every
`performanceMode` frame/GET/replay — a null principal is ambiguous alone (show
engine "nobody unlocked saving" vs bench "no gate exists") and the engine knows,
so it says so; an ABSENT field preserves the previous value. Exit sheet gains the
`takeover_passcode_sheet` idiom (wiped field, no remember), an error box, and the
`Captain's passcode only.` caption; passcode rides the SAME request as the
choice. New `components/edit_session_chip.tsx` (amber `SAILOR/CREW SESSION —
LIVE, NOT SAVING`, silent for owner/locked/bench, tap = escalate) and
`useEditPersistLock()` folded into PlaylistPanel's `editable`. New
`utils/edit_session.ts` leaf owns the refusal copy and `TAKEOVER_PASSCODE_HEADER`

## _231 — Wedding: SPECIAL EVENT show #2, built from the existing catalog — 2026-08-15

**The operator said "also add a wedding program too", and that is the whole
spec.** Shipped `wedding_program` as PURE DATA — no engine code, no route, no UI
component, and **no new pattern**. Six stages, one thumb: `GATHERING →
PROCESSION → CEREMONY → THE KISS → CELEBRATION → PHOTO GLOW`, in **both**
scenes' `special_events/` (`simulation/scenes/test_bench/special_events/` did
not exist before — the bench had no shows at all, so the flow was unrehearsable
off the ship). CEREMONY rides the grand master down to 0.55 over 6 s and
authors **zero quick effects** on purpose (nothing on that screen can flash the
ship during vows). THE KISS is a ceremonial CHOICE like the reveal, because a
wedding kiss has one outcome but *what follows it* does not: `KISS → PARTY` and
`KISS → GLOW` share an identical 900 ms white flash and differ only in the
landing. CELEBRATION is a real stage, not a hold — it activates `wedding_party`
whichever way the kiss went. Report
`.agent/reports/202608/20260815_231_wedding_show.md`.

**Five playlists, 45 entries, every pattern already in the catalog.** 
`wedding_gathering` (10) · `wedding_procession` (8) · `wedding_ceremony` (6) ·
`wedding_party` (15) · `wedding_glow` (6), byte-identical across `titanic` and
`test_bench`. All use `defaults: {}` — the pattern's own authored defaults,
matching the curated `first_class_1912` — so nothing second-guesses the pattern
authors. Each list is ordered as an **arc** (procession: one white breath →
rising horizon → cathedral ribs → orbit rings → crown → tide → wake → arrival;
party: confetti-in, strobe-last), which is why every rotating stage sets
`shuffle: false`. The two calm stages lean on the **WHITE ONLY family (60-64)**,
which declares no `colorPalette1/2` and therefore **cannot be tinted by the live
global palette** — that is the only reason CEREMONY and PHOTO GLOW look right
regardless of what the deck was doing before ARM. Everything else takes the live
palette, and the schema has no palette verb (`globals` takes NUMBERS;
`colorPalette1/2` are `hsv` objects), so: **set a warm palette before ARM**
(`phoenix` is the closest shipped pair; there is no champagne/gold entry).

**The find that changed the show — THE KISS was DISSOLVING, not cutting.**
Measured on the bench: fire at 26174 ms, deck actually landed `wedding_party` at
**31911 ms (+5.7 s)**, so the 900 ms flash hid nothing and the audience would
have watched a five-second crossfade out of the candle-lit ceremony. Cause: the
runner applies a stage's `autopilot.transition` to the deck BEFORE that stage's
actions, and **a stage with no `autopilot:` block inherits whatever the previous
stage left latched** — here the ceremony's 5 s crossfade. Fixed inside the show
file: `kiss` authors `autopilot: { active: false, transition: { enabled: false } }`
— `active:false` keeps rotation off, `transition.enabled:false` is the real
payload. Re-measured: **+719 ms, under the flash.** Cost is a parked rotation
card on THE KISS; worth it. CELEBRATION and PHOTO GLOW re-establish soft
transitions so the cut does not leak, asserted in the test.

**Two engine gaps found, deliberately NOT fixed (runner is `_230`'s this wave).**
(1) The `globals` verb is **not restore-covered**: the special-event pre-show
snapshot uses `captureLook()` (master + deck + overlays + groups) and never
calls `captureGlobalsForSnapshot()`, so pinning SPEED for the vows would survive
FINISH and leave the night retuned. The wedding therefore speaks only
`playlist | masterFade | effect`, and a test pins that. (2) A stage with no
`autopilot:` block should arguably reset the deck transition rather than inherit
the last one, so no future show has to discover the latch the hard way.

**Verify.** New `marsin_engine/tests/special_events/wedding_show.test.js` —
**16/16** (a NEW sibling file, not an edit to `show_schema.test.js`, because
`_230` is editing that concurrently). It covers both scenes' byte-identity, the
ARM playlist contract offline (all five loadable, every pattern on disk AND in
`manifest.json`), the flash-before-swap ordering on **both** kiss variants, the
ceremony's dim + no-quick-effects, the cut, the rotation set, palette-immunity
majorities, and **all 34 distinct patterns compiling and rendering LIT on both
show models** (titanic 964 px, test_bench 166 px). Siblings green and untouched:
`show_schema` 27/27, `special_events_api` 28/28, `special_events_timeline_api`
3/3. **`special_events_autopilot_api` 0/13 is FOREIGN and in-flight (`_230`)** —
it fails identically with my engine down; diagnosis for whoever owns it: its
harness is `portBase 17230, portSpan 3`, and **:17230 is currently bound by
another agent's CaptainPad web serve** (it answers `<!DOCTYPE html>`, which is
the exact `waitForReady` error). Offline walk-through on a throwaway engine
(`--dest 192.0.2.x`, scratch `MARSIN_STATE_DIR`): every authored crossfade
duration is visible in its stage's playlist arrival time (3.0 / 4.0 / 5.0 / 4.0 s),
`409 NO_EVENT_ARMED`, `409 STAGE_NOT_ARMED`, `400 CHOICE_REQUIRED`,
`400 CHOICE_NOT_FOUND` all correct, and **FINISH restored the exact pre-show
playlist AND entry id AND master in 17 ms**; a second pass did `KISS → GLOW` +
ABORT. Screenshots on the fresh `:7167` dist (console-muted, `:69xx` requests
aborted at the interceptor) in `~/tmp/fix_231/`:
`events_picker_wedding_card`, `events_wedding_armed_column`,
`events_wedding_ceremony_kiss_armed` (shows `_230`'s autopilot card carrying MY
authored 2m / crossfade 5s), `events_wedding_celebration_quick_effects`,
`events_wedding_finished`.

**Isolation/residue.** Nothing bound, started or killed on 6966-6972 / UDP 5568;
the operator's stack and the ARMED bench mirror were never contacted at all, not
even a GET. Engines on **17231** then **17234** (moved off 17231 once `_230`'s
harness range 17230-17232 was discovered), `--dest 192.0.2.x`, state redirected
to scratch — **no tracked file under `marsin_engine/states/` was written.** Zero
edits to the runner, the schema, the routes, the tab, or `pattern_manifest.cjs`.
`CaptainPad/dist` was rebuilt (gitignored). No git ops.

**Open for the operator (all one-line YAML edits):** show id/name
(`wedding_program` / "Wedding"); the KISS button words and whether it should be
one button instead of two (instructions are in the YAML); stage words; the

## _236 — perf-exit hang fixed + persisted boot-mode toggle — 2026-08-15

Two operator orders. **(1)** "when going from perform mode to the edit mode, now
the 'restore pre-show' or the 'Keep live state' isn't making progress anymore."
**(2)** "in the config, add a new config toggle to go straight to edit mode or
performance mode, and make sure that's stored as part of the state persisted."
Report: `.agent/reports/202608/20260815_236_exit_hang_fix_boot_toggle.md`.
`docs/56` amended in two places (boot toggle under D1, the loudness rule under D8).

**The hang was ENTIRELY pad-side, and it was two bugs wearing one symptom.**
Reproduced offline (isolated auth engine `:17236`, `--dest 192.0.2.x`, fixture
secrets; fresh dist on `:7170` with the served bundle hash verified against the
export). The engine was never at fault — raw owner-passcode exits answered
**200 in 95 ms / 121 ms** and the whole `_228` suite is green. **(a)** The sheet
computed `choicesDisabled = pending || (passcodeRequired && passcode.length === 0)`,
so on the operator's `authRequired:true` engine BOTH exits rendered at 0.45
opacity with `aria-disabled`, swallowed the tap, fired no request, and printed
**no reason anywhere** — a mute client-side guess at a gate the ENGINE owns.
**(b)** Every refusal outside the four `EXIT_*` codes went to `Alert.alert`,
which react-native-web 0.21.2 implements as `class Alert { static alert() {} }`
— an empty stub — so `400 PERFORMANCE_MODE_NOT_ACTIVE` (second pad exits first),
`423 TOUCH_CONTROL_LEASE_HELD` (Live Touch armed; `/performance-mode` is NOT in
`TOUCH_CONTROL_EMERGENCY_PATHS`), `409 SPECIAL_EVENT`, a `500` snapshot failure
and the client's own 8 s timeout ALL left the sheet open, mute. Fixed: the
choices disable only while a request is in flight (an empty submit earns the
engine's `401 EXIT_AUTH_REQUIRED` in the error box — free, since
`verifyPrincipalPasscode` returns on a missing header BEFORE `verifyPassphrase`,
so mashing cannot 429 anyone mid-show), a standing hint sits under the field, and
`performanceExitFailureMessage()` ALWAYS returns a sentence (named guidance per
code; unrecognised codes echo the enum only, `/^[A-Z][A-Z0-9_]{0,63}$/`, never a
raw engine body). It renders in the SHEET, not a toast — the sheet persists.
**Ruled out with evidence:** the operator's pad is NOT stale (their `:6967` Metro
bundle carries `EXIT_KEEP_SAVE_OWNER_ONLY` / `EDIT_PRINCIPAL_READONLY` /
`editPrincipal`); the exit route, the W4 backlog skip, the `_emit` dedup fix and
CORS preflight all verified fine.

**Boot mode** = `settings_state.yaml → bootMode` (same file + same atomic write
as `autoSave`, extends `POST /settings`, no new route, broadcast on
`engineSettings`). CONFIG → ENGINE SETTINGS → **BOOT MODE**. **Semantics chosen:
booting into EDIT lifts the SHOW LOCK, never the AUTH GATE** — `editSession
.principal` still starts null, so `principalMaySave()` is false and the engine
persists NOTHING until someone asserts a principal via `POST /edit-session`
(the pad already renders `NO EDIT SESSION — NOT SAVING` for exactly that state).
Editable rig, frozen disk — the only reading consistent with docs/56's
engine-side gate never opening by itself. Default `'performance'`, and every
unreadable/absent/typo value coerces there (a gate must never open because a
YAML was junk). An interrupted show still wins over the toggle. No pre-show
snapshot on an edit boot. `400 INVALID_BOOT_MODE` on an unknown value (no
coercion at the route), optional on the wire, and it inherits `/settings`'s
`409 PERFORMANCE_MODE` + `403 EDIT_PRINCIPAL_READONLY` gates.

**Suites.** Engine `npm test` **3451 / 3444 pass / 7 fail** — the failing list is
the stated baseline family and NOTHING else: 5× `dev_test_bench`
(`all_models_load_lint`) + the 2 Baby-playlist cross-scene parity findings from
the concurrent curation wave. NEW `tests/security/boot_mode_toggle.test.js`
**9/9**; `settings_state` 8/8 (+4 pins); `principal_scoped_persistence` **9/9**
unchanged; `captainpad_auth_api` 4/4, `special_events_timeline_api` 3/3,
`live_touch_timeline_priority_api` 3/3, `performance_mode` 11/11,
`autosave_gating` 7/7, `state_corrupt_load` 6/6, `http_malformed_sweep` 36/36.
CaptainPad vitest **80 files / 1584 pass / 6 skip / 0 fail — failing list EMPTY**;
`tsc` clean for this wave (only `_235`'s in-flight `pixel_view_logic` errors
remain); `eslint` **0 errors**.

**Browser regression.** New re-runnable `simulation/agent_tools/exit_sheet_regression.cjs`
ASSERTS as well as captures (aborts stray `:69xx` so every frame provably comes
from the isolated engine) — **17/17 checks pass**: R1 empty passcode is tappable
+ loudly refused, R2 wrong passcode, R3 a non-family refusal is VISIBLE, R4 KEEP
resolves, R5 RESTORE resolves, R6 the BOOT MODE toggle persists in both
positions. Screenshots in `~/tmp/fix_236/` (`r1a`…`r6b`, plus the pre-fix
`repro_nopass_1_sheet.png` showing the dead greyed buttons).

**Isolation/residue.** Nothing bound, started or killed on 6966-6972 / UDP 5568.
The operator's engine was read with GETs ONLY (`/performance-mode`, `/status`),
and their `:6967` Metro bundle fetched read-only once to rule out staleness — no
POST, no passcode, no mode toggle. Engines on 17236 / 17237 / 17238 with scratch
state + playlist dirs, `--dest 192.0.2.x`. Fixture passcodes are obvious
placeholders in `~/tmp` (gitignored) and the suites' own scratch YAML — no
credential material in the repo. `CaptainPad/dist` rebuilt (gitignored). No git ops.

**RESTART REQUIRED — both halves.** Part 1 is pad-side: the operator's pad is on
the `:6967` Metro dev server, so a hard reload (Metro restart if it serves stale,
per the standing note about this box) is what makes it live. Part 2 changes
engine code, so **the engine must be restarted** before the toggle exists at all
— and by design the setting then takes effect on the boot AFTER the one where it
is set.

**Follow-up worth filing.** `Alert.alert` survives in a handful of CaptainPad
surfaces and is a silent no-op on every web build. `utils/op_dialog.ts` is the
replacement (2026-08-15 ruling) and a concurrent agent has begun the migration; a
sweep that finishes it plus a lint rule banning the raw import would close this
CLASS of bug instead of this instance.

## _237 — CaptainPad alerts become in-app UI (one notice/dialog system) — 2026-08-15

Report: `.agent/reports/202608/20260815_237_in_app_alert_system.md`.
**Client-only — no engine change was needed or made.**

**Operator ruling**, filed with a screenshot of a raw Chrome dialog
(`localhost:6967 says / Switch failed / special event "baby_reveal" is running
and owns the deck …`): *"do a deep analysis of alerts and make sure they are
not like this regular HTML shit, and is handled properly as part of the app UI
itself to be compatible with ipad too"*.

**Two bugs, not one.** react-native-web 0.21.2 ships Alert as a literal no-op
(`class Alert { static alert() {} }`), so **81 `Alert.alert` sites were SILENT
on the web build** — engine refuses, panel rolls back, podium operator sees the
UI snap back with no message. The 2026-07 patch for that (`utils/op_alert.ts`)
bought loudness with `window.alert`: unthemed, origin-stamped, ignores all five
themes, and **blocks the JS thread** so engine WS frames queue behind it — 16
sites, and the one in the screenshot. Neither could carry a button (RN-web
drops Alert callbacks), which is why `ConfirmSheet` already existed. **Worst
find: the BABY REVEAL fire confirmation in `timeline.tsx` was the only alert
with buttons, so on the podium it rendered nothing and the cue never fired — a
dead safety gate on a ceremonial cue.**

**Inventory: 97 operator-facing sites, 97 converted, 0 left, 0 HANDOFF.**
(a) error/refusal 95 · (b) destructive confirm 1 · (c) info 1 · (d) text prompt
**0** — nothing used `window.prompt`/`Alert.prompt`, text entry already goes
through in-app modals, so **no prompt primitive was built**. `_236` owned the
passcode/exit sheets at inventory time; none held a real call site, and a
re-audit after `_236` landed found **zero** raw alert surfaces anywhere.
`utils/op_alert.ts` **deleted**. `ConfirmSheet` + its 9 consumers left alone —
it is the DECLARATIVE confirm; the new `opConfirm` is its imperative twin, and
the two are drawn identically on purpose.

**System** reuses the `takeover_passcode` idiom exactly — pure-TS module-level
broker + ONE host outside `<Tabs>`: `utils/op_dialog.ts`
(`opError`/`opWarn`/`opInfo` → non-blocking themed TOAST; `opDialog` →
`Promise<actionId|null>`; `opConfirm` → `Promise<boolean>`, so a call site reads
`if (await opConfirm({...}))`), `styles/op_tone.ts`,
`components/op_dialog_host.tsx` + `ui/op_toast_stack.tsx` +
`ui/op_dialog_sheet.tsx`, `utils/engine_refusal.ts`. The ~90 "engine rejected X,
we reverted" notices are **toasts** — on a live show the operator must know but
must never be stopped mid-cue. docs/54 canon reused verbatim: dialog is
`globalStyles.panel` (row 19, "a modal IS a panel"), same backdrop tint, 44pt +
8pt hitSlop, `accentFill(C.error)` danger ink; toasts bottom-right `zIndex
1300` (the top band is already a four-way banner contest) with
`pointerEvents="box-none"` so taps reach the faders. **Three tones, zero new
palette keys.**

**A real contrast bug the new tests caught.** The first design filled the toast
with `errorContainer`; `op_tone.test.ts` measured **gruvbox `error` at 3.23:1
on its own wash**, and only 3.82:1 even untinted — because the token contract
pins **`warning`** as AA text on every surface but has **never pinned
`error`**. Resolved by making the accent a NON-TEXT carrier (icon + 3px bar,
3:1) with `C.text` as title ink; tone still reads via icon, bar, border and a
spoken `accessibilityLabel`. Pinned by a test. **The `error`-not-AA gap in the
shared token layer is left for its owner — recorded, not fixed.**

**The screenshot's case** now routes through `reportSwitchFailure()`: the
engine's `409 SPECIAL_EVENT` is a navigation instruction, not a status message,
so it gets a modal that stays put with **`OPEN EVENTS`** →
`router.push('/special_events')`. The engine sentence passes through
**verbatim** (it already names the show); `engine_refusal.ts` **throws** if the
engine ever sends that code with no reason rather than inventing one.

**Two guards.** (1) eslint `no-restricted-imports` bans the `Alert` named
export from `react-native`, error-level, message pointing at `op_dialog.ts` —
proven by planting a probe file. (2) `components/no_raw_alerts.test.ts` scans
source for what lint cannot see: `window.alert/confirm/prompt`, bare
`alert('x')`, namespace access, re-imports of the retired `op_alert`; strips
comments first and self-tests that the scanner actually walks the tree.

**Verify.** `tsc --noEmit` **clean**; `expo lint` **0 errors** (14 pre-existing
warnings, none new); `vitest` **80 files / 1588 pass / 6 skip / 0 fail —
failing list EMPTY** vs `_236`'s 80/1584/6/0 baseline (+4 are late additions to
`op_tone.test.ts`). New: `op_dialog.test.ts` 22, `op_tone.test.ts` 13,
`engine_refusal.test.ts` 7, `no_raw_alerts.test.ts` 8. Screenshots in
`~/tmp/fix_237/` on a **private snapshot** of the fresh dist
(`entry-554e0287…`) served on `:7171` — the shared `CaptainPad/dist` was being
rebuilt by a concurrent agent mid-run, so it was copied out of the way:
`02_409_refusal_dialog` (the operator's exact scenario, themed, with OPEN
EVENTS), `03_409_dialog_ipad_narrow` (834×1112), `05_toast_error` (fully real
refusal, non-blocking), `07_toast_ipad_narrow`, `06_destructive_confirm`,
`01_playlist_loaded`. `baby_reveal` is **not in this tree** (only
`wedding_program` loads on `test_bench`) so captures name the wedding show —
same engine template byte for byte. `opConfirm`'s destructive path has no
screenshot: its one call site needs a `c_baby_reveal_*` cue, which no bench plan
carries; covered by unit tests.

**Isolation/residue.** Nothing bound/started/killed on 6966-6972 / UDP 5568;
the harness **aborts every request to those ports at the interceptor** (it
blocked one `:6969` pixel-map fetch). One read-only `GET /status` afterwards to
confirm the live stack was still up. `:17237` and `:7171` shut down.
**Residue:** my FIRST bench run passed `MARSIN_STATE_DIR` as an MSYS path
(`$HOME/tmp/…`), which Node on Windows ignores, so it wrote tracked
`marsin_engine/states/test_bench/{deck,globals}_state.yaml` + a stray
`.mixer_state.yaml.*.tmp` before I caught it; later runs used a Windows path and
the redirect took. `states/titanic/*` changes are **foreign** — I never ran that
model. **Lesson: `MARSIN_STATE_DIR` must be a Windows-style path when launching
from Git Bash, or the redirect silently does nothing.** `CaptainPad/dist`
rebuilt (gitignored). No git ops.

**Open:** `_236` independently converged on the same module/file names — verified
on disk there is exactly ONE `op_dialog.ts` and ONE host, mounted once, and the
shipped module is the superset. The engine has **no** `baby_reveal` special-event
show in this tree though `config.yaml` still carries its palettes and the
operator's screenshot shows one running — worth confirming it does not live only
on the show server (see `_238`). `opInfo` has no call site yet (three lines,
cheaper to complete the triad than retrofit it).

## _239 — per-key vis caps (PIXELS at full rate) + the FRONT / TE SIGN fit — 2026-08-15

free number. Every in-code reference says `_239`.

**Order 1 — `_225`'s open item.** The Deck PIXELS window printed
`100/964 COLOUR SAMPLES`: `vis.maxPixels: 100` capped EVERY `/ws/viz` key,
because every consumer used to be a `<PixelStrip>` (one RN `<View>` per sample
per channel). `_225` added a consumer with the opposite cost model — a canvas,
whose cost is per pixel DRAWN and whose fidelity IS the sample count.

**The cap is now PER KEY** (`marsin_engine/lib/vis_budget.js`, new, pure,
23 tests). `vis.maxPixels` stays the default that every per-CHANNEL key takes;
`vis.keyMaxPixels: {rig: full, preDimmer: full}` raises only the whole-rig
composites. `full` = model verbatim. **Validation is loud**: unknown `vis.*`
field, unknown/mis-cased key name, non-integer or non-positive budget, or a
per-CHANNEL key named in `keyMaxPixels` all THROW at boot naming the valid set
— a silently-ignored `maxPixel: 900` typo is exactly the failure that leaves
the operator staring at a window that never sharpened. One index table +
scratch buffer per DISTINCT budget (rig+preDimmer share; 8 channels share);
full-rate returns the buffer itself, no copy. Frame gained `pixelCounts`
(per key) + `modelPixelCount`; `pixelCount` keeps its old meaning for old
clients.

**This REQUIRED a strip fix, not optionally.** `preDimmer` also feeds the deck's
LIVE OUTPUT strip and the mixer master strip, and `PixelStrip` drew **the first
N samples**. Handed 964 it would have drawn model pixels 0…255 — the bow of the
ship across a bar that reads as the whole rig. Silent, plausible, wrong. The
strip now declares its OWN budget and strides ACROSS the buffer with the
engine's own rule (`components/ui/pixel_strip_logic.ts`, 11 tests).
`STRIP_MAX_SEGMENTS = 100` is exactly what strips have drawn since the cap
existed, so **strip render cost changes by zero**.

**Measured — full rate costs the canvas NOTHING.** 720 glyphs / 1441 fill calls,
draw **1.8–2.6 ms median** (p95 3.3–3.5; worst single frame 8.6 ms with the
engine suite hammering the same CPU) vs `_225`'s 100-sample baseline of
1.1–7.1 ms / median 2–4 ms. The glyph count never changed, which IS the argument
for the split. **WS payload: 3,449 → 17,273 B/frame at 4.92 Hz = 136 → 680
kbit/s, delta +544 kbit/s** (~933 kbit/s with all 8 channels open). Under 1 % of
even a poor 2.4 GHz link on one socket the app already holds — reported, not
silently reduced; `keyMaxPixels: {rig: 240}` is one documented line away.

**Order 2 — the operator, mid-pass:** *"fix these views please the other 2 are
perfect. TE Signs and FRONT need some adjustment and proper fitting"*.

**It was not a fitting constant — `_225` was drawing the panels ON TOP OF EACH
OTHER.** `_225` recorded "the shipped Titanic views are single-panel". They are
not: `front` = left(198) + right(198), `te_sign` = sign_1(74) + sign_2(74) —
and every panel's coordinates fill the sim's WHOLE 900×520 design rect, because
the exporter lays each panel out against the full canvas and expects the
consumer to give each its own sub-rect. `flattenView` merged them, so FRONT drew
the ship's left half superimposed on its right and TE SIGN drew sign 2 on sign 1.
**The two views he called perfect are the two single-panel ones** — that was the
tell. The canonical consumer already had the answer and `_225` never read it:
`docs/ui/touch_control_pixel_views.js` → `panelSubRects` + `panelTransform` +
`reprojectView`.

**`layoutView()`** — weighted strips separated by `design.panelGap` (both now
REQUIRED by the parser, fail loud), each letterboxing the view's COMMON BOX,
then the composite fitted to `FIT_FILL = 0.92` and centred. Two deliberate
departures from the sim's consumer, both measured, neither naming a view:
(a) the **union box** rather than the full design rect — the design rect's empty
margin is charged twice, once per panel, which is why te_sign's signs sat small
with a chasm between them (618×463: scale **0.457 → 0.837**, 1.8× larger,
nothing moved relative to anything else); (b) panels arranged along whichever
**axis measures bigger** — the Live Touch pad is always wide, a deck window is
any shape (front at 618×463: columns 0.433 vs rows **0.494**; at 283×433:
0.195 vs **0.401**; at 900×500 columns wins again at **0.634**). `view.framing`
(his zoom/pan of the LT PAD, in that surface's pixels) still deliberately not
applied. **No regression on the two perfect views** — single-panel, same path,
identical measurements (top_down 0.804, strands 0.980) and pixel-identical in
the before/after sheet.

**Caught by the capture log, not the eye:** the honesty caption read `drawRef`
during render while the flatten happens in an effect, so after every view switch
it showed the PREVIOUS view's pixel count (`720 PX` while drawing FRONT's 396).
Now state. The caption also prints the arithmetic on BOTH paths now —
`720 PX · 964/964 COLOUR SAMPLES · FULL RATE`, not a bare "FULL-RATE COLOUR";
a claim with its numbers attached is checkable.

**Verification.** Engine 3451 tests / 12 fail; baseline 3415 / 10 fail — same 10
(`all_models_load_lint` ×5, `deck_entry_autocapture` ×4, `baby_color_contract`),
plus 2 NEW in `special_events/{show_schema,wedding_show}` failing on
`"effectId 'blastWhite' is not allowed as a QUICK EFFECT"` — a concurrent
session's schema work, files I never opened. CaptainPad 80 files / **1588 pass /
0 fail** (baseline 75 / 1498 / 0); my two files 65/65. tsc clean, eslint clean on
all six touched files. **My failing list is EMPTY on both suites.**

**Isolation/residue.** Offline engine on **:17235**, `--dest 192.0.2.x`
(TEST-NET-1), isolated `MARSIN_{CONFIG_FILE,STATE_DIR,PLAYLISTS_DIR,TIMELINE_DIR}`
under `~/tmp/fix_239` — boot log names only the black hole, no Art-Net line,
`outputRouting.controllers: []`. Both scratch services shut down; `:6968` verified
still up afterwards. The only live-stack traffic was read-only GETs of the sim's
pixel-map artifact on `:6969`. `marsin_engine/states/*` churn is the engine test
suite's expected residue (plus foreign changes). Screenshots in `~/tmp/fix_239/`
(9 PNGs) off a fresh dist on **:7169** with the served bundle hash verified
against the export before every shoot (`_232`'s trap). No git ops.

**Live reload: the ENGINE MUST BE RESTARTED.** `vis.keyMaxPixels` is read once at
boot; the operator's running `:6968` is still shipping 100 samples/key and the
window will keep printing `100/964` against it until he restarts. Nothing
degrades meanwhile — the capped path is intact, tested and honest. CaptainPad
needs a fresh web build; the sim is untouched.

**Open:** the composites cost 544 kbit/s whether or not PIXELS is open (it is
default-closed) — a demand-driven `/ws/viz` subscription would spend it only when
someone is looking, but that is a protocol change, not a budget one, and was not

## _244 — FOLLOW NOTE colour mode + method autopilot + LIVE RETUNE (DESIGN) — 2026-08-15

Doc: `docs/59_follow_note_color_autopilot.md` · Report:
`.agent/reports/202608/20260815_244_follow_note_design.md`. Design only

transport/sel) and `_242` (dial + presets, read from the working tree).
Awaits an Opus implementer.

Operator orders: (1) "use the note as the main color … follow note, and have
the method cycling smoothly on a timer" — note drives base hue, scheme
generators cycle on an autopilot timer with smooth fades. (2) follow-up:
live retune — "changing of the parameters for those existing ones too
doesn't need a full stop and start again" (crossfade + TURNS + follow-note).

**The four calls.** (1) LOOP: engine-side, a `mode:'followNote'` of the ONE
colour daemon (`lib/color_autopilot.js`) — the engine ALREADY has the note
(`audioNote`/`audioNoteHue` in the CPC at 10 Hz via the companion's
DerivedSignals, hold-through-silence test-pinned; `audio_reactive_profile`
is the precedent consumer). Note→hue = `audioNoteHue` (the companion's
operator-tunable noteColors wheel), NOT a second Scriabin table; W9 offers a
Scriabin PRESET for that wheel. Mutual exclusion with TURNS/crossfade by
construction — one daemon, one mode, one front door. Note listener =
`paramCenter.subscribe` + changed-value bail; method cycle = the existing
generation-guard timer. (2) GENERATORS: ported to new pure
`marsin_engine/lib/color_schemes.js`, parity pinned by a shared reference
table (9 ids × 3 base hues → exact HSV) in BOTH suites — the `_217` lerpHue
idiom. (3) SMOOTHNESS: method fades 3 s default (holds 10/30/60/120/300 s,
default 60 — own rows, not the `_224` seconds-scale transport); note changes
SLEW 400 ms default (Live Touch snaps; a two-slot 180° snap on the rig reads
as a fault), `noteFadeMs:0` = snap. One tween, latest-event-wins, always
ramps from `_currentParams`. `rotationKind` gains 'follow-note';
`manualWriteGate` unchanged; scheme tap while following = method override
via the daemon's front door; never silent auto-pause (`_211` §D).
(4) SILENCE: hold-last, visibly — companion holds the committed note, a dead
feed just stops the events (method cycle keeps breathing on the held hue),
card says "HOLDING LAST NOTE (audio silent)" off `audioSilence`. No wheel-
base fallback.

**LIVE RETUNE (the follow-up):** `ColorAutopilot.patchState(sparse)` +
`PATCH /deck/color-autopilot` (`_230` sparse-patch idiom). Load-bearing rule:
patch NEVER bumps `generation`, never cancels the tween — the restart lived
in the bump + cursor reset, not in the tick (which reads state fresh at fire
time). Holds re-arm phase-preserving off a new `_lastTickAtMs`; fades apply
from the next fade (stated in UI microcopy); ring restages adopt at next
transition fading from live params (`_224` one-tap restage becomes a
palettes-only PATCH — phase survives); `sel` retweens now; `active`/`mode`
refused (setState takeovers). Acceptance: fake-clock walk — 2 s→10 s retimed
crossfade never snaps, countdown continuity provable.

door/broadcast/timeline → W5 live retune → W6 client logic (incl.

Scriabin preset. Screenshot matrix + test plan in docs/59 §9.

## _242 — COLORS hue DIAL (the jump killed) + preset palettes with generated icons/names + baby-palette audit — 2026-08-15

Report: `.agent/reports/202608/20260815_242_hue_dial_palette_presets.md`.
Branch `feat/bm_readiness` (the brief's `feat/bm_audio_tuning` was a stale
snapshot — same correction `_240` recorded). **ENGINE RESTART REQUIRED** —
the `/color-pairs` validator and its state-file shape moved together.

**1. THE DIAL (order 1: "when i click, it has an unpleasant jump ... make it a
dial ... I can consistently control by touch").** The jump was structural, not a
tuning problem: `onPanResponderGrant` ran `hueFromPoint(touch)` straight into
`onPick`, so the ring was an ABSOLUTE control and there was NO gesture that
touched it without writing it. A fingertip is ~40 pt on a 190 pt wheel, so
"thumb on the handle" could never mean "change nothing", and reaching for the
far side threw the hue half a revolution in one frame. Replaced with the
jog-wheel model: touch-down ANCHORS, the hue follows the ACCUMULATED angular
delta geared by `DIAL_GAIN = 0.5` (one physical revolution = half a hue
revolution — twice the resolution the absolute ring could offer). A tap moves
nothing BY CONSTRUCTION (zero delta), the grab point is irrelevant, the 0/360
seam is an ordinary step because every sample is a SHORT-ARC delta from the
previous sample, and multi-lap drags accumulate. HUB RULE: a sample inside
`DIAL_DEAD_RADIUS_PX` (14) has no angle, sets `lastAngle = null`, and a change
needs TWO consecutive samples that both have one — so no jump can come out of
the hub and a swipe THROUGH the centre freezes (a stroke across the middle is a
line, not a turn). `onDragStart`/`onDragEnd` now fire only for a drag that
MOVED, so a tap no longer puts a frame on the wire. New `dialValue` prop: while
a scheme is latched the dial steers the LATCH'S BASE, not `hues[armed]` — the
two diverge the moment A points at a ring slot other than T1, and that is
exactly where the jump would have come back. All maths pure in
`colors_window_logic` (`wrap01`/`turnDelta`/`beginDial`/`dialSample`/`dialHue`/
`dialTicks`). KEPT VERBATIM: `_211` gesture armor (capture-phase responder +
termination refusal + web `touchAction:'none'`), S=V=1 pin, throttled atomic
`/param-center` write, `_224` `{scheme, base}` latch re-theme, A/B `GRAB_PX`
targeting — which now only ARMS. Chrome is a real docs/54 rotary: knurled hub,
36-mark tick scale (`dialTicks`, asserted not eyeballed), pointer on the value,
hub rim + pointer light while gripped.

**2+4. PRESET PALETTES (orders 2+4).** Widened the EXISTING SAVE PAIR store
rather than adding a sibling — a pair IS the degenerate palette, and two
galleries would make "where did I save that" a question with two answers.
`c1`/`c2` stay REQUIRED and unchanged, which IS the migration (a v1 file's rows
are already valid v2 rows); `schemaVersion: 2` adds optional `name`,
`ring`+`sel`, `scheme`+`base`. Grouping is all-or-nothing per pair and validated
LOUDLY on both sides (`presetExtras` client / `validateColorPreset` engine):
ring⇔sel, scheme⇔base, scheme⇒ring, `sel[0] !== sel[1]`, known scheme id, ring
≤ 5. Ring stored ALONGSIDE the scheme, never derived — the ring is what the
operator saw (they may have hand-edited a slot), the latch is how it
re-generates. ABSENCE is the ONE encoding of "unnamed" (empty/whitespace names
are never stored), so order 4's "accept an empty name" needs no second code
path. Failure modes: future `schemaVersion` → THROW (GET 500, shown standing in
the gallery); one malformed ROW in the hand-editable file → dropped with a warn,
gallery survives; a malformed row POSTed → 400, whole write refused. ICON is
`presetIconColours` + new shared `components/ui/preset_icon.tsx` — a disc of one
wedge per colour, clockwise from the top like the dial, drawn from data (no
asset, nothing to go stale), and the naming card and the gallery chip call the
SAME component with the SAME list so the preview IS the result. NAME comes from
a new `opPrompt` added in `op_dialog`'s own idiom: `OpDialogRequest` gains
`input`/`swatches`, `resolve` gains an optional value arg, `opDialog()` keeps
its exact signature (every existing call site untouched), and `''` vs `null` are
kept DISTINCT — `''` saves unnamed, `null` saves nothing, or CANCEL would be
indistinguishable from SAVE-with-no-name. A submit with no value THROWS (P0).
The gallery cap is checked BEFORE the name is asked for. Recall restores the
whole staged state (ring + sel + latch) or behaves exactly as before for a bare
pair. Duplicate identity is by COLOURS, not name.

**3. BABY PALETTES — AUDITED, NOTHING REMOVED, `config.yaml` UNTOUCHED.** All
three (`baby_reveal_duet`, `baby_pink`, `baby_blue`, `config.yaml:357-368`) are
live: each is referenced twice by `simulation/scenes/titanic/timeline/
playa_default.yaml` (cues `c_baby_reveal_pink` :234/:251/:263/:280 and
`c_baby_reveal_blue` :306/:323/:335/:352 — a `palette:` value plus a
single-entry `colorAutopilot.palettes`), and
`tests/timeline/baby_reveal_sequence.test.js:182-184` reads the REAL config and
pins all three present. NOT referenced by: any show YAML (the special-event
schema has no palette verb — `wedding_program.yaml:50`), the house
`colorAutopilot.palettes` rotation (`config.yaml:451-460`, nine ids, no baby),
any CaptainPad source, or the `baby_*` playlists (their notes say "no palette
binding"). **OPEN FOR THE OPERATOR:** the three are the FIRST THREE of 23 and
`/color-palettes` serves the list verbatim, so they head the SHOW PALETTE
gallery on every iPad for a cue used twice. If "clean up" meant *get them out of
my picker* rather than *delete them*, a `hidden: true` flag or a move to the
tail is a two-line change — flagged, not guessed at.

**Verification.** CaptainPad `tsc` clean; `expo lint` 0 errors and no warning on
any touched file; `vitest` 84 files / **1676 pass / 0 fail** (~45 new). Engine
`tests/effects/color_window_engine_api.test.js` **20/20** (was 14) on a scratch
