## _246 — CaptainPad derives its engine address from the host it was served from — 2026-08-15

Report: `.agent/reports/202608/20260815_246_api_base_derivation.md`. Operator hit
it live on an iPad: `config.yaml`'s `api_base: http://127.0.0.1:6968` was the
DEFAULT for every device, so a pad loaded the UI over the LAN and then asked
**itself** for every data call. The cure was hand-typing the address per device.
`touch_control.tsx` had already named this exact failure for its panel URL; the
engine address never learned it. **No engine restart** — client-side only.

**RESOLUTION, not a fallback** (header block says so): each step reads a
DIFFERENT named source, in a fixed order, and the module LOGS the winner — one
`console.info` for a derived address, one `console.warn` for the YAML last
resort. (1) AsyncStorage `API_BASE` — the operator's explicit override, always
wins, unchanged. (2) THE SERVING HOST: web → `window.location.hostname`; native →
`Constants.expoConfig?.hostUri`, else `expoGoConfig?.debuggerHost` (verified
against the installed `expo-constants@18.0.13` — `hostUri` is typed on
`expoConfig` and documented "only present during development using @expo/cli";
the deprecated `manifest`/`manifest2` path was deliberately NOT read). (3)
`config.yaml` — LAST RESORT, correct exactly on the engine host, in an
`expo export` prerender pass, or a bare test env. **Only the hostname is taken;
`http` and port 6968 are PINNED** — the serving port (`:6967`, `:7175`, Metro's
`:8081`) is never the engine's, and mirroring an `https` page scheme would derive
a dead address. IPv6 is bracketed on the way in and unwrapped on the way out. The
YAML contract still THROWS at import BEFORE resolution runs, so a broken config
can never be masked by a lucky page host (there is a test for that ordering).

**Leaf rule kept.** `expo-constants`, RN `Platform` and the YAML are PLATFORM
leaves — none imports from `utils/`, so the `api → engineEvents → engineBus → api`
ring the header guards against cannot form; the header now says this. **`api.ts`
was NOT touched** (three agents were in it) — the CONFIG tab imports the new
`getApiBaseSource` straight from the leaf. One shape change: `require('@/config.yaml')`
→ a static `import`, because Node's `require` inside vitest knows neither the `@`
alias nor `vi.mock`, which made the module **untestable**; the static form is the
repo idiom (`useMidiControl.ts`), `types/yaml.d.ts` already declares it, and the
`?.default || raw || {}` hardening is kept verbatim. A real `expo export` built
and prerendered clean on it.

**CONFIG copy fixed** — "RESET TO YAML" became **RESET TO DEFAULT**, and the card
now names the winning source live (`derived from this page's host` /
`derived from the Metro host` / `saved on this device` / `CaptainPad/config.yaml`)
plus a paragraph stating the precedence. `config.yaml`'s comment block says
LAST RESORT; **the value is unchanged** — still right for the case it now covers.

**Verification.** New `utils/api_base_resolution.test.ts`, **29 tests**, each a
real cold start (`vi.resetModules()` + per-case stubs of RN / expo-constants /
AsyncStorage / the YAML). Suite **85 files / 1706 pass / 0 fail**, failing list
EMPTY; `tsc` clean; `expo lint` 0 errors, 14 pre-existing warnings, none on a
touched file. **LIVE:** a fresh export served on **:7176** and loaded by headless
Chrome at the machine's LAN address `10.x.x.NNN` logged `[apiBase] engine address
derived from the served-host (platform=web): http://10.x.x.NNN:6968` and made
**28/28 engine requests to the LAN host, 0 to loopback**, first one
`/status`. Screenshots `~/tmp/fix_246/`: the Deck over the LAN with LIVE data
(`● CONNECTED`, `MODEL titanic`, live meters, running playlist) with nothing
typed into CONFIG, plus the new engine-address card. Operator ports 6966-6972,
:7175 and :6981 confirmed listening before and after — nothing bound or killed
there; `CaptainPad/dist/` NOT rebuilt. **Picked up automatically** by the :7175
mirror on its next rebuild and Expo Go on its next reload; a pad that already has
an override keeps it. *Residue note:* `expo export --output-dir "$HOME/…"` under
Git Bash writes to a stray `C:\c\Users\…` (Node reads the POSIX `$HOME` as a
drive-relative path); `_246`'s copy was moved out and deleted, **`_243`'s is
still there** and `C:\c` is harness-protected from removal.

### _245 addendum — post-landing "[object Object]" bundle-host fix — 2026-08-15

**My defect, caught live at gen-6 boot.** `detectLanHost()` returns
`{host, source}`; `main()` bound the whole OBJECT to `lanHost` and handed it to
`REACT_NATIVE_PACKAGER_HOSTNAME`, which Node stringified to `"[object Object]"`.
Metro's `@react-native/dev-middleware` InspectorProxy fed that to `new URL()` →
`TypeError: Invalid URL` → captainpad child exits → launcher (correctly) tears
the whole stack down at boot. Both "bundle host" log lines printed
`[object Object]` — the tell. Coordinator hot-fixed it at `launcher.js:1503-1510`
(`lanHostInfo` = object, `lanHost` = `.host` string, comment names the failure);
**kept as-is**.

**Why _245's own tests missed it:** they only exercised the helper's RETURN
VALUE. The bug was at the CALL SITE — correct helper, wrong unwrap. So the two
new regression tests pin the call site, not the function
(`launcher_supervision.test.js`, now **24/24**): (1) source-level — the env value
must be a bare identifier (never an inline `detectLanHost(...)`), that
identifier's declaration must contain `.host`, and EVERY `bundle host ${…}` log
must interpolate the same identifier so the log can't disagree with the env var;
same technique/justification as the existing "ORDER: cmdStop blackout before
force-kill" test. **Mutation-checked** — it fails on the buggy binding, passes on
the fixed one. (2) shape contract — `{host, source}` keys, `host` is a string
matching an IPv4/hostname shape (what `new URL()` needs), and
`String(info) === '[object Object]'` so the hazard is stated in the suite.

**Other consumers checked (coordinator ask):** exactly ONE production call site
(the fixed one); `lanIpv4Candidates` is internal to `detectLanHost`; both are
exported only for tests, which consume `.host` consistently. Nothing else in the
repo reads either. No further unwrapping to fix.

**Also fixed** (flagged by `_247`'s README review): the stale `openProfileUis`
header comment at `launcher.js` ~L966 claiming "prod (no captainpad process) →
sim → Companion" — false since `_245`; now says every profile opens all three,
with a note that a show server is unaffected (`--no-launch`, `boot_server.ps1`
opens its own tabs). **Numbering:** `_247` is right that TWO reports occupy
`_245` — mine (`…_245_launcher_prod_deploy_prep.md`) and a foreign
`…_245_deck_transition_debug_audit.md` from a concurrent session. Foreign file
LEFT ALONE; collision recorded in §8 of my report. This `_245` block refers to my
report only. `node --check` clean; no port 6966-6972 / UDP 5568 touched.

from the performance mode, I cannot see the config, it's hidden." Performance
mode is engine-owned and the flip is an engine route, and `docs/56` D1 (+`_228`)
makes an auth-enabled engine BOOT locked — so an unreachable engine leaves the
pad on the locked face forever, with CONFIG (engine-address card, TEST
CONNECTION, BOOT MODE) hidden by the very lock CONFIG would help you escape.
**No engine file changed; every gate is exactly where it was.**

**A — CONFIG in performance mode.** `captainpad_tab_policy.ts`:
`config.showInPerformance` → `true`, and STUDIO/MIDI/OSC flip **with** it. The
`_232` invariant ("a sub-view is exactly as reachable as its parent") is KEPT,
not relaxed — the sub-views cost no rail slot either way (reached through
CONFIG's cards), so flipping them together keeps the constraint real. Nothing is
loosened: the engine still 409s structural writes under the lock (`docs/56`
D2/D6) and `usePerfLock()` still greys. Show rail is now DECK · MIXER · LIVE
TOUCH · EVENTS · **CONFIG**. Line NOT crossed (new test): AUDIO / TIMELINE /
SCHEDULER / DIMMER RACK / 2D SIMULATOR stay frozen out. Overlay-level perf-hide
(deck PARAMETERS+AUTOPILOT, mixer pixel-view) untouched — those read
`usePerformanceMode().active`, not the tab policy.

**B — offline LOCAL VIEW override.** New module state in `usePerformanceMode.ts`
(`_connected` from the /ws/control bus, `_localOverride: boolean|null`) resolved
by one pure fn in `performance_mode_logic.ts`:
`resolveLocalViewOverride(engineActive, engineConnected, override)` — **a
connected bus ignores the override outright**, which IS the reconnect guarantee
in one line. `usePerformanceMode()` returns `PerformanceModeView`, a strict
SUPERSET of `PerformanceModeState`: `active` is now the EFFECTIVE face, plus new
`localOverride` / `engineOffline`. `_243`'s mixer contract unchanged in shape.
Dedupe guard moved from `_emit` onto the projected view so a disconnect/pick
fans out while a redundant re-seed still doesn't.

**The one-line unlock:** `usePerformanceModeReady()` was the real lock —
`!ready` reads as LOCKED in `_layout.tsx` + `performance_route_guard.tsx`, and a
bus drop sets `_resolved=false`. It now means "does this pad have a definite
answer": `_resolved || (!_connected && _localOverride !== null)`. Because of
that, **the tab policy, route guard, deck workspace, mixer overlay and
`usePerfLock()` needed ZERO edits** — smallest blast radius, which mattered with
`_243`/`_248` in the tree.

`setLocalPerformanceView(active)` **throws when connected** (codex P0 — with a
live engine the only legitimate flip is the gated POST; a silent local flip
would be a client-side lie about a shared lock). **No passcode offline, and it
weakens nothing:** the credential ring is engine-side so nothing is verifiable
offline, and D2/D3/D6 are enforced per request — with no connection there is no

documented as such: its callers (timeline/special-events takeover gates, MIDI
LED projector) shape requests TO the engine and must use engine truth; new
`getPerformanceModeView()` / `isPerformanceModeReady()` expose the projection.

**Chip (`PerformanceModeControl.tsx`):** `busy` no longer includes

chip.** Offline tap → local toggle, no sheet; label names the view you switch
TO (`LOCK` suppressed, `END GLOBAL` hidden — it POSTs); captions `ENGINE
OFFLINE` + amber `LOCAL VIEW`. All three sheets (`_236` exit, ENTER confirm,
privileged auth) are `visible={… && !engineOffline}` and an effect closes+clears
them on a drop. APC SOLO summon does the same local toggle offline. **Online:
byte-identical, passcode flow untouched.**

## _248 — FOLLOW NOTE colour mode + method autopilot + LIVE RETUNE (docs/59 W1-W9 SHIPPED) — 2026-08-15

Two operator orders, both landed. *"use the note as the main color … follow
note, and have the method cycling smoothly on a timer"* and *"the changing of
the parameters for those existing ones too doesn't need a full stop and start
again."* All nine W-items of `docs/59` (the `_244` design), W9 included.

**FOLLOW NOTE is a MODE of the ONE colour daemon, not a sibling.** `mode:
'palettes' | 'followNote'` on the existing wire; **absent ≡ palettes**, so every
config written before this is byte-unchanged AND byte-understood. Mutual
exclusion with TURNS / crossfade / palette-set is therefore **by construction** —
one daemon, one mode, one broadcast, one front door — not by a second active
flag every surface has to remember to check. The note loop lives INSIDE
`color_autopilot.js` as a `paramCenter.subscribe` on `audioNote`/`audioNoteHue`
(the companion already publishes both at 10 Hz and already holds the committed
pitch through silence), so it survives an iPad sleep and satisfies the deadman
rule. Method timer = the existing generation-guard model; hold and fade stay
ADDITIVE (asserted: hold 10 s + fade 2 s arms at `tick+2000+10000`).

**W1 — the port, and the float that would have made the parity table a lie.**
New `lib/color_schemes.js` carries the nine generators with **zero imports of
any kind** (asserted — the module is pure arithmetic, so "no CaptainPad import"
is strengthened to "no import"). FOLLOW NOTE needs the engine to re-derive the
ring on every committed note, and a precomputed client ring cannot express a hue
nobody has played yet. Parity is the `_217` `lerpHue` idiom: ONE literal of **9
ids × 3 base hues → the full five `{h,s,v}` triples, asserted EXACT (no epsilon)
in BOTH suites** — 27 assertions a side. My first draft "normalized" the base
hue with `((h%1)+1)%1`; that is **not the identity on an in-range hue** (0.1 →
0.10000000000000009), so it would have put the engine's ring a float off the
client's for exactly the hues that look safest. The engine now THROWS on a base
outside `[0,1]` — a boundary check, not a wrap, with its own test.

**W2 + the merge that would have 400'd every START.** Follow-note mode FORBIDS
every palettes-mode field (naming the offender); palettes mode CARRIES a
follow-note block inert, validated on the way in so a mode toggle cannot fail a
week later on a block stored broken. The route's old `{...state, ...body}` merge
**cannot survive a mode discriminator** — live state always carries `palettes`,
so a body saying `mode:'followNote'` merged into a both-modes config and got
refused. New `ColorAutopilot.mergeWire` scopes the carry-over to the TARGET
mode; the inert block rides along so a there-and-back toggle restores the
operator's tuning instead of erasing it (proved on the offline walk:
`methodHoldS: 30` survived palettes ← followNote ← palettes without being
re-sent).

**W5 — LIVE RETUNE. `patchState` NEVER bumps `generation` and NEVER cancels the
tween** — that is the whole mechanism, and it is safe because the reset was
never in the TICK (which reads state, ring and durations fresh at fire time), it
was in the bump and the cursor reset. `active`/`mode` refused by name (takeovers
stay on POST); a cross-mode field refused naming both; the CONT spin-loop rule
re-checked against the MERGED pair so a patch is not a side door into a config a
POST refuses. **One honest deviation from docs/59 §5.1, stated:** the design says
re-arm to `lastTickAtMs + newHold`, which is only phase-preserving when the fade
is zero — with a real fade the hold begins AFTER the fade lands, so measuring
from the tick would silently eat the fade out of the cycle and break the
additive contract. Both instants are recorded; the re-arm uses
`_holdStartedAtMs`. With a hard cut they coincide, so §5.3's stated identity
`nextSwapAtMs === lastTickAtMs + 10000` holds **exactly** and is tested as
written.

**FOUR REAL BUGS, all found by tests or the walk rather than by eye.**
(1) The first method advance **repeated the starting method** — the prime
applied `schemes[0]` but left the cursor at −1, so the first "advance" was a
three-second crossfade to itself. (2) The card's note letter was **a whole
method hold stale**: measured on the walk, the rig had moved to G while the card
still said E, because nothing re-broadcast between advances (60 s by default).
New `onNoteChange` hook, fired on a COMMITTED change only — the hop-rate
republishes never reach it. (3) **A WHITE-SCREEN:** loading the deck while
follow-note ran crashed the whole screen — the focus seed put the mode-scoped
payload straight into state, `palettes` became `undefined`, and
`ColorAutopilotPanel` read `.length` off it. Fixed at both doors, and that panel
is now mode-aware: it SAYS "FOLLOW NOTE is driving the colours … its controls
are in the COLORS window" instead of drawing an empty chip row as though the
operator had chosen nothing.

(4) A `mode`-LESS palettes POST — the shape every pre-existing caller uses (the
timeline cue path, older builds, scripts) — inherited the LIVE mode, so **once
FOLLOW NOTE had been used once, every one of them came back 400**;
`color_window_engine_api` went 20/20 → 10/20 the moment the persisted block was
left in follow-note mode, which is exactly the state the operator's engine is in
after trying the feature. New `inferMode`: the mode comes from the body's OWN
fields, and a body carrying BOTH is refused by name rather than guessed.

**W6/W7 — client + UI.** `rotationKind` gains `'follow-note'` from the broadcast
MODE, never sniffed from palette shapes (a follow-note config HAS no palettes);
`schemeTapOutcome` gains `method-override` (the `_224` restage idiom on the
method axis — the tap PATCHes `followNote.method` through the daemon's own front
door and the rig crossfades over the cycle's own `methodFadeS`, indistinguishable
from a timer-driven advance because that is what it is); `manualWriteGate`
UNCHANGED, its kind-agnostic sentence still true. **`colorAutopilotWritable`
learns the mode** — the palettes-only test would have called every follow-note
config un-toggleable and quietly dropped the colour half of the APC clip_stop
press. Third transport card: state line, live ring with A/B arm-then-tap (stored
as INDICES, so the pick survives every re-theme the music causes), method chips
with three distinct states (off / in the cycle / **on the rig now**), METHOD HOLD
`[CONT,10,30,60,120,300]` default 60 and METHOD FADE `[1.5,3,6,10]` default 3 in
their OWN rows — a MOOD cadence, deliberately not the `_224` seconds-scale PAIR
transport, or 1 s method thrash would be one tap away. **Live-retune microcopy on
all three cards** ("HOLD applies now · FADE from the next fade — no stop and
start"), worded from the same table the patch builder obeys, because live retune
is otherwise invisibly partial. **Zero timers added** — grep-clean for
`setInterval`/rAF; the countdown is the existing self-ticking `<SwapCountdown>`.

**W9 SCRIABIN INCLUDED** — a one-tap preset for the companion's `noteColors`
wheel, sent as a single 12-field patch through the ORDINARY `setDerivedConfig`
door (validated, persisted, broadcast like a hand turn of the slider; no
preset-shaped side channel). HUE ONLY, stated: Scriabin varies S/V but this
wheel is hue-only by design and `generateScheme` takes a bare hue, so the S/V
could not ride through the generators anyway. The static UI bundle's copy is
pinned byte-for-byte against the engine constant by test.

**Verification.** Engine: `color_schemes` 39/39, `color_autopilot_follow_note`
54/54, `color_autopilot` 48/48, `color_window_engine_api` 20/20,
`note_color_scriabin` 7/7; full suite with MY failing list EMPTY (a mid-wave run
showed 7 foreign failures in `timeline_zoom_e2e`, `all_models_load_lint` ×5 and
`ambient_playlist_campaign` — concurrent agents' files, untouched by me).
CaptainPad **89 files / 1830 pass / 0 fail / 6 skip** (`colors_window_logic`
125 → 228); `tsc` + `expo lint` clean on every file I touched (`tsc` errors
remain in `_243`'s brand-new `pixel_paint_target_*`). **Offline walk 29/29** on
a real engine at **:17248, `--dest 192.0.2.x`**, note injected via
`POST /param-center` (the HIL trick — mic never opened, live companion never
contacted): rig landed on `complement@0.25` = `c1.h 0.25 / c2.h
0.41666666666666663` at `s=0.95`; **20 republishes of the same note wrote
nothing**; **follow-note HOLD 10→30 s mid-hold wrote no colour and moved the
countdown by exactly 20000 ms**; **crossfade HOLD 2→10 s wrote no colour and
moved it by exactly 8000 ms**; every refusal 400'd with its naming sentence.
Seven inspected screenshots in `~/tmp/fix_248/` from a fresh :7177 dist (bundle
hash verified against the export) against the offline engine — the live
6966-6972 stack and :6981 Metro got READ-ONLY GETs only. The two-frame retune
shot is the point of the new tool
(`simulation/agent_tools/colors_follow_note_capture.cjs`): FADE 8 s → 3 s

**GATES: THE ENGINE MUST RESTART** (daemon + generator module + routes moved

## _253 — a CANCELLED deck transition was killing the engine mid-show — 2026-08-15

`_248`'s full run left 18 special-events reds on an unhandled rejection
`Deck transition … was cancelled`, reproducing in isolation. **They were not 18
assertion failures — they were ONE ENGINE PROCESS DYING** and 18 later requests
hitting `ECONNREFUSED`. **Real runtime defect, show-critical**, not a harness
artefact: `engine.js`'s `unhandledRejection` handler prints `⛔ ENGINE FATAL` and
`exit(1)`, so *ABORT/FINISH a Baby Reveal or the wedding while a deck crossfade
is animating → the whole rig goes down.*

**Root cause, three facts colliding.** (1) A cancelled deck swap REJECTS —
`loadPlaylistEntryWithTransition`'s `onCancel` does `rejectDone(err)` with
`err.code='ECANCELED'`, and cancellation is *routine and deliberate*: PANIC, a
look/snapshot morph (`morphToLook` → `mixer.cancelDeckPatternSwap()`), a newer
swap, and **every special-event FINISH/ABORT restore** (`_endRun` →
`recallSnapshotFade`). (2) `timelineLoadPlaylistOnDeck` — **synchronous at HEAD,
with the explicit comment "the returned `done` promise is intentionally NOT
awaited"** — was rewritten in the (uncommitted) working tree as `async` with
`await activeDeckSwapDone` + `await result.done` so the Timeline could serialize
behind an active swap. Right for the Timeline; it changed the failure surface for
EVERY caller. (3) Two callers are FIRE-AND-FORGET and lost their error handling
in that rewrite: `SpecialEventsService._applyAction` case `'playlist'` (a show
may never wait out a fade, so it cannot await → the promise has no caller to
reject onto) and the panel-deadman `revertToAutomaticShow`, whose `step()` helper
is a **synchronous** try/catch that can no longer see the callee's documented
`'playlist not found'` throws. `done` itself always had a baseline `.catch`, so
`done` was never the unhandled promise — **the async function's own promise
was**. Net: a routine supersession became a fatal exit, and so did any genuine
deck-load failure on those two paths. `git log -S` finds nothing — `lib/special_events/`
is untracked and the async rewrite is uncommitted, so this is all working-tree work.

**Fix — 3 hunks in `lib/api_server.js`, 1 in `special_events_service.js`, plus
the contract test.** (A) New `settleDeckTransition(promise)` helper next to
`deckSwapInFlightReason`: `catch (error) { if (!error || error.code !==
'ECANCELED') throw error; }`, and both of `timelineLoadPlaylistOnDeck`'s awaits
route through it. **NOT a fallback** — it absorbs exactly one sentinel this file
issues itself, and every other rejection (compile error, `onComplete` bookkeeping
failure) propagates untouched; the semantic is honest, the caller was superseded
by a LATER authoritative action, so its await must settle. (B) The unawaited
`done.catch` stops calling a supersession a failure (`console.log` "cancelled
(superseded)"; `console.error` reserved for a real break) — otherwise a show
prints a red line at every handover. (C) The two fire-and-forget callers get
their handling back: the revert attaches the SAME warning `step` used to print
(so one bad playlist can't abort step 1, "light the ship"), and `_applyAction`
routes a rejection into the runner's existing loud contract — `lastError` on the
wire + `console.error` + `_broadcast()`, identical to what
`_scheduleActionTimer` already does for a delayed action. Loud, operator-visible,
never silent, never fatal to the rig. (D) `deck_transition_path_contract.test.js`
pinned the old source text and correctly went red on the fix; it now pins the
`settleDeckTransition` shape plus two new tests — that ECANCELED **and only**
ECANCELED is absorbed, and that the baseline handler distinguishes a cancellation
from a failure.

**Verification** (`--test-concurrency=1`, isolated engines at `:17230`/`:17231`
with `--dest 192.0.2.x`; the operator's 6966-6972 + 5568 band untouched):
**special_events 109/109** (was 91/109), **timeline 445/445**,
`deck_transition_path_contract` **6/6**, effects **730/732**, mixer **600/615**;
`node --check` on both edited files and a clean `--dry-run` boot. **The 11
mixer/bump reds `_248` attributed to `_243` are STILL RED** — re-run as asked,
not touched: 10 in `tests/mixer` (8 `follow_link`, the render-health test,
`triggerMixerTransition clears the solo set`) + 1 `tests/effects/bump_flash`,
failing inside `PatternMixer` itself (`No compiled blend handle for mode
'blend_screen' on channel 'L'`; `solo cleared when a transition begins` 1 !== 0).
Other foreign reds unchanged: **5** `dev_test_bench` model-lint (the pre-existing
ambient set) and **1** `touch_control_wire_layers_contract`, which asserts on
`CaptainPad/app/(tabs)/touch.tsx` — the file `_252` is rewriting right now.

**GATE: THE ENGINE MUST RESTART.** The live `:6968` process still carries the
crash. Nothing else moves — no schema, no YAML, no wire change, no client
rebuild. **Follow-up:** `timelineLoadPlaylistOnDeck` going async changed the
failure surface of every call site and only the Timeline's own `await` was
updated to match; the two misses are fixed here, but a sweep for other
sync→async conversions in `api_server.js` with fire-and-forget callers is cheap
insurance, because the failure mode is a FATAL ENGINE EXIT rather than a visible
error. Report: `20260815_253_deck_cancel_unhandled_rejection.md`.

## _252 — CaptainPad is an iPad NATIVE app now: Skia pixel surfaces + Live Touch WebView — 2026-08-15

Implemented the full W-item contract of `docs/60_captainpad_native_first.md`
(the `_251` plan). Operator: *"make sure captainpad is a ipad native app, then
web browser!"*. Three surfaces refused to exist on the iPad — the deck **PIXELS**
window, the mixer's **nine** pixel-view bands, and the whole **Live Touch** tab.
All three work there now, and **no web pixel moved**.

**W0 preflight.** `npx expo install @shopify/react-native-skia` → **2.2.12**
exactly (the SDK 54 pin in `expo/bundledNativeModules.json:117`, the version
Expo Go ships) — the only dependency change. A **baseline** iOS bundle was
exported FIRST so any breakage would provably be mine: before
`entry-5bf889842906d8ec390e89e7bd0cf96b.hbc` **5,584,124 B**, after
`entry-3660c07c0fdae4c872f94f8768016bc9.hbc` **6,206,437 B** — the native bundle
compiles and links, and `tsc` typechecks with the NATIVE peers resolving (the
files that actually import Skia and WebView). The physical device is the
operator's; the 10-item on-device checklist is in the report §7.

**Track A — pixel surfaces.** `pixel_view_paint.ts` became a platform-neutral
pass order over a `PixelPaintTarget`: a canvas-2d adapter for the browser and a
Skia adapter that records an `SkPicture` into a **Reanimated shared value** —
zero React commits per vis frame, two pre-built `SkPaint`s (`Plus` for halos,
`SrcOver` for cores) reused for every glyph, one reused `Float32Array` for
colour. The Skia adapter imports **nothing** from `@shopify/react-native-skia`
(factories by injection, the scheduler's own idiom), which is why its entire
call sequence is unit-tested in node against a fake `SkCanvas`. The `_243`
scheduler is untouched. New `PixelSurface` platform pair owns the element plus
the shared ResizeObserver/IntersectionObserver **moved verbatim** out of the
band (the deck window now shares that one pair too), and on native `onLayout` +
`useIsFocused`. `pixel_surface_visibility` answers `document.visibilityState`
on web and `AppState` on the iPad. **Both refusal cards and the
`usePixelViewArtifact(isWeb)` gate are deleted in the same change that makes the
native path draw** — never before it.

**THE PARITY PROOF.** `pixel_view_paint_parity.test.ts` holds the
**pre-refactor painter copied verbatim** and diffs its 2D-context call stream
against the new stack — every `fillStyle` string, every arc/ellipse/rect
argument, every composite flip, the backing-store size — across **4 sizes × 5
frame states** plus the zero-size refusal. **21 comparisons, all identical.**
Stronger than any screenshot, and marked do-not-edit-to-match.

**Track B — Live Touch.** `touch_control_theme.js` grew a **transport object**
(standalone / iframe / native). Native out = `ReactNativeWebView.postMessage`,
in = an injected `window.__captainpadDeliver` **installed before
`touch-control-theme-ready` is posted** while the host marks itself ready ONLY
on that event — the injection race is dead by ordering, and a test asserts the
hook existed at the moment ready went out. In native mode the `window` 'message'
listener is **not installed at all** (no new listening surface); iframe keeps
both strict origin checks, byte-identical. `captainpad_embed=native` with no
`ReactNativeWebView` fails LOUDLY through the existing `fail()` path. All four
embed touchpoints covered: the `_223` head gate now also stamps `theme-pending`
for the native param (**no flash of standalone blue on iPad**), the spatial
requester asks the transport, and the wire's release ack rides it too — a test
proves **no page-side file posts to `window.parent` by hand any more**. Host
side: `resolveLiveTouchPanelUrl` (the `_246` leaf, extended) adds
`captainpad_embed=native` and declares **no** parent origin on native;
`live_touch_surface.web.tsx`/`.tsx` split iframe from WebView (full gesture
mitigation prop set, transparent over a themed container, teardown script);
`touch_control.tsx` keeps every platform-neutral behaviour and loses its refusal
card; a 15 s watchdog + `onError`/`onHttpError` render a loud in-view card
naming the URL with **RETRY**. Spatial fullscreen collapses the rail and zeroes
`sceneStyle.marginLeft` via a pure broker — **style only, the WebView never
moves** (RN remounts a reparented native view, which would reload the page and
drop the deadman lease). `_layout.tsx` took a deliberately 4-hunk diff.

**GATES: NO ENGINE RESTART, NO COMPANION RESTART** — client + `docs/ui` only.
What IS needed: a **CaptainPad web rebuild**, and a **Metro restart + fresh Expo
Go / dev-client load** on the iPad, because Skia is a new native module.
`app.json` deliberately untouched — the scoped
`NSAllowsArbitraryLoadsInWebContent` contingency is on-device-verified only,
never added speculatively.

**Suites.** CaptainPad **91 files / 1861 pass / 0 fail / 6 skip**, failing list
**EMPTY** (baseline on this shared tree at session start was 86/1791/0; +5 files
/ +70 tests are mine). `tsc` clean, `expo lint` **0 errors**. Simulation node
suite 2333 tests / **7 foreign failures** in scene-geometry, patch-chain, CLI
parity and scene-writer-guard files none of which read anything in this report;
`_252`'s own `touch_control_embed_transport.test.js` is **19/19**. I fixed the

**Web regression, fresh dist on :7179** (bundle hash verified against the

canvas present and DPR-sized (347×442 / 283×412 / 670×335) with the ship drawn

## _255 — COLORS interaction model: FOLLOW NOTE yields on leave, modes visible everywhere (DESIGN) — 2026-08-15

Fable, operator-ordered, design only (zero product files). Order: *"I just got
a conflict with follow note. when going from follow note to another tab for
example, it should safely disable the follow note so it's not confusing. for
the others too — plan interaction and mechanism of the color."* Contract:
**`docs/61_colors_interaction_model.md`** (60 was taken).

**Diagnosis (C1-C8):** the COLORS mode cards are LOCAL state, the daemon's
family is ENGINE state, and nothing links or names them — no follow-note
footnote/STOP off its own card (C1); the kind-agnostic gate sentence names
nobody (C2); **scheme taps on the TWO COLOUR card while following silently
PATCH `followNote.method`** — the `schemeTapOutcome` table keys on engine kind
only, so a staging tap re-themes the rig (C3, the sharpest trap); the BLEND
ramp/scrubber endpoints collapse to the daemon's own moving outputs under
follow-note (C4); nothing outside the Deck says a colour mode runs while
Mixer/CPC/MIDI colour writes get eaten ungated (C5); `_248` inferMode lets any
legacy palettes POST end follow-note unnarrated here (C6); the window always
mounts on TWO COLOUR under a remote-armed mode (C7); and part of what the
operator just hit is pre-`_248` engine skew — START 400s / PATCH 404s until
the gen-7 bounce (C8).

**Model: intent gestures yield; disappearance never does.** Leaving the
FOLLOW NOTE card by an explicit navigation tap (card switch, COLORS hide,
app-tab switch — each behind a one-line constant, D1) posts a bare
`{active:false}`: mode+tuning survive via inferMode, freeze-in-place is
native, narrated on success AND failure, navigation never blocks, and the
legacy-shape stop works on pre- and post-`_248` engines. Sleep/kill/WS-drop
never stop anything — **no engine lease/deadman for any mode** (would strobe
on WS blips and invert the `_211`/`_217` survives-sleep goal; D5). TURNS /
crossfade / palette-set PERSIST everywhere (D2) behind new visibility: a
broadcast-derived DRIVING STRIP with inline STOP on every card, kind-NAMED
gate sentences (`manualWriteGate(disabled, kind)`), card auto-select of the
running family on window entry, and an app-wide header chip `COLORS · FOLLOW
G / TURNS / XFADE / SET` (read-only, tap → Deck). Arbitration: takeover
messages name the loser; `schemeTapOutcome` gains a `surface` arg so
method-override is only reachable from the follow card; scrubber inert under
follow-note; manual gestures still refuse, never auto-stop (`_211` §D holds,
re-scoped to gestures). Scheme latch = client draft, engine-free, survives
hide, dies with the app.

**Slicing (client-only, no engine restart needed):** W1 pure logic
(`colors_window_logic.ts` only — yieldDecision/strip model/kind sentences,
table-driven tests) → parallel W2 (`colors_window.tsx` strip + L1 yield +
surface-aware taps), W3 (`index.tsx` L2/L3 triggers, loser-named messages,
zero-POST-on-reconnect), W4 (`useEngineState` + header chip, no-write grep);

race, 10-shot matrix). Must-not-change pinned: `_242` dial, `_224` transport,

decisions D1-D7 with defaults (incl. D7: the C5 engine-side palette write

## _261 — the Live Touch "HANDING BACK TO DECK" curtain that never lifted on the iPad — 2026-08-15

**Operator symptom (physical iPad, Expo Go on Metro :6981):** entering the Live
Touch tab showed an opaque, touch-swallowing **HANDING BACK TO DECK** panel over
the whole pad that never went away — Live Touch was unusable.

**Root cause, two halves that only meet on native.** (1) `touch_control.tsx`
asks for a Deck release every time the app leaves the foreground (home swipe,
auto-lock, app switcher, Control Centre) — a rule docs/47 wrote *for a browser*:
"while the iframe and WebSocket are still alive". iOS suspends the app's JS AND
the WebView's on resign and may reclaim the WebView's content process, so the
acknowledgement cannot come back until the operator returns — and the coordinator
raised its full-pad navigation curtain for that release, unconditionally, then
waited 30 s for an answer that could not arrive. Every background→foreground
round trip re-armed it, so it read as permanent. (2) The native transport LIED:
`LiveTouchSurface.send` returned `true` as soon as a WebView ref existed, but
`injectJavaScript` is fire-and-forget and a call into a page that has not
installed `window.__captainpadDeliver` (never loaded, reloaded by the panel's
RELOAD button, or reclaimed by iOS) throws inside the WebView where nobody
listens. The iframe peer answers that question truthfully for free via
`contentWindow`.

**Fix (3 files, ~30 lines).** `handoffCurtainTarget(target, reason)` in
`utils/live_touch_bridge.ts` — the curtain is a NAVIGATION blend curtain; a
`background` release runs headless (still requested, still acknowledged, still
loudly timed out). `canDeliverToNativePanel(webViewMounted, panelReady)` gates
every injected delivery on the panel hook existing RIGHT NOW: `panelReadyRef`
rises on `touch-control-theme-ready` and is cleared by every `onLoadStart` and
by RETRY, so an undeliverable release fails fast and loudly instead of hanging
the pad. The two coordinator refusals stopped saying "iframe" on an iPad.

**Proof.** New guard `components/live_touch_handoff_curtain.test.ts` (6 source
+ structure assertions): **3 of 6 FAIL on the pre-fix sources** (A/B run with the
files temporarily reverted, then restored), 6/6 pass after. CaptainPad vitest
**97 files / 2021 pass / 0 fail**, failing list EMPTY; `tsc` clean across the
tree, `eslint` clean on every file I touched. **Web parity, fresh dist on :7157**
(`entry-853153c6c46aee9099c460dd45c07acd.js`): A3 identical to `_252` — iframe
`src` carries `captainpad_origin` and no `captainpad_embed`, panel
`captainpad-embedded theme-applied`, `CaptainPadEmbed.mode === 'iframe'`,
`--bg #f8f9fa`, no native hook, zero bridge-error text; **B** drove a real
background release (`visibilitychange` → hidden) end to end: the panel posted
exactly one `touch-control-surface-released` and the curtain never appeared in
**80 samples over 4 s**; A4 standalone untouched. Zero engine writes (an idle
panel answers a background blur with `planHandoff === 'ack'`); the live
6966-6972 stack got read-only GETs only.

**No restart needed** — CaptainPad client code only, no engine/wire change. The
iPad needs a fresh Expo Go load of the new bundle. Report:
`20260815_261_live_touch_handoff_curtain.md`.

## _263 — COLORS hue dial: the native scroll-lock seam (the iPad drag that also scrolled the pane) (Opus) — 2026-08-15

Operator, physical iPad / Expo Go: dragging the `_242` COLORS hue dial **also
scrolled the surrounding pane** — unusable. **Root cause: the `_211` gesture
armor is WEB armor and native never saw it.** Capture handlers +
`onPanResponderTerminationRequest: () => false` are React responder-system
moves; a native `ScrollView` is a `UIScrollView` whose pan recognizer never
consults that system, and under the New Architecture (`newArchEnabled: true`,
RN 0.81.5, Expo 54) RN's one bridge is severed at both ends — cited from
`node_modules`: `RCTMountingManager.setIsJSResponder:blockNativeResponder:`
**drops** the flag, and `RCTScrollViewComponentView.touchesShouldCancelInContentView:`
answers from `_shouldDisableScrollInteraction`, which walks `self.superview`
**UPWARD** and so can never see a responder living **inside** it. (Old arch is
no better: `RCTUIManager` declares the flag `__unused`.) So the scroll view
cancelled the content-view touches, the pane panned, and the drag died as a
TERMINATE. `touchAction:'none'` is already gated to nothing on native — the dial
had, in practice, **no armor at all** on the iPad.

**Fix — an opt-in scroll lock**, generalising the seam `dimmer_rack.tsx`
hand-wired for its fader row. New `components/ui/scroll_lock.ts` (pure TS,
module-level store, **not** a context — the cooperating parties have no common
ancestor worth threading; `release()` is idempotent **by construction**, a
`Set.delete` of a unique symbol, so there is no guard and no counter to
corrupt) + `components/ui/lockable_scroll_view.tsx`
(`useSyncExternalStore` → `scrollEnabled={locked ? false : scrollEnabled}`).
`hue_wheel.tsx` and `HorizontalFader.tsx` take the lock in **GRANT** (touch-down
— the scroll view decides within a few points of travel, so first-move is too
late) and release it in Release, Terminate **and** unmount; the dial locks
**after** the `readOnly` refusal, so a refused touch leaves the column
scrollable. `app/(tabs)/index.tsx` (3 minimal hunks in the contended file):
both deck scroll hosts — wide `SectionHost` and narrow `ColumnsScrollRest` —
become `LockableScrollView`. Fixing the shared fader is what repairs the COLORS
**BLEND scrubber** with **zero edits to `colors_window.tsx`**, so `_211`
throttling and `_259` yield/gate logic are untouched by construction.
**Blast radius is opt-in** (a plain `ScrollView` never listens — mixer strips,
timeline, dimmer rack unaffected); **web is byte-identical** (every acquire is
`Platform.OS !== 'web'`-gated, so nothing acquires there and the prop passes
through). `_242` semantics pinned by guard: anchor-on-touch, `DIAL_GAIN`,
`dialSample`, `dialValue` latch, and **a tap still writes nothing**.

**Sibling audit.** FIXED: the dial + `HorizontalFader` (BLEND scrubber and every
fader inside the deck columns — GlobalParams, Modulation, DeckOverlayStack,
MiniFader, GroupRail). FINE, with reasons: all COLORS ring arm-taps / scheme
pills / gallery / strip STOP are `TouchableOpacity` **taps**, which RN already
arbitrates against a scroll view; `live_touch_surface` already hard-sets
`scrollEnabled={false}`; `NauticalFader` only really lands in `dimmer_rack`,
which already has its own seam; the `split_playlist_panes` divider has **no
scroll owner** (PATTERNS is pinned / has no `SectionHost`) — **but it needs the
same three-line seam if the docs/63 declutter wave ever puts PATTERNS inside a
scroller**; `pixel_view_window` has no responder at all. FLAGGED, not touched:
`components/timeline/DayView.tsx` has a bare `PanResponder` (no capture, no
termination refusal) inside its own `ScrollView` — same class, milder, timeline
owner's call.

**Proof.** New `components/ui/scroll_lock.test.ts` (9 real unit tests) +
`components/native_gesture_armor.test.ts` (30 source-text guards over the four
`.tsx` files vitest cannot render — the `colors_window_wiring.test.ts` idiom).
Honesty **proved, not asserted**: a scratch probe applied **19 targeted
mutations** (drop the grant lock, drop either release, drop the unmount cleanup,
drop the web gate, revert either deck host, revert the `scrollEnabled` ternary,
drop the subscription, break each `_242` invariant, reorder the lock ahead of
the read-only refusal) — **19/19 flipped a guard pass→fail**. Baseline before
any edit **97 files / 2021 pass / 0 fail**; after, **100 files / 2132 pass / 6
skipped / 0 fail**, failing list EMPTY. `tsc` clean on everything this wave
touched; **ONE FOREIGN RED** in the tree at final run —
`components/deck/colors_window.tsx:1156 Property 'badge' does not exist` from a
concurrent COLORS wave (tsc was clean at 17:39 with all my source edits in; it
appeared by 17:43) — **I made zero edits to that file**. `expo lint` 0 errors /
14 pre-existing warnings. No service touched: no restarts, no rebuilds, nothing
against 6966-6972 / 5568 / 6981 / 7175, no engine, no git.

**No restart needed** — CaptainPad client code only. The iPad needs a fresh
Metro reload. **Operator's 2-step device check:** (1) drag the hue dial — the
hue follows the finger for the whole gesture and the pane behind it must not
move a pixel, including on a deliberately vertical drag; (2) tap the dial — the
hue readout must be **unchanged**, and the pane must scroll normally again on a

`20260815_263_colors_dial_native_scroll_lock.md`.

## _264 — PALETTE TURNS: the selected pair keeps its distance and orbits (Opus) — 2026-08-15

**Order.** *"For the PALETTE TURNS we have 2 selected colors — keep their
distance, and rotate them in a window to the right, and then loop back when
going over the end."*

**What was wrong.** `_224` shipped two features that never met. The sliding
window built the ring as five **adjacent** pairs starting at T1; the A/B pick
(arm-then-tap, stored as ring INDICES) decided only what the TWO COLOUR card put
on the rig. An operator who picked T3+T5 and pressed START TURNS got a rotation
that ignored both their spacing and the pair currently lit.

**The design — one number.** The ring is now built FROM the operator's pair:
with `d = (selB − selA) mod n`, turn `i` is slots `selA+i` and `selA+i+d`. Both
ends step one slot right per turn, the spacing never changes, the lap closes
after `n`, and every staged colour still reaches the rig twice — blended with
the colour `d` slots along instead of always its neighbour. New
`orbitPairs(colours, sel)` + `orbitDistance(sel, n)` in `colors_window_logic.ts`;
`turnsPairs(colours)` survives as exactly `orbitPairs(colours, [0,1])`, which is
what keeps the crossfade (a two-entry ring with no selection of its own)
byte-unchanged. `rotationAutopilotPatch`/`turnsAutopilotPatch` take an OPTIONAL
trailing `sel` — absent means the adjacent ring.

**D1: the orbit STARTS on the operator's pair** (shipped, vetoable). The ring is
posted beginning at COLOUR A's slot, not T1 — not cosmetic: a restage is a full
`setState`, which resets the daemon's cursor to −1, so entry 0 is what plays
first. Starting at A is what makes START TURNS *and* a mid-rotation A/B pick land
on the pair ALREADY LIT instead of jumping, generalising a property the default
selection had by accident. Cost: a non-default pick puts a ROTATION of the staged
five on the wire, so new `orbitPhase(staged, wire)` recovers the offset and the
adoption effect adopts a live ring ONLY when it is not a rotation of the staged
one — the operator's T1..T5 numbering stays put while the rail and state line
read the wire. **D2: the default pick is a pure superset** — no pick made means
`d = 1` and today's behaviour exactly. **D3 (flagged):** the picker stays on the
TWO COLOUR card (the TURNS card has no A/B arm control to hang it from); TURNS
gained read-only A/B badges on its five slots plus a spacing caption, so the ring
that plays is legible on the card that plays it. Picking from the TURNS card is a
follow-up.

**The reader had to generalise too.** `isTurnsConfig` tested that the pairs
CHAIN (each `c2` is the NEXT entry's `c1`) — true only at `d = 1`, so a `d = 2`
ring the window itself posted would have read back as `'palette-set'` and the
card would have shown a ring the engine was not rotating. Replaced by
`turnsOrbit(palettes)`, which finds the one `d` with `pairs[i].c2 ===
pairs[(i+d)%n].c1` for every `i` and returns `{ring, distance}`; at `d = 1` that
IS the old chain test, and **smallest `d` wins** so a MASTER ring (five identical
colours, every spacing fits) still reports 1 unchanged. `rotationCursor` needed
NO change — it projects onto the posted ring's from→to segments and never assumed
adjacency (verified explicitly against all 20 selections rather than assumed).
`cursorRailSegments` returns the **single 2-cell capsule at distance 1** — the
highlight the rail has always drawn; splitting it into two pills would have put a
notch in it — and two 1-cell segments past that, with the existing
`left`/`left − n` clip trick carrying the T5→T1 seam crossing unchanged.

**Engine: unchanged and unaware, verified first.** `color_autopilot.js` validates
`palettes` entry by entry, cycles them sequentially (`(cursor+1) % length`) and
tweens between consecutive resolved param sets; nothing in the daemon ever asks
whether two pairs share a colour. The orbit is a client-side construction of the
SAME wire. **No engine file edited; no engine restart needed.**

**Back-compat proof — byte-identical, three ways.** (1) `orbitPairs(ring,[0,1])`
deep-equals `turnsPairs(ring)` for all nine generators; (2)
`JSON.stringify(turnsAutopilotPatch(ring,5,1.5,[0,1]))` equals the unselected
patch for all nine, and `crossfadeAutopilotPatch` stringifies identically to the
`rotationAutopilotPatch` it delegates to; (3) through a REAL engine the default
patch comes back from `GET /deck/color-autopilot` byte-identical to the pre-orbit
wire (343 bytes). Strongest signal is the negative one: **all 263 pre-existing
`colors_window_logic` tests and all 28 wiring tests passed unmodified** before a
single new test was written — nothing in the old contract had to be relaxed.

**Offline walk 100 %** (`~/tmp/orbit_260/engine_verification.txt`) — real
`engine.js` on **:17262**, sACN black-holed on TEST-NET-1 `192.0.2.x`, throwaway
config/state/playlist/timeline dirs, all three walls ASSERTED before any
scenario; readout computed by the **REAL client `rotationCursor` +
`orbitWindowSlots`**, esbuild-bundled from the TypeScript the UI imports. With
A=T3, B=T5: engine accepted the `d=2` ring, read back distance 2 / phase 2, turn
1 was exactly the operator's pick, and the observed sequence was **`T3+T5 →
T4+T1 → T5+T2 → T1+T3 → T2+T4 → T3+T5`** — all 6 windows exactly 2 slots apart,
one slot right on each of 5 transitions, the T5→T1 wrap observed 1×, 2 windows
straddling the seam, 56 settled + 18 mid-fade samples resolved, and the first
five turns putting every staged colour on COLOUR A. `d = 1..4` all accepted and
round-tripped verbatim at constant spacing.

**Gates.** 22 new logic tests (263 → 285) covering all 20 legal selections × all
4 distances, wrap coverage, the smallest-`d` rule, `orbitPhase` round-trip,
cursor inversion on non-adjacent windows at three fade positions each, and rail
segments including the seam. Full CaptainPad suite **101 files / 2174 pass / 6
skipped / 0 fail**, failing list EMPTY, **no foreign reds**. `tsc` clean; eslint
clean on all three touched files. The transient `colors_window.tsx:1156 Property
'badge' does not exist` that `_263` reported as FOREIGN was **mine**, caught
mid-edit between a call site and its declaration — resolved.

**Hygiene.** 6966-6972 / 5568 / 6981 / 7175 never bound, restarted or swept; no
export, no dist write, no Metro touch, no git. Walk engine stopped; it ran
entirely inside a throwaway temp world, so nothing was written to
`marsin_engine/states/**` or `simulation/scenes/**`. Hunks are confined to the
TURNS transport and slot-row region — disjoint from the concurrent `hue_wheel` /
responder and mixer-relayout waves.

**No restart needed** — CaptainPad client code only; the iPad needs a fresh Metro
reload. **Operator's 4-step check:** (1) TWO COLOUR, latch a scheme, arm A→tap
T3, arm B→tap T5 (badges read `A=T3 · B=T5`); (2) switch to PALETTE TURNS — the
slots carry `T3 · A` / `T5 · B` and the caption says *2 slot(s) apart*; (3) START
TURNS — begins on T3+T5 with **no jump**, then T4+T1, T5+T2, T1+T3, T2+T4, back
to T3+T5, with the rail showing **two separated cells travelling together**; (4)
with no pick made, everything behaves exactly as before. Report:
`20260815_264_palette_turns_orbit.md`.

## _265 — 2D Pixels: the dark ghost ship, and the Lighting Controls menu that rendered blank (Opus) — 2026-08-15

**Order.** Two operator-reported defects on the iPad's 2D Simulator tab (PROD
stack, `?profile=2d_pixels&lighting_mode=sacn_in`): the Lighting Controls menu
renders EMPTY, and a dark "ghost ship" sits slightly larger than and behind the
live 2D pixel map. Find the real mechanisms — verify, don't assume.

**Neither was what it looked like.** Both were reproduced first, in a full
scratch sim (7869–7872, UDP **15568**, never 5568) whose only trick is a static
server that answers `/simulation/config.yaml` from the scratch file — the page
derives the save-server and both sACN bridge ports from that document, so
without it a probe browser would have joined the operator's live input-bridge
client census. Live 6966-6972 / 5568 / 6981 / 7175 never bound or restarted;
the scratch save-server logged **zero writes**.

**Ghost — root cause: an edge-triggered latch versus an unconditional writer.**
`animate.js` hides the 3D canvas on the headless EDGE only
(`if (_headless !== _headlessLatched)`) — it fires once. `split_layout.js` runs
`applyLayout()` on **every** window resize, and its not-engaged branch called
`placeCanvas(null, true)` → an unconditional `canvas.style.display = ''`. So any
resize (an iPad WebView rotation, a layout settle, the keyboard) re-showed the
full-window 3D canvas in `2d_pixels`, and the already-latched hide never took it
back. What shows is the last frame `composer.render()` drew before headless was
entered — the unlit hull. `setSize` never repaints it and a same-size resize does
not even reallocate the buffer, so it survives indefinitely. Measured:
`entering 2d_pixels → inline:'none'` then `same-size resize → inline:''`, and the
map-hidden capture is three dark grey hull sections.

**Fix: one authority — the layout ASKS, the profile VETOES.** New
`src/core/canvas_visibility.js` (pure, DOM-free): `canvasDisplayFor(profileId,
layoutWantsVisible)` returns `'none'` for any `headless` profile whatever the
layout wants, still obeys the layout for 3D profiles (mapMax still hides;
leaving `2d_pixels` still restores), and throws on a non-boolean request.
`applyCanvasVisibility` additionally calls `renderer.clear()` whenever it hides,
so no stale frame is left for any future caller to reveal — belt and braces.
Both `animate.js` and `split_layout.js` now go through it; headlessness is read
from the registry, so a second headless profile inherits the rule for free.
After: canvas `'none'` through same-size resize, real resize, and the
controller-map split — and `06_back_to_3d` shows the 3D view rendering live
inside the split. **Not a one-way door.**

**Empty menu — root cause: an unreachable auto-collapse, not profile design.**
The panel is NOT empty by design in `2d_pixels` (it carries Atmosphere, Model
Transform, Layout Tools, DMX Fixtures, LED Fixtures, Options and renders them all
at 1180×820). `gui_builder.js` ended with `if (window.innerWidth <= 768)
gui.close()` — closing the lil-gui ROOT, whose `.title` this panel HIDES (our own
header replaces it). A closed root therefore had **no affordance left to reopen
it**. Measured at 760×1000: a 330×848 panel titled "🔦 LIGHTING CONTROLS" with
**1103 `.controller` rows in the DOM and 0 of them rendered**, `bodyText: ""`.
The small-screen protection it duplicated already lives one layer up —
`control_drawer.js` defaults to collapsed below 800 px and leaves a reopen tab.
The root close was redundant and broke the drawer it was copying. Removed:
`visibleControllers` 0 → 24.

**And named anyway.** New `src/gui/profile_capability_notice.js`: a panel that
goes contentless must never be mute. `profileNoticeMode(profileId, controlCount)`
→ `none` (3D profile — not this module's business) / `banner` (headless with real
controls) / `sole` (headless with ZERO rendered controls: the notice IS the
panel). Counting is by **rendered** rows (rect height > 0) because presence is not
content — that is exactly the 1103-vs-0 case. Wired at the end of `setupGUI` and
in the `lightingProfile` handler, so it appears AND disappears at runtime in both
directions. Copy names the label and the id, says what the profile does not
render, states plainly that patching/mapping/sACN are unaffected, and points at
Options → 💡 Lighting Profile. `sole` says *"empty on purpose — it is not
broken"*; `banner` is tested never to claim an unpopulated panel. No control
invented, `profile_registry.js` untouched. Styling reuses the existing
`--warning*` theme tokens (theme_parity stays green).

**Gates.** Sim suite **2409 tests / 2399 pass / 9 fail / 1 todo**; the two new
files **24/24 green**. All 9 reds pre-existing and FOREIGN — none of their files
imports anything touched here (`scene_data_lint` + `bench_mirror_state`: the
`scenes/summer_camp_dome/patches.yaml.original` residue the test itself says the
operator must clear, report `20260805_163`; `bench_section_sync` ×5: foreign
working-tree scene edits/deleted playlists from other in-flight waves;
`launcher_supervision` ×2: real children / shared Metro env while the live stack
owns 6969-6972; `touch_control_pixel_views` ×1: orientation projection).
Before/after screenshots inspected in `~/tmp/ghost_sim/{before,after}/`.

**No git. No restart done here** — the sim serves these files statically, so the
fix reaches the live surface at the coordinator's end-of-batch sim restart (or a
hard reload; `http-server` runs `-c-1`). No engine restart needed.
**Operator's check:** rotate/resize the iPad on the 2D Simulator tab — no dark
ship behind the pixel map, ever; then open the Lighting Controls drawer — it
names the profile at the top and lists its sections, and switching Lighting
Profile to `full` removes the notice as the 3D view returns. Report:
`20260815_265_2d_pixels_ghost_and_empty_menu.md`.

## _266 — The supervised Expo Go Metro, the stale-Metro guard, and `rebuild-pad`: docs/62 W-B + W-C (Opus) — 2026-08-15

**Built ON `_260`'s W-A** (shell-free spawns, real-pid lock, `stackPorts`,
`reapStaleStack`, ARM-interlocked kills, the sentinel) — reused, not re-derived.
Every remaining docs/62 decision taken on the recommended default: **D3** flag
not a fourth profile · **D4** `:7175` retired · **D5** in-place export · **D6**
warn, never refuse, on a stale dist.

**W-B1 — the Expo Go Metro is a launcher child now.** A show profile serves the
web pad from the prebuilt dist, which Expo Go cannot load, so the native half
used to be a hand-run background `expo start`: a straggler by construction,
outside every teardown path and every guard. `node launcher.js prod
--with-native-pad` adds child `captainpad-native` on the new
`captainpad_native_port: 6981` — in `stackPorts`, in the lock
(`withNativePad`), a row in `status`, resolved-pid recorded (it is the
shell-shim class), reaped by W-A3/A5, torn down with everything else, and the
startup summary prints the `exp://<lanHost>:6981` line. **Refused by name on an
expo profile** (exit **2**, raised inside `validate()` — i.e. before
`assertSingleInstance`, so a bad flag can never take the show down first),
because two Metros race `node_modules/.cache`. Both Metros now share ONE env
contract, `metroChildEnv(lanHost)`: `CI` genuinely DELETED, `BROWSER=none`,
bundle host a plain STRING.

**W-B2 — the stale-Metro class is self-announcing and self-healing.** Before any
Metro start the launcher fingerprints `package-lock.json` + npm's installed-tree
marker and compares it with the last Metro start that reached readiness:
changed → `expo start --clear` with a loud line; unchanged → normal start
(`--clear` every boot costs playa minutes for nothing); **package-lock newer
than the installed tree → the boot REFUSES**, naming `npm install`. That last
state is tonight's phantom `Unable to resolve` for files that exist
(TypefaceFontProvider) — no cache policy can fix a manifest nobody installed.
The stamp is written only AFTER readiness, so a Metro that never came up cannot
certify its own cache.

**W-C1 — `node launcher.js rebuild-pad` is the ONE dist-refresh path.** Expo's
own `web:build` command with `CI` deleted, in place, streamed as `[rebuild]`;
success proven STRUCTURALLY (exit 0 **and** `dist/index.html` rewritten this run
**and** an entry bundle, whose name it prints so the hash can be checked on the
iPad). No restart: the static server reads from disk and sends HTML `no-store`,
so an iPad reload picks it up mid-show. It is **serialized** — refusing by name
over another `rebuild-pad`, over any `expo export` running elsewhere on the box,
and over a launcher Metro still warming — because parallel exports corrupt the
metro cache and emit a blank-page bundle that reads as a product crash (`_259`).

**W-C2/W-C3 —** a prod boot now WARNS (never refuses, D6) when `dist/` is older
than `CaptainPad/{app,components,hooks,utils}`, naming `rebuild-pad`; and the
per-profile **cadence table** landed in `.agent/ops/stack_lifecycle.md` +
README: engine/sim/companion ⇒ bounce (arm-marker check first, both profiles);
**prod CaptainPad-web ⇒ `rebuild-pad` + iPad reload, NO bounce**; native deps ⇒
the fingerprint guard self-heals on next launch.

**Proof.** `launcher_supervision` **76/76 PASS** on the final run (+26 new; all 50 W-A
still green). Three mutation checks, each reverted and the file verified
byte-identical afterwards: drop the installed-tree term from the fingerprint →
RED; let the native-pad flag onto any profile → 2 RED (unit + the real-CLI
exit-2); remove the rebuild lock → the SERIALIZATION test RED with two
concurrent exports, i.e. the mutation reproduces `_259`'s corruption exactly.
Serialization also proven with real concurrency (exactly one export ran) and a
real CLI run that refused with **no dist created**. Native-pad env contract
proven by a REAL spawn with `CI=true` in the parent: `'CI' in process.env` is
false and the bundle host is a plain string. CaptainPad `api_base_resolution`
29/29. A mid-session red was FOREIGN and has cleared — another session's `ghost_sim`
scratch processes squatted this suite's 78xx map (started 17:26, left alone);
the same `start.js` on a free map logged the pid the assertion wants, proving a
collision rather than a regression. **That 78xx map is not exclusive — check the
ports before believing an L1 red.**

**Live stack untouched:** 6966-6972 / 5568 / :6981 / :7175 all still LISTENING
on the same pids before and after, the live lock unchanged, and the **ARMED**
bench mirror never approached. No `expo export` ever touched the real
`CaptainPad/dist` (tests use a `BM26_REBUILD_PAD_DIR` scratch seam). `:7175`'s
repo scaffolding is retired in the docs; the RUNNING :7175 process is the
coordinator's to stop at batch end.

**GATE: LAUNCHER RESTART REQUIRED to activate** — the coordinator's
end-of-batch bounce. Report:
`20260815_266_native_pad_and_pad_upkeep_wbwc.md`.

Order 1 is a `_217`-style DERIVED suppression (zero writes, static caption, a
manual OUTPUT hide survives PIXELS cycles). `CPCControls` gained deck-only

## _274 — Deck minimize/maximize FIXED: the narrow stack arbitrates, a restored window can no longer take over the pattern list (Opus) — 2026-08-16

Operator order: "when all is hidden and one is turned back on, it takes over the
patterns' list — that's a corner case not handled properly. Screenshot a
reproduced error, then fix, and screenshot again." **He RULED it a DEFECT**,
which supersedes `_267`'s open **decision 14** (portrait reopen recorded as
shipped content-sizing, declined citing pins). Client-only: zero engine files,
zero engine traffic, zero persisted-state change — no reducer action added,
`deck_workspace_layout_v1` untouched in schema and content.

**MECHANISM, named before code.** The narrow columns host has exactly two
children — the PATTERNS track and the ONE `ColumnsScrollRest` region — sized by
**two independent rules that never looked at each other or at the host**:
PATTERNS took a rigid, NON-SHRINKABLE `max(400|500, 38.5 % of the DEVICE
WINDOW)` pin (`flexBasis` + `height`, `flexShrink:0`); the region took `flex:1`
and its windows are content-sized (their `SectionHost` is a plain View in
narrow, because `narrowScrollOwner` forbids a nested same-axis ScrollView). Two
failures fall out, BOTH reproduced and measured on a scratch dist. **(1) the
operator's report:** 834×1194 PATTERNS **835 → 460 px, 12 visible playlist rows
→ 4** the instant a second window appears, while the newcomer claims **1010 px
in a 383 px viewport** (COLORS) or stretches to 100 % of it (PIXELS) — one chip
tap costs two thirds of the list; 1024×1366 is 1007 → 526, 15 rows → 6. **(2) a
strictly worse variant found while probing the corner:** when the pin EXCEEDS
the host (880×620, host **309**, pin **400**) the non-shrinkable PATTERNS
**overflows the host by 95 px** — spilling under the bottom PANIC bar with the
list clipped mid-row — and the region is starved to **ZERO**, so **the window
the operator just restored never appears at all**. Screenshot proof of both.

**HONESTY on the "renders OVERLAPPING/ON TOP" in the operator's shot: a literal
box intersection could NOT be reproduced on the web dist.** `getBoundingClientRect`
was captured for PATTERNS and every shown window across 36 states plus a 12-state
tight sweep; the overlap verdict fired zero times. What the screenshots DO show
is the two failures above, which read exactly as described — a squeezed (or
off-screen) PATTERNS with the PIXELS chips + ship + honesty caption owning
everything else. Failure 2 is also the overflow class that CAN paint over a
sibling on native, where the columns host does not clip.

## _279 — Mixer: hiding LOCAL PARAMS finally gives the room to the pattern list (Opus) — 2026-08-16

Operator ask: *"in the mixer view, when hiding params, make room for the pattern
list so we show more patterns in the view please — that was the whole purpose of
hiding the params :)"* — **correct, and the defect was total**: hiding params
freed **nothing**, in either orientation. Measured on a scratch export at iPad
1194×834 / 834×1194, the playlist viewport was **byte-identical** shown vs
hidden (portrait 292×158 = 2 rows either way; landscape 176×24 = 1 partial row
either way) and the params panel did not shrink one pixel — it kept its full
share while rendering only the 28 pt stub. Dead ground: a ~100 pt empty band
under the stub in portrait, a 135×102 pt empty column beside the list in
landscape.

**Cause:** the body's two children were never told to stop claiming. Portrait
(COLUMN) — the params panel carries `flexGrow: 1`, and a flex WEIGHT is claimed
whether or not anything fills it. Landscape (ROW) — `width: '40%'`, likewise
unconditional. **PIXELS never had this defect and is the control**: its band is
a full-width block in the card's VERTICAL stack, so collapsing it returns the
height to `channelBody` (`flex: 1`) for free — measured landscape 24 → 167 pt
(0 → 2 rows), portrait 158 → 253 pt (2 → 4 rows), with no layout code of its
own. Params is a SIBLING PANEL, not a block above, so it could not inherit it.

**Fix** — new pure rule in `mixer_scroll_layout.ts` (`mixerParamsColumnMode` →
`full` / `stub` / `empty`, mirroring `ChannelStrip`'s render branches including
perf's asymmetry) plus four panel constants: portrait drops the flex weight
(`flexShrink: 0` keeps the stub tappable), landscape clears the 40 %, an
`empty` perf column costs `width: 0` + `padding: 0`, and the playlist becomes
the row's only grower. Applied LAST in `mixer.tsx`'s two style arrays so it
beats the base 60/40 and perf's 45/55. **View-only — zero engine calls, no new
scroll-acquire sites, floor-of-one untouched.**

**Before → after:** portrait 292×158 → **292×242/244, rows 2 → 3/4** (same at 2
and 3 visible channels); portrait with the master band open 62 → 98 pt;
landscape 176 → 196 pt wide at 3 channels and **283 → 374 pt at 2** (long
pattern names stop truncating). **Params SHOWN is geometrically identical
before and after** in every scenario measured, and pixels-hidden is untouched.

**Landscape gains WIDTH, not rows, and that is geometric** — the params column
is BESIDE the list there, and no flex rule turns width into rows. The row lever
in landscape is PIXELS (0 → 2, already working). Also measured and worth Sina
knowing: **with the pixel band open in landscape the list is only ~24 pt tall —
one partial row**, params or no params. Considered and NOT taken: relocating the
band into the vacated column (what perf mode already does), which would buy
~180 pt of height and ~5 rows but shrink the band from ~330×122 to ~135×50 at 3
channels. **Operator call — it is a ~10-line follow-up if he wants it.**

**Trap banked:** the first implementation cleared the 40 % with
`width: undefined` and changed nothing — on **react-native-web a later
`undefined` does not override an earlier value** (the resolver drops undefined
instead of overwriting). `'auto'` does, and a test now pins it.
`cardStyle` in `mixer.tsx` (~3355) still carries the same latent
`width: undefined`, masked there by `flex` + `maxWidth`.

**Pre-existing bug found, NOT caused here** (identical on the before build,
filed as a task): **landscape + MASTER VIEW open crushes the card body to
zero** — playlist 283×**0**, params 206×16, both painting under the MUTE/SOLO
and TRANSITION rows, chevron untappable. It is the LANDSCAPE twin of the
portrait W0 fix: landscape's panels are percentage widths with no `flexShrink`,
so they never join the shrink negotiation.

**Gates:** CaptainPad vitest **2291 pass / 0 fail / 6 skipped** —
`mixer_scroll_layout.test.ts` 5 → 14, so **+9 is mine**; a concurrent thread
edited `components/special_events/*.test.ts` mid-session and owns the rest of
the drift off the 2281 baseline. Zero failures at every point. `tsc` clean; `expo lint` **0 errors** (the 14 warnings
are all in untouched files); the three touched files scan clean. Live stack
never bound/killed/restarted, `CaptainPad/dist` never written, scratch servers
:7191/:7192/:7193 all stopped; 4+ channels covered structurally (the rule never
reads the channel count, and portrait ≥3 — the fixed-320 branch 4+ uses — was
measured).

**CaptainPad rebuild REQUIRED**; no engine restart. Report:
`20260816_279_mixer_params_room_for_patterns.md`.

## _283 — CONFIG leaves the performance UI; the offline exit becomes the escape hatch; playlist switching opens on deck + mixer (Opus implement+validate) — 2026-08-16

Two operator asks, one wave. (1) "please hide the config from the performance
UI — just make sure the EXIT PERFORMANCE MODE is possible using the UI even if
the engine is not connected, so I can go into edit and go to config to select a
new server or sth". (2) "in the performance mode, allow playlist changing in
the deck and mixer too."

**REVERSES `_250`.** `config` + `studio`/`midi`/`osc` go `showInPerformance:
false`. `_250` had put them on the performance rail as an OFFLINE ESCAPE HATCH
(boot-locked engine + hidden CONFIG = stranded pad); the operator moved that
hatch to the EXIT itself, which is the right door — CONFIG is a setup surface,
not a performance surface. Perf rail is now DECK · MIXER · LIVE TOUCH · EVENTS.

**What the exit depended on, and what was severed.** The offline exit MECHANISM
already existed and needed no change: online, `doExit` POSTs and is totally
engine-bound (correct, untouched); offline, the chip routes to `_250`'s
`setLocalPerformanceView()` — no request, no passcode, sheets force-hidden. The
break was in what the pad did with the answer: BOTH the rail and
`performance_route_guard` computed `!ready || active`, and offline `ready` NEVER
arrives on its own (it resolves only once a local view is taken). So a pad that
boots against a dead engine sat at `active:false, ready:false` = LOCKED: rail
frozen with no CONFIG, chip reading idle "PERF" so the first tap went the WRONG
WAY (into the lock) and only a second reached edit — and the guard's
`if (!ready) return null` made even a `/config` deep link a PERMANENTLY BLANK
screen (a latent `_250` gap in its own right). Severed with ONE shared rule,
`performanceNavigationLocked()` in `captainpad_tab_policy.ts`, used by both
consumers: `if (engineOffline) return active; return !ready || active;` — online
byte-identical and still fail-closed — plus the guard's hold is exempt offline.
Now: engine dies mid-show → chip reads EDIT → ONE tap → CONFIG back; pad boots
against a dead address → ZERO taps, CONFIG simply there and its deep link
mounts. NOT a forbidden fallback: the operator specified it, nothing is masked
(standing `ENGINE OFFLINE` + `LOCAL VIEW` captions and a red offline banner
throughout), and no gate is loosened — presentation only, every real gate is
engine-side per request, and the override is discarded on reconnect.

**Playlist switching.** The client was NOT the only gate — the engine 409'd the
switch too, so a client-only unlock would have produced a refusal, not a
feature. Exactly TWO routes left the 409 table: `POST /deck/playlist` and
`POST /mixer/channels/:id/playlist`. Safe by construction: `saveAllState()` is
ALREADY a no-op while live (`effectiveAutoSave()` reads
`!performanceMode.active`) so a mid-show switch writes ZERO bytes (byte-compared
in test), it is not structural (nothing created/destroyed/reordered — same class
as the always-open `/deck/playlist/entry`), and `captureLook()` carries the
binding so RESTORE returns the pre-show playlist. STILL GATED: playlist
create/delete, `/deck/playlist/secondary` (split-pane BINDING is structural),
both `/playlist/capture` routes, overlay playlist, modulation/midi-mapping PUTs,
and the whole pre-existing matrix. Client: new pure
`components/playlist_access_logic.ts` splits `editable` into `selectable`
(`!locked`) vs `editable` (`!locked && !perfLocked && !persistLocked`);
`PlaylistPanel` is the ONE playlist surface (deck primary + pane 2 + overlays +
every mixer channel) so pinning the policy pins both paths. `persistLocked` is
deliberately OUT of `selectable` — it asks "will this be written to disk", the
wrong question for a non-persistent action, and leaving it in would have
silently re-blocked the ask on every real show engine (the engine pins
`editPrincipal` to null during a show, so it is true whenever `authRequired`
is): the feature would have worked on the bench and failed on the playa. The
library modal gains `crudEnabled` and, when false, hides duplicate/delete/NEW
and says `SWITCH ONLY — PLAYLIST EDITING RESUMES IN EDIT MODE.`

unshrinkable chrome stays **411** — of which the per-channel **PIXELS band is
208, half the card**. Body entitled to exactly 0. Correct arithmetic on an
impossible budget.

28 pt LOCAL PARAMS stub away entirely ⇒ section **unreachable** (docs/64 §3.1);
any body floor ejects MUTE/SOLO **and** TRANSITION from the card. Only "the
PIXELS band yields height" keeps every control (body 160, **1 row**). The
one-line escape inside the owned files was tested and **fails**: narrowing the
band's slot shrinks the picture aspect-honestly (327×174 → 142×75, never
clipped) but its OUTER height stays pinned at 208 — cap-driven, not
canvas-driven, surplus reserved as centred card ground.

**Decision needed (§6 of the report):** may `CHANNEL_EDIT_CAP_HEIGHT` be
lowered when a landscape card cannot afford it? Declined to pre-empt it —
`_279` §5 escalated exactly this to Sina, and `pixel_view_band_logic.ts`'s own
header records `_243` resolving the same budget by MOVING the band rather than
shrinking it. It also needs the band's stage restructured into a shrinkable
flex child in a component shared with the deck and the perf-mode wave.

`28+72=100`), landscape row height is **60 pt**, so even the maximum legal
reallocation buys **ONE row** — the landscape card needs to shed a block, not
trim one. Mechanism if taken: band slot `flexShrink:1` + `flexBasis:28+176` +
`minHeight:28+72`, body `minHeight` floor, and the channel/edit cap follows the
**measured slot height** exactly as the perf dominant-fill path already does.

## _286 — Mixer: the portrait rail fixed for REAL (Yoga EXECUTED in vitest) + the scroll lock lands in the same frame as the grant — docs/69 W1+W2, PARTIAL — 2026-08-16

Two of the operator's three orders off the rebuilt pad, implemented and
gate-green. **W3 (patterns-first landscape card) still pending — lands as
`_287` in the same session.**

**W1 — portrait rail (order 2).** `_275`'s override was **inert**: it composed
`{flexGrow:0,flexShrink:0,flexBasis:'auto'}` over `masterBarFill`'s `flex:1`,
and flattening never drops the shorthand, so Yoga saw both — an explicit
`'auto'` basis falls through `processFlexBasis` while the co-flattened positive
`flex` forces basis 0 (native never uses web defaults) and the explicit
`flexGrow:0` wins ⇒ grow 0 · shrink 0 · basis 0 = **0 pt**, the same zero as
`_273`. CSS resolves it the other way, which is why web passed twice while the
iPad failed twice; the `_275` guard pinned `flexBasis:'auto'` by name, i.e.
**the guard enforced the bug**. Fix = style **SELECTION**:
`MASTER_BAR_SEAT_LANDSCAPE {flex:1,minWidth:0}` (byte-equal to before) and
`MASTER_BAR_SEAT_PORTRAIT {minWidth:0}` — **no flex-family key exists in the
portrait object**, so the trap is structurally unreachable — exported pure from
`mixer_workspace_bar_logic.ts`, selected by `isPortrait ? … : …` in
`mixer.tsx`; the two old styles deleted. **Rule banked: never override a
`flex:N` base with longhands on native — select, don't fight.**

**The net that was missing:** devDep `yoga-layout@3.2.1` (WASM build of the
same C++ Yoga RN vendors; dev-only, app bundle unchanged) + a **Yoga-EXECUTED**
vitest over the real exports. Measured: pre-`_275` `{flex:1}` → **0**, shipped
`_275` composition → **0**, shipped portrait seat → **36**, landscape seat →
**250** of a 400 pt row. Mutation-verified RED on both historical compositions.
Guard flipped to assert flex-key ABSENCE structurally over `Object.keys` of the
real object + the mixer.tsx consumption pin.

**W2 — drag-start glitch (order 1).** Acquire timing was already touch-down;
the hole is propagation (notify → `useSyncExternalStore` → render → Fabric
commit ≈ 1-2 frames vs UIScrollView's ~10 pt slop). `LockableScrollView` gains
a **synchronous native fast path**: composed internal ref + a
`subscribeScrollLock` effect whose listener, gated `Platform.OS !== 'web'`,
calls `getNativeScrollRef()?.setNativeProps({scrollEnabled})`; effect returns
its unsubscribe. Render path **byte-identical** (`locked ? false :
scrollEnabled`, the `_263` pin) and remains the truth; unlock restores
`callerProp ?? true` through pure vitest-pinned
`resolveFastPathScrollEnabled`. **Zero acquire-site changes.** Verified against
RN 0.81.5 rather than trusted — `getNativeScrollRef` real, Fabric
`setNativeProps` real, and **`scrollEnabled` IS in `validAttributes` for both
ScrollView configs** (had it not been, the payload would drop it and the fast
path would be silently inert — the `_275` failure mode one layer down).
Frame numbers are mechanism-derived, not device-measured; the device check is
the closing evidence.

scroll"). **Read the CAVEAT before trusting the row numbers.**

**Shipped:** in LANDSCAPE EDIT the per-channel 2D PIXELS band leaves the card's
vertical stack and mounts at the TOP of the media column above LOCAL PARAMS —
perf's proven grammar (`_243`/`_270`) extended to edit, so the mixer now has ONE
landscape body shape. Portrait keeps its band (no side-by-side column there);

`mixerMediaColumnMode` delegates byte-for-byte to `_279`'s
`mixerParamsColumnMode` whenever `perfActive || isPortrait` and adds ONE
branch: landscape edit = `'full'` if `paramsShown || pixelsShown`, else
`'stub'` (never `'empty'`, asserted). `mixerLandscapeMediaBandSlot` bounds the
band (shrink + floor of header+`MIN_BAND_CANVAS_HEIGHT` + `overflow:hidden`).

**THE CRUSH IS FIXED, and that is a re-ruling.** `_285` landed NO code and
handed the fix back to W3 while disproving D7's premise (landscape's
`channelBody` is a ROW sized by `align-items:stretch`; the real defect is an
over-subscribed card whose PIXELS band is 208 pt = half of it). Shedding that
block IS the remedy. Measured 1194×834, 2 ch, MASTER VIEW open: `channelBody`
515×**0 → 515×180**; playlist scroller 283×**0 → 283×102-104**; MUTE/SOLO now
9 pt clear of the body bottom, TRANSITION 24 pt inside the card, nothing paints
outside the scroller. **`CHANNEL_EDIT_CAP_HEIGHT` NOT lowered** — sidestepped
by MOVING the band (as `_243` did); still Sina's call.

**Rows:** 1366×1024, 3 ch, default: 246 pt/**4 rows → 428-430 pt/7 rows**
(target ≥7 ✔). 1194×834: 56 pt/**0 rows → 238-240 pt/3 rows** — missed ≥4 by
3-5 pt, so **R1 was taken** (docs/69 D5's own default, coordinator-approved):
`minHeight:44` compact rows (docs/66 floor EXACTLY) via a NEW `compactRows`
prop threaded ONLY from mixer.tsx — deliberately separate from `compact`
(which `DeckOverlayStack` also sets), so the deck's rows are untouched, pinned
by a scope test. **R1 is one line to reverse.**

**Two defects found and fixed inside the wave.** (1) Both-hidden INVERTED —
column widened to 247.64 pt, playlist shrank to 89.7 pt — because the collapsed
column's `_279` `flexShrink:0` hugged `PixelViewBand`'s header at full
intrinsic width (it kept rendering `TOP-DOWN ▾` + `100/964` while collapsed).
Fix: `compactWhenCollapsed` hides that optional chrome (**chevron never
gated** — it is the only way back), landscape-edit mount ONLY; collapsed column
→ `flexShrink:1` + `minWidth:44` + `overflow:hidden`. (2) Band canvas 70 pt vs
its own 72 floor: react-native-web `View` is `boxSizing:border-box` and Yoga
matches, so the picture box carrying `borderWidth:1` delivered `(w-2)×(h-2)` —
a floored 72 rendered 70. Fix compensates the border on the picture box;
`bandCanvasSizeForAspect`/`MIN_BAND_CANVAS_HEIGHT`/paint engine untouched. This
one is UNIVERSAL, so master/perf bands need a regression look.

only STRUCTURALLY — root `{flex:1}`, no page ScrollView, channel row

browser compositing, second never started); §2/§3 numbers are DOM rects.

change.** The count-heuristic hypothesis is DISPROVEN — `scrollEnabled` tracked
real overflow at every boundary (landscape 3 ch 1082 vs 1082 no overflow; +
COLORS 1420 vs 1082; 4 ch 1756 vs 1082; portrait 2 ch 722 vs 722; 3 ch 1024 vs
